It is the \u003cem\u003eopposite\u003c/em\u003e end of the spectrum from Quartz's SPA.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003enav\u003c/code\u003e is a single global YAML list; OKF is graph-shaped, not a strict tree, so a single linear nav is the wrong mental model.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eserver-rendered static HTML as one of the build targets\u003c/strong\u003e (portability, no JS); \u003cstrong\u003esection-aware search with built-in + optional-hosted split\u003c/strong\u003e; \u003cstrong\u003ePython hook-style plugin lifecycle\u003c/strong\u003e; rendering \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e as a \u003cstrong\u003etimeline\u003c/strong\u003e; snippet-include as an optional transformer.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"4-notion-reference-for-structuredrelational-data\"\u003e4. Notion  \u003cem\u003e(reference for structured/relational data)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(a) What it is.\u003c/strong\u003e A hosted block-based workspace. Its \"databases\" are tables whose rows are pages, with typed properties, \u003cstrong\u003erelations\u003c/strong\u003e between databases, and \u003cstrong\u003erollups\u003c/strong\u003e (aggregates over related rows).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(b) Mechanisms worth stealing.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTyped properties + relations + rollups\u003c/strong\u003e as a model for \u003cem\u003eoptional\u003c/em\u003e structure. OKF's frontmatter is untyped free-form; an \u003cstrong\u003eoptional typed-relation extension\u003c/strong\u003e (see §11 and Synthesis) could let a concept declare \u003ccode\u003edepends_on: [/tables/customers.md]\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eowner: @alice\u003c/code\u003e, with the viewer rendering a relations panel and computing simple rollups (count of backlinks, latest \u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e among children).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFiltered views\u003c/strong\u003e (table/board/calendar/gallery) over the same data. OKF's viewer could offer filterable listings over frontmatter (e.g. \"all \u003ccode\u003etype: BigQuery Table\u003c/code\u003e tagged \u003ccode\u003esales\u003c/code\u003e, sorted by \u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e\").\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBlock model\u003c/strong\u003e (everything is a typed block; pages compose blocks). Too heavy for OKF, but the \u003cem\u003eidea\u003c/em\u003e that a concept's body has addressable sections (\u003ccode\u003e# Schema\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e# Examples\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e# Citations\u003c/code\u003e) that can be embedded/queried is worth keeping.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(c) What does NOT translate.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eNotion is \u003cstrong\u003eproprietary, hosted, block-graph-in-a-database\u003c/strong\u003e, not plain files. It is not portable, not diffable, not git-friendly — the opposite of OKF's core values.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRollups require a typed schema and a database; OKF deliberately avoids a schema registry (SPEC §1 non-goals). Keep relations \u003cem\u003eoptional and unvalidated beyond link-target-existence\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e an \u003cstrong\u003eoptional typed-relation frontmatter layer\u003c/strong\u003e rendered as a relations panel + lightweight rollups; \u003cstrong\u003efilterable/sortable listings\u003c/strong\u003e over frontmatter (this is just a Dataview/MkDocs-tags hybrid — cheap).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"5-logseq-outliner-graph-journals\"\u003e5. Logseq  \u003cem\u003e(outliner + graph + journals)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(a) What it is.\u003c/strong\u003e Local-first open-source outliner-knowledge-base (markdown/org-mode files on disk), block-granular.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(b) Worth stealing:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eblock references\u003c/strong\u003e and \u003cstrong\u003ejournals\u003c/strong\u003e (daily pages as a default capture surface); \u003cstrong\u003eDatalog queries\u003c/strong\u003e over the block graph (more rigorous than Obsidian's Dataview). \u003cstrong\u003eDoesn't translate:\u003c/strong\u003e the outliner model (indentation = structure) is alien to OKF's prose+headings; block-level references impose the same anchor-management cost as Obsidian's. \u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e the idea that \u003cstrong\u003equeries are a first-class reading surface\u003c/strong\u003e, and that a \u003cstrong\u003edated \"journal\"-style surface\u003c/strong\u003e is a good home for \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"6-foam-dendron-markdown-knowledge-bases-in-the-editor\"\u003e6. Foam / Dendron  \u003cem\u003e(markdown knowledge bases in the editor)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(a) What they are.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eFoam\u003c/strong\u003e = VSCode extension + conventions for a markdown knowledge base (graph, backlinks, wikilinks, templates), built on \u003ccode\u003emarkdown-it\u003c/code\u003e. \u003cstrong\u003eDendron\u003c/strong\u003e = VSCode extension with \u003cstrong\u003enote hierarchies\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eproject.area.topic\u003c/code\u003e dotted paths), \u003cstrong\u003eJSON note schemas\u003c/strong\u003e that validate hierarchy structure, \u003cstrong\u003elookup\u003c/strong\u003e (fuzzy-find to traverse/create hierarchies), \u003cstrong\u003emulti-vault\u003c/strong\u003e (mix several git-backed folders), and a publish step.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(b) Worth stealing:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDendron's schemas as an \u003cem\u003eoptional\u003c/em\u003e structural validator.\u003c/strong\u003e OKF forbids a global schema registry (SPEC §1), but a \u003cem\u003ebundle-local\u003c/em\u003e schema (\"concepts under \u003ccode\u003etables/\u003c/code\u003e must have a \u003ccode\u003e# Schema\u003c/code\u003e section and a \u003ccode\u003eresource\u003c/code\u003e URI\") is a natural plugin. This is how OKF can offer strict checks \u003cem\u003ewithout\u003c/em\u003e breaking permissiveness: strictness is opt-in per subtree, layered atop the always-on conformance checks (SPEC §9).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMulti-vault\u003c/strong\u003e → OKF multi-bundle composition (mount several bundles, resolve \u003ccode\u003e/...\u003c/code\u003e links against a union root). Useful for org-wide cross-linking.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFoam's template snippets\u003c/strong\u003e (frontmatter templates for new concepts) → a \u003ccode\u003eokf new\u003c/code\u003e scaffolding generator per \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(c) Doesn't translate:\u003c/strong\u003e both are \u003cstrong\u003eeditor-integrated\u003c/strong\u003e (VSCode); Dendron's dotted-path hierarchy is one opinion OKF shouldn't mandate (OKF paths are free-form).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eoptional per-subtree structural schemas\u003c/strong\u003e as a plugin; \u003cstrong\u003emulti-bundle mounting\u003c/strong\u003e; \u003cstrong\u003eper-type frontmatter templates\u003c/strong\u003e for scaffolding; Dendron \u003cstrong\u003elookup\u003c/strong\u003e-style fuzzy navigation in the viewer.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"7-lightweight-markdown-search-pagefind-lunr-minisearch-stork-flexsearch\"\u003e7. Lightweight markdown search  \u003cem\u003e(Pagefind, Lunr, MiniSearch, Stork, FlexSearch)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eTool\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eStack\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eModel\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhy it matters to OKF\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePagefind\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRust indexer + WASM runtime + UI\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePost-build static\u003c/strong\u003e: scans built HTML, emits sharded fragment index; WASM searches in-browser; lazy-loads shards per query\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBest-in-class for \u003cem\u003estatic\u003c/em\u003e sites: zero server, tiny bandwidth, scales to large corpora, supports \u003ccode\u003edata-pagefind-filter\u003c/code\u003e (facets) and \u003ccode\u003edata-pagefind-weight\u003c/code\u003e. The right default for OKF's static-HTML build target.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlexSearch\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eJS\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eIn-memory, prefix tokenizer\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhat Quartz uses; \u0026lt;10ms @ 500k words. Good for the live dev-server / SPA viewer.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMiniSearch\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eJS, \u003cstrong\u003ezero deps\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eIn-memory, prefix + fuzzy + field-boost + autosuggest + custom \u003ccode\u003etokenize\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eprocessTerm\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eextractField\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBest fit for a \u003cem\u003eself-contained single-HTML\u003c/em\u003e viewer: tiny, offline, field-weighted, no build step.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLunr.js\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eJS\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eIn-memory, 14 stemmer languages, boost, fuzzy, wildcards\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eMature classic; weaker than MiniSearch on API ergonomics.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStork\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRust → WASM, config-driven index file\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBuild-time index, WASM search\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eFine alternative to Pagefind for pre-built indexes.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe composite lesson:\u003c/strong\u003e OKF needs \u003cstrong\u003etwo lexical search surfaces\u003c/strong\u003e — (1) a build-time shard index (Pagefind-style) for the static site, and (2) an in-memory JSON index (MiniSearch/FlexSearch-style) for the self-contained single-HTML file and the live dev server. Both should be generated from the \u003cem\u003esame\u003c/em\u003e canonical content index (Quartz §1 lesson).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003ePagefind for the static site\u003c/strong\u003e (post-build, sharded, faceted); \u003cstrong\u003eMiniSearch for self-contained HTML\u003c/strong\u003e (zero-dep, field-weighted); expose a \u003cstrong\u003esingle search plugin interface\u003c/strong\u003e so either (or the Python BM25 baseline) can sit behind it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"8-hugo-jekyll-content-model-taxonomies-render-hooks\"\u003e8. Hugo / Jekyll  \u003cem\u003e(content model + taxonomies + render hooks)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(a) Worth stealing:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTaxonomies\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecategories\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eseries\u003c/code\u003e, custom). Hugo auto-generates term-list pages and term pages — the same synthesize-listings pattern. OKF already makes \u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e first-class (SPEC §4.1) and explicitly says tag views are \"synthesized at consumption time\" (SPEC §3.1) — so this is \u003cem\u003emandated by the spec\u003c/em\u003e; okf-loom just implements it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSections / content organization\u003c/strong\u003e and \u003cstrong\u003erender hooks\u003c/strong\u003e (Hugo \u003ccode\u003elink.render\u003c/code\u003e-hook lets you rewrite every link — exactly the \u003ccode\u003eCrawlLinks\u003c/code\u003e idea, in Go).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShortcodes\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003e{{\u0026lt; foo \u0026gt;}}\u003c/code\u003e) → OKF \"include concept section\" / \"embed graph\" transformers.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFast incremental builds\u003c/strong\u003e (Hugo). OKF's watcher/dev-server should rebuild only changed concepts.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(b) Doesn't translate:\u003c/strong\u003e both are \u003cstrong\u003eblog/docs SSGs\u003c/strong\u003e with a linear content model; OKF is graph-first. Shortcodes/template languages are non-portable. \u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e auto-generated \u003cstrong\u003etaxonomy pages\u003c/strong\u003e (mandated anyway), \u003cstrong\u003elink render-hooks\u003c/strong\u003e, \u003cstrong\u003eincremental rebuild\u003c/strong\u003e for the dev server.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"9-docusaurus-versioning-i18n-presets\"\u003e9. Docusaurus  \u003cem\u003e(versioning + i18n + presets)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(a) Worth stealing:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVersioning\u003c/strong\u003e of \u003cem\u003edocs\u003c/em\u003e (snapshot a version, route under \u003ccode\u003e/version-2.x\u003c/code\u003e) via a \u003ccode\u003eversioned_docs/\u003c/code\u003e directory. OKF bundles already carry \u003ccode\u003eokf_version\u003c/code\u003e (SPEC §11); okf-loom could render bundle version-history (git tags) as a Docusaurus-style version switch.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePlugin/preset system\u003c/strong\u003e + \u003cstrong\u003eswizzlable theme components\u003c/strong\u003e (override a single React component). The \"override one component without forking\" idea maps to OKF template overrides.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSearch\u003c/strong\u003e: Algolia DocSearch (hosted) \u003cstrong\u003eor\u003c/strong\u003e local search plugin; \u003cstrong\u003ei18n\u003c/strong\u003e with locale sub-paths.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMDX\u003c/strong\u003e (markdown + components).\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e(b) Doesn't translate:\u003c/strong\u003e React/MDX toolchain; opinionated docs-site product. \u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eversion switcher\u003c/strong\u003e over bundle history; \u003cstrong\u003eswizzlable component overrides\u003c/strong\u003e as the \u003cem\u003etemplate-override\u003c/em\u003e mechanism; \u003cstrong\u003elocal-vs-hosted search split\u003c/strong\u003e (again).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"10-semantic-search-over-markdown-embeddings-vector-stores-hybrid\"\u003e10. Semantic search over markdown  \u003cem\u003e(embeddings + vector stores + hybrid)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom already commits to this split: the baseline stays dependency-light with a PyYAML-preferred fallback, while richer semantic providers remain optional. The research confirms this is the right instinct and fills in the pluggable backend.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEmbedding options (offline-capable):\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003esentence-transformers\u003c/strong\u003e (HuggingFace): dense bi-encoders (e.g. \u003ccode\u003eall-MiniLM-L6-v2\u003c/code\u003e, 384-dim), \u003cstrong\u003eSparse encoders\u003c/strong\u003e (SPLADE — learned sparse, BM25-like but semantic), and \u003cstrong\u003eCross-encoder rerankers\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003ems-marco-MiniLM\u003c/code\u003e). Relevant efficiency techniques: \u003cstrong\u003eMatryoshka\u003c/strong\u003e embeddings (truncatable to smaller dims with little quality loss), \u003cstrong\u003estatic embeddings\u003c/strong\u003e (no attention, CPU-friendly), \u003cstrong\u003ebinary/scalar quantization\u003c/strong\u003e. Requires \u003ccode\u003etorch\u003c/code\u003e + \u003ccode\u003etransformers\u003c/code\u003e (heavy); fine as an \u003cem\u003eoptional\u003c/em\u003e extra.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAPI embeddings\u003c/strong\u003e (OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage, Nomic): higher quality, but require network + keys + money — explicitly out of scope for the \"works without GPU/internet\" baseline. Expose as an optional remote backend only.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVector stores for small/corpus-on-disk scale:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003esqlite-vec\u003c/strong\u003e (successor to sqlite-vss): pure C, \u003cstrong\u003ezero deps, runs anywhere SQLite runs — including WASM in the browser\u003c/strong\u003e, stores float/int8/binary vectors in \u003ccode\u003evec0\u003c/code\u003e virtual tables, KNN queries. Mozilla-sponsored. \u003cem\u003eIdeal for OKF\u003c/em\u003e: one SQLite file ships with the bundle; even the static viewer could query it via WASM. Companion \u003ccode\u003esqlite-lembed\u003c/code\u003e (local GGUF embeddings) and \u003ccode\u003esqlite-rembed\u003c/code\u003e (remote) exist.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLanceDB\u003c/strong\u003e: embedded (local, no server) on the Lance columnar format; \u003cstrong\u003evector + full-text + SQL\u003c/strong\u003e hybrid in one engine; Python/JS/Rust. A heavier but self-contained option that unifies lexical + dense in a single query — attractive if okf-loom wants one store for everything.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFAISS / Chroma\u003c/strong\u003e: FAISS = library, index you manage yourself; Chroma = embedded vector DB (client/server). Both fine; heavier than sqlite-vec for OKF's scale.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIn-memory cosine\u003c/strong\u003e: for very small bundles, just numpy/sklearn cosine over a 2-D matrix — no store at all. Good default for the \u003ccode\u003e[semantic]\u003c/code\u003e extra at small scale.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChunking markdown:\u003c/strong\u003e chunk by \u003cstrong\u003eheading\u003c/strong\u003e (so each \u003ccode\u003e# Schema\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e# Examples\u003c/code\u003e block is a retrievable unit), keep concept ID + heading path as metadata, and \u003cem\u003ealso\u003c/em\u003e keep a concept-level summary embedding (of \u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e+\u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e). Heading-chunking aligns with OKF's conventional body sections and gives citations that point to a section, not just a document.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHybrid BM25 + dense:\u003c/strong\u003e the robust recipe is \u003cstrong\u003eretrieval-time fusion\u003c/strong\u003e (BM25 candidate set ∪ dense candidate set, then reciprocal-rank-fusion or score normalization), optionally a \u003cstrong\u003ecross-encoder rerank\u003c/strong\u003e of the top-K. SPLADE can replace BM25 if you want learned-sparse without maintaining two systems.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWorks without GPU/internet?\u003c/strong\u003e Yes: TF-IDF/BM25 (pure Python or MiniSearch/Lunr) is the always-on baseline; \u003ccode\u003eall-MiniLM-L6-v2\u003c/code\u003e + sqlite-vec runs on CPU offline (download the model once); everything degrades gracefully to lexical-only when the extra isn't installed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e a \u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e interface\u003c/strong\u003e with three providers — \u003ccode\u003e(1)\u003c/code\u003e lexical BM25/TF-IDF (always on, the \u003ccode\u003e[semantic]\u003c/code\u003e=sklearn default), \u003ccode\u003e(2)\u003c/code\u003e optional local dense (\u003ccode\u003esentence-transformers\u003c/code\u003e + \u003ccode\u003esqlite-vec\u003c/code\u003e or in-memory cosine), \u003ccode\u003e(3)\u003c/code\u003e optional remote (API embeddings) — combined via \u003cstrong\u003ereciprocal-rank-fusion\u003c/strong\u003e with optional cross-encoder rerank; \u003cstrong\u003eheading-aware chunking\u003c/strong\u003e; a concept-summary vector alongside per-section vectors.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"11-entity-relation-extraction-from-prose-find-missing-relations\"\u003e11. Entity / relation extraction from prose  \u003cem\u003e(find missing relations)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSPEC §5.3 says link \u003cem\u003esemantics\u003c/em\u003e are conveyed by surrounding prose, and §5 says consumers MUST tolerate broken links. Auto-discovery of \"missing\" entities/relations means mining bodies for: (i) mentions of known concept titles/IDs that aren't linked, and (ii) novel entities/relations worth promoting to frontmatter or links.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTooling usable offline:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGLiNER\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003cstrong\u003ezero-shot NER\u003c/strong\u003e (\"give labels, get spans, no training\"), plus \u003cstrong\u003ejoint NER + relation extraction\u003c/strong\u003e via the \u003cstrong\u003eRelEx\u003c/strong\u003e architecture — \u003cem\u003ebuild a knowledge graph in one pass\u003c/em\u003e. Optimized for \u003cstrong\u003eCPU\u003c/strong\u003e, supports INT8 quant and \u003cstrong\u003eONNX export\u003c/strong\u003e. \u003ccode\u003egliner_small-v2.5\u003c/code\u003e. This is the strongest single offline pick for \"find entities/relations in markdown notes\" with user-supplied label sets.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003espaCy NER\u003c/strong\u003e: fast, rule-based (\u003ccode\u003eEntityRuler\u003c/code\u003e) + statistical; great for stable entity types and for \u003ccode\u003egliner-spacy\u003c/code\u003e integration; deterministic and light.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eREBEL\u003c/strong\u003e (seq2seq relation extraction): older, T5-based; superseded functionally by GLiNER-RelEx for new work.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLLM zero-shot extraction\u003c/strong\u003e: highest quality, highest cost; the \u003ccode\u003e[llm]\u003c/code\u003e extra's natural use — output \u003cem\u003estructured\u003c/em\u003e relation suggestions (subject concept, relation type, object concept, evidence span) for human/agent review.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCrucial design point:\u003c/strong\u003e extraction output must be \u003cstrong\u003estructured and attributable\u003c/strong\u003e so the managing agent can apply it reliably — an \u003cem\u003eagent-readable update plan\u003c/em\u003e (a diff of proposed links/frontmatter keys + evidence + confidence). Whether that plan is applied directly by the agent (the current default — see \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/spec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e §10) or routed through an opt-in review step is a product choice, not a property of the extraction. This dovetails with Section C's \"auto-update without destroying hand-curated content.\"\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSchema-aware extraction:\u003c/strong\u003e combine a bundle-local schema (Dendron §6) with GLiNER labels so extraction targets the relations \u003cem\u003eyour bundle cares about\u003c/em\u003e (e.g. for a BigQuery catalog: \u003ccode\u003ejoins\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edepends_on\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eowner\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esla\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e a \u003cstrong\u003ediscovery pass\u003c/strong\u003e = (a) unlinked-mention detection over known concept titles (Obsidian §2, pure string/fuzzy match — always on), (b) optional \u003cstrong\u003eGLiNER zero-shot NER + RelEx\u003c/strong\u003e (CPU, offline) for novel entities/relations, (c) optional \u003cstrong\u003eLLM\u003c/strong\u003e for high-quality relation hints — all emitting a \u003cstrong\u003estructured, attributable update plan\u003c/strong\u003e the managing agent applies through the mutators (directly by default in the current studio model — \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/spec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e §10; reviewable as an opt-in user constraint).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"12-knowledge-graph-tooling-typed-relations-interoperability\"\u003e12. Knowledge-graph tooling  \u003cem\u003e(typed relations + interoperability)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNeo4j/Memgraph (labeled property graphs: nodes + typed edges + properties), RDF/SPARQL (triples, open-world), n-quads/JSON-LD/schema.org (web-interop vocabularies). These represent \u003cstrong\u003etyped relations natively\u003c/strong\u003e; OKF deliberately doesn't (SPEC §5.3: link kind is conveyed by prose, graph edges are \"untyped\").\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCould OKF adopt an optional typed-relation frontmatter key without breaking the spec?\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eYes — and the spec already permits it.\u003c/strong\u003e SPEC §4.1 allows arbitrary frontmatter keys, and §9 forbids rejecting bundles over unknown keys. So a \u003cem\u003econvention\u003c/em\u003e such as:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003erelations:\n  depends_on: [/tables/customers.md, /jobs/ingest.md]\n  joins_with: [/tables/customers.md]\n  owner: @data-platform\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eis \u003cstrong\u003ealready spec-legal\u003c/strong\u003e as producer-defined keys. okf-loom should:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRecognize a small, conventional relation vocabulary\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003edepends_on\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ereferences\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003epart_of\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ederived_from\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eowner\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esee_also\u003c/code\u003e) in a \u003cem\u003ecapability/extension namespace\u003c/em\u003e (e.g. prefix \u003ccode\u003eokf.rel.*\u003c/code\u003e or a \u003ccode\u003erelations:\u003c/code\u003e map) — \u003cem\u003erecognized, not required\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRender typed relations in the viewer as \u003cstrong\u003elabeled graph edges\u003c/strong\u003e (color/style per relation type) and in a relations panel.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eOptionally \u003cstrong\u003eexport\u003c/strong\u003e the bundle to JSON-LD (using schema.org where types fit) or n-quads/Neo4j CSV for external graph tools — a one-way \u003cem\u003ebridge\u003c/em\u003e, never a source of truth.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMap untyped prose-links (the default) to a generic \u003ccode\u003erelates_to\u003c/code\u003e edge so the graph is never empty.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDoesn't translate:\u003c/strong\u003e RDF open-world/IRI identity, SPARQL federation, graph DB transactions — far beyond OKF's \"cat a file\" philosophy. Keep KG interop as an \u003cem\u003eexport transformer\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e an \u003cstrong\u003eoptional, namespaced typed-relation frontmatter convention\u003c/strong\u003e (already spec-legal), rendered as labeled edges; a \u003cstrong\u003eJSON-LD / schema.org export transformer\u003c/strong\u003e for interop; treat the prose graph as the canonical, always-present \u003ccode\u003erelates_to\u003c/code\u003e baseline.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"13-diátaxis-a-default-concept-type-taxonomy\"\u003e13. Diátaxis  \u003cem\u003e(a default concept-type taxonomy?)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eDiátaxis divides docs into \u003cstrong\u003eTutorials\u003c/strong\u003e (learning by doing), \u003cstrong\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/strong\u003e (achieving a goal), \u003cstrong\u003eReference\u003c/strong\u003e (information-oriented, authoritative), \u003cstrong\u003eExplanation\u003c/strong\u003e (understanding-oriented). It's a \u003cem\u003epurpose\u003c/em\u003e taxonomy, not a domain taxonomy.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRelevance to OKF:\u003c/strong\u003e SPEC explicitly \u003cem\u003edeclines\u003c/em\u003e a fixed type taxonomy (§1 non-goals) and §4.1 lists example \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e values (\u003ccode\u003eBigQuery Table\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ePlaybook\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eReference\u003c/code\u003e, …). Diátaxis is therefore \u003cstrong\u003enot a mandate but a strong recommended default for doc-oriented bundles\u003c/strong\u003e: okf-loom could ship an \u003cem\u003eoptional\u003c/em\u003e Diátaxis preset that suggests \u003ccode\u003etype: tutorial|how-to|reference|explanation\u003c/code\u003e, validates each type's conventional sections (tutorials have steps; reference has schema), and renders a four-quadrant landing page. For data-catalog bundles it's irrelevant (those types are domain-specific). Keep it as an \u003cstrong\u003eopt-in type-vocabulary plugin\u003c/strong\u003e, never core.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e ship Diátaxis as an \u003cstrong\u003eoptional type taxonomy + section checker\u003c/strong\u003e for documentation bundles; never impose it on domain catalogs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"14-roam-devonthink-bear-apple-notes-what-consumers-want\"\u003e14. Roam / DEVONthink / Bear / Apple Notes  \u003cem\u003e(what consumers want)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSurveyed for \u003cem\u003eexpectations\u003c/em\u003e, not mechanisms: consumers want \u003cstrong\u003einstant capture\u003c/strong\u003e (Roam's daily notes), \u003cstrong\u003ebi-directional links without ceremony\u003c/strong\u003e (Roam/Obsidian), \u003cstrong\u003estrong search + AI-assisted browsing\u003c/strong\u003e (DEVONthink's see-also/classify), \u003cstrong\u003efast tag/note navigation + beautiful typography\u003c/strong\u003e (Bear), \u003cstrong\u003eubiquity + sharing\u003c/strong\u003e (Apple Notes). Common thread: \u003cstrong\u003elow-friction linking, instant search, and \"what's related?\" assistance\u003c/strong\u003e. OKF's toolkit already targets all three via auto-discovery (§11) + hybrid search (§10) + graph/backlinks (§1/§2). Nothing here is portable as a \u003cem\u003emechanism\u003c/em\u003e (all are closed/local-DB apps); they confirm priorities.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cem\u003eproduct priorities\u003c/em\u003e — make linking and \"see also\" effortless and instant; these are the features users will reach for first.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"15-self-contained-html-viewer-patterns-single-file-vs-spa-vs-server-rendered\"\u003e15. Self-contained HTML viewer patterns  \u003cem\u003e(single-file vs SPA vs server-rendered)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe brief's reference design (call it \u003cstrong\u003ePattern A\u003c/strong\u003e: one HTML file embedding the whole bundle as JSON + Cytoscape.js + marked) sits at one end of a spectrum:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003ePattern\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eExample\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003ePros\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCons\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eOKF fit\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA. Single self-contained HTML\u003c/strong\u003e (bundle-as-JSON inline)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOKF \u003ccode\u003eviz.html\u003c/code\u003e reference; \u003cstrong\u003eMiniSearch/Lunr\u003c/strong\u003e in-page\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eMaximally portable: email it, \u003ccode\u003efile://\u003c/code\u003e-open it, drop in any repo; git-diffable; no server; works offline\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRe-encodes \u003cem\u003eall\u003c/em\u003e content into one file → large for big bundles; no per-URL linking/bookmarking; Cytoscape.js is heavy (~hundreds of KB); search is whole-bundle-in-memory\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGreat as a \"share one bundle\" export\u003c/strong\u003e and a zero-setup default; should be a \u003cem\u003ebuild target\u003c/em\u003e, not the only surface\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eB. SPA (multi-file static)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQuartz\u003c/strong\u003e, Obsidian-publish\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePer-concept URLs (deep-linkable, bookmarkable); code-splits; rich interactivity (popovers, SPA nav, graph, search); CDN/any-static-host\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eNeeds JS; less \"single artifact\"; client-side routing\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBest interactive reading experience\u003c/strong\u003e; default for the published site\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eC. Server-rendered static\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMkDocs Material\u003c/strong\u003e, Hugo\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eNo-JS/SEO-friendly; clean URLs; printable\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eNo client graph/SPA; rebuild to update\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBest for portability/SEO/print\u003c/strong\u003e; good default for \"static docs\" consumers\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eD. Live HTTP dev server\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eQuartz dev, MkDocs serve\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eHot reload, interactive editing, run discovery live\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRequires a process\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEssential authoring loop\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRecommendation (detailed in Synthesis B):\u003c/strong\u003e support \u003cstrong\u003eall four\u003c/strong\u003e from one content index, because they serve different deployment shapes OKF explicitly wants (portability, git-friendliness, interactivity, embedding in a harness). For Pattern A specifically: prefer \u003cstrong\u003eMiniSearch\u003c/strong\u003e (zero-dep, field-weighted) over rolling a bespoke search, and make the graph \u003cem\u003elazy\u003c/em\u003e (only the local subgraph on open) so a single-file viewer stays responsive. Avoid bundling Cytoscape.js unconditionally — offer a lighter force-directed renderer (e.g. \u003ccode\u003ed3-force\u003c/code\u003e + canvas/SVG) and treat the heavy Cytoscape option as an override.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhat OKF should steal:\u003c/strong\u003e treat single-file HTML as \u003cstrong\u003eone export target\u003c/strong\u003e (not the only viewer); default the static site to \u003cstrong\u003eQuartz-style SPA\u003c/strong\u003e for interactivity and \u003cstrong\u003eMkDocs-style server-rendered\u003c/strong\u003e for portability; always include a \u003cstrong\u003elive dev server\u003c/strong\u003e; generate \u003cstrong\u003eall surfaces from one canonical content index\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"synthesis\"\u003eSynthesis\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"a-search-architecture-for-okf\"\u003eA. Search architecture for OKF\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLayered design, all behind one interface.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCanonical content index (produced once).\u003c/strong\u003e A single in-memory model — \u003ccode\u003e{ concepts: [{id, path, type, title, description, tags, timestamp, resource, headings, sections, body_text, frontmatter, out_links, in_links}], bundle: {okf_version, ...} }\u003c/code\u003e. This is the Quartz \u003ccode\u003eContentIndex\u003c/code\u003e lesson: search, graph, and listings all read the \u003cem\u003esame\u003c/em\u003e object. It is also the validation graph (so link/structure checks share code with search).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLayer 0 — always-on lexical (zero deps).\u003c/strong\u003e BM25/TF-IDF over \u003cstrong\u003etitle + description + section bodies + tags\u003c/strong\u003e, with \u003cstrong\u003efield weights\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e \u0026gt; \u003ccode\u003eheading\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eSchema\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eExamples\u003c/code\u003e \u0026gt; body \u0026gt; tags-for-text), markdown stripped at index time, tokenization with CJK support, prefix/fuzzy matching. This baseline is implemented in pure Python (or, for the JS viewers, generated into a MiniSearch/FlexSearch index). Tag-mode search via \u003ccode\u003e#\u003c/code\u003e. This layer alone satisfies \"search by term/relation/entity\" for lexical needs and \u003cstrong\u003eworks without GPU/internet\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLayer 1 — optional semantic (local, \u003ccode\u003e[semantic]\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003e[llm]\u003c/code\u003e extras).\u003c/strong\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEmbeddings:\u003c/strong\u003e prefer \u003cstrong\u003esentence-transformers\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eall-MiniLM-L6-v2\u003c/code\u003e (CPU, offline, 384-dim, Matryoshka-truncatable). Chunk \u003cstrong\u003eby heading\u003c/strong\u003e + keep a concept-summary vector of \u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e+\u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStore:\u003c/strong\u003e default \u003cstrong\u003ein-memory cosine\u003c/strong\u003e (numpy/sklearn) for small bundles; scale to \u003cstrong\u003esqlite-vec\u003c/strong\u003e (one \u003ccode\u003e.db\u003c/code\u003e file, WASM-able, float/int8/binary) when the bundle is large or the static viewer must query offline. \u003ccode\u003esqlite-vec\u003c/code\u003e is the standout pick because it runs in-browser via WASM, matching OKF's \"plain files, no server\" ethos.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAPI embeddings\u003c/strong\u003e (OpenAI/Cohere/Voyage/Nomic) as a remote provider behind the same interface.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLayer 2 — hybrid fusion + rerank.\u003c/strong\u003e Retrieve BM25 top-N \u003cstrong\u003e∪\u003c/strong\u003e dense top-N, merge by \u003cstrong\u003ereciprocal rank fusion\u003c/strong\u003e, optionally rerank top-K with a \u003cstrong\u003ecross-encoder\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003ems-marco-MiniLM\u003c/code\u003e). Expose a \u003ccode\u003erelation\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eentity\u003c/code\u003e facet (from §11 extraction) so \"search by relation/entity\" is a filter over typed relations + NER tags.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePlugin interface (what a backend must implement):\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003e   class SearchBackend(Protocol):\n       def index(self, content_index: ContentIndex) -\u0026gt; None: ...\n       def search(self, query: str, *, mode: SearchMode,\n                  filters: Filters | None, limit: int) -\u0026gt; list[SearchResult]: ...\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ewith \u003ccode\u003eSearchMode = LEXICAL | SEMANTIC | HYBRID | TAG\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eSearchResult\u003c/code\u003e carrying \u003ccode\u003e{concept_id, section_path, score, match_spans, source_backend}\u003c/code\u003e. A \u003ccode\u003eLexicalBackend\u003c/code\u003e (always present), \u003ccode\u003eDenseBackend\u003c/code\u003e (sentence-transformers), \u003ccode\u003eRemoteBackend\u003c/code\u003e (API), and a \u003ccode\u003eHybridBackend\u003c/code\u003e (fusion of any two) all implement it. Registration via entry-points so downstream harnesses plug in their own.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eJustification:\u003c/strong\u003e the layering matches the spec's permissiveness and the checkout's explicit optional proof dependencies; the \u003cstrong\u003econtent-index-first\u003c/strong\u003e design avoids N indexes; \u003cstrong\u003esqlite-vec + MiniSearch\u003c/strong\u003e give \"offline, no-server, single-artifact\" search that no incumbent fully delivers together.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"b-viewer-architecture-for-okf\"\u003eB. Viewer architecture for OKF\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOne content index → four build targets\u003c/strong\u003e (rationale in §15), with \u003cstrong\u003ewiki navigation and graph view coexisting in one experience\u003c/strong\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — live HTTP dev server. Watch bundle; on change, rebuild only affected concepts (Hugo-style incremental); run validator + discovery pass; push results over WebSocket. This is the authoring loop and the harness-embedding entrypoint (a meta-agent points a browser at \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom build --spa\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Quartz-style multi-file static site (per-concept URLs, SPA routing, popovers, local+global graph, FlexSearch/MiniSearch). Best interactive reading experience; deep-linkable. \u003cstrong\u003eDefault published surface.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom build --static\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — MkDocs-style server-rendered, no-JS HTML (printable, SEO, airgapped). For consumers who reject JS.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom build --single-file\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — one self-contained HTML (bundle JSON + MiniSearch + a light \u003ccode\u003ed3-force\u003c/code\u003e graph), for sharing/emailing/\u003ccode\u003efile://\u003c/code\u003e. The brief's Cytoscape+marked pattern belongs here, as an \u003cem\u003eoption\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUnifying wiki + graph navigation\u003c/strong\u003e (the hard requirement), following Quartz/Obsidian:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eEvery concept page renders a \u003cstrong\u003ebacklinks\u003c/strong\u003e panel (incoming links + unlinked mentions) and an \u003cstrong\u003eoutgoing-links\u003c/strong\u003e panel, both with \u003cstrong\u003epopover previews\u003c/strong\u003e (Wikipedia-style hover, using a \u003ccode\u003epopover-hint\u003c/code\u003e class to select title+description+tags+first section).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA \u003cstrong\u003elocal graph\u003c/strong\u003e widget (≤N hops, degree-weighted nodes, visited-node coloring) sits beside the page; clicking a node navigates (SPA) to that concept. A header button toggles a \u003cstrong\u003eglobal graph\u003c/strong\u003e overlay.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAll three (backlinks, local graph, search) read the \u003cstrong\u003esame \u003ccode\u003econtentIndex.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e emitted by the build, so they're consistent and cheap.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFilterable/sortable listings\u003c/strong\u003e (Notion/MkDocs-style) for directories (from \u003ccode\u003eFolderPage\u003c/code\u003e-equivalent) and tags (from \u003ccode\u003eTagPage\u003c/code\u003e-equivalent), overridable by hand-authored \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExtension points\u003c/strong\u003e (mirroring Quartz's three customization tiers):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTransformers\u003c/strong\u003e (per-concept map: parse frontmatter, resolve links, extract description, run checks, embed), \u003cstrong\u003efilters\u003c/strong\u003e (decide emit), \u003cstrong\u003eemitters\u003c/strong\u003e (reduce → site files: pages, index, search index, graph data, RSS, JSON-LD). Order matters; declare in a \u003ccode\u003eokf.config\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTemplate overrides\u003c/strong\u003e (Docusaurus \"swizzle\" style): override one partial (e.g. the graph component, the concept header) without forking.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTheme\u003c/strong\u003e (colors, fonts, layout composition via a \u003ccode\u003eFlex\u003c/code\u003e-style layout config).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLink resolution mode\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eabsolute\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003erelative\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eshortest\u003c/code\u003e) and \u003ccode\u003eignorePatterns\u003c/code\u003e as first-class config.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eJustification:\u003c/strong\u003e Quartz proves SPA + graph + search + backlinks can coexist from one index; MkDocs proves server-rendered portability; the single-file target (Pagefind/MiniSearch) proves no-server search. OKF can offer all of these because they're \u003cem\u003erenderings\u003c/em\u003e of the same model — exactly the \"embeddable in any harness\" requirement.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"c-forward-compatibility-for-okf\"\u003eC. Forward-compatibility for OKF\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom must stay correct as the spec moves (v0.1 → 0.x → 1.0) \u003cstrong\u003eand\u003c/strong\u003e let bundles extend without breaking. Concrete mechanisms:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSpec-version tracking.\u003c/strong\u003e A single \u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.spec.SPEC_VERSION = \"0.1\"\u003c/code\u003e plus a parser of the rules in SPEC §9 (conformance = parseable FM + non-empty \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e + reserved-filename structure). At load time, read the bundle's declared \u003ccode\u003eokf_version\u003c/code\u003e (SPEC §11, root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e frontmatter); if okf-loom doesn't \u003cem\u003eunderstand\u003c/em\u003e that version it does \u003cstrong\u003ebest-effort consumption\u003c/strong\u003e (SPEC §11 mandate) and emits a warning, never a hard failure. Keep a \u003ccode\u003eVersionedRuleSet\u003c/code\u003e keyed by \u003ccode\u003e(major, minor)\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCapability registry (the key forward-compat mechanism).\u003c/strong\u003e A manifest of named capabilities okf-loom \u003cem\u003erecognizes\u003c/em\u003e, each declaring: an id (e.g. \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.typed_relations\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.diataxis_types\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.log_timeline\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.embeddings\u003c/code\u003e), min spec version, whether it's \u003ccode\u003ecore\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003erecommended\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eoptional\u003c/code\u003e, and the frontmatter keys / body sections it governs. This is the \u003cem\u003eextension namespace\u003c/em\u003e from §12: typed relations live under \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.typed_relations\u003c/code\u003e and use a \u003ccode\u003erelations:\u003c/code\u003e key — recognized-if-present, never required. Bundles \u003cstrong\u003eopt in\u003c/strong\u003e by using the keys; okf-loom activates the matching behavior. Unknown keys are always passed through (SPEC §9).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBundle-local capability declaration.\u003c/strong\u003e A bundle may carry its own extensions via a reserved, namespaced frontmatter block (e.g. in root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e):\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e   okf_version: \"0.1\"\n   okf_extensions:\n     - okf.cap.typed_relations   # recognized built-in\n     - acme.custom_types         # user-defined, registered via plugin\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUser-defined capabilities are supplied as \u003cstrong\u003eplugins\u003c/strong\u003e (transformer/filter/emitter + a JSON-schema fragment for the keys they introduce). This is how \"custom body sections / typed relations\" extend OKF \u003cem\u003ewithout\u003c/em\u003e touching the spec — the spec already allows arbitrary keys; the registry just makes them \u003cem\u003emeaningful\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMigration hooks.\u003c/strong\u003e Between minor bumps: a registry of idempotent \u003ccode\u003emigrate(old_minor -\u0026gt; new_minor, bundle)\u003c/code\u003e functions; okf-loom runs them on \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom upgrade --check\u003c/code\u003e (dry-run, prints a diff) and \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom upgrade --apply\u003c/code\u003e. Between major bumps: explicit, opt-in, with a backup/branch recommendation. Migrations are \u003cem\u003etransformers\u003c/em\u003e, reusing the same pipeline.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAuto-update without destroying hand-curated content\u003c/strong\u003e (the hard constraint). The model is \u003cstrong\u003e\"synthesize by default, defer to hand-authored, touch only marked regions.\"\u003c/strong\u003e Mechanism:\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e regeneration:\u003c/strong\u003e if a directory's \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e is \u003cstrong\u003ehand-authored\u003c/strong\u003e (no \u003ccode\u003egenerated: true\u003c/code\u003e marker OR a \u003ccode\u003eokf-managed\u003c/code\u003e comment-fence region), the generator \u003cstrong\u003enever overwrites it\u003c/strong\u003e — it only \u003cem\u003efills missing entries\u003c/em\u003e or emits a warning listing what's absent (Quartz \u003ccode\u003eFolderPage\u003c/code\u003e behavior). If the file is \u003cstrong\u003etoolkit-generated\u003c/strong\u003e (frontmatter \u003ccode\u003egenerated: true\u003c/code\u003e or content between markers like \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;!-- okf:generated:index begin --\u0026gt; … \u0026lt;!-- okf:generated:index end --\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e), the generator rewrites \u003cstrong\u003eonly the marked region\u003c/strong\u003e, preserving anything outside it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e append:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cem\u003ealways append-only\u003c/em\u003e under a today-dated \u003ccode\u003e## YYYY-MM-DD\u003c/code\u003e heading (SPEC §7); never edit history. New entries are derived from \u003ccode\u003egit log\u003c/code\u003e/diffs since the last recorded date (set via a \u003ccode\u003eokf:last_log_date\u003c/code\u003e marker or the newest existing heading).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003erelations:\u003c/code\u003e / tags / frontmatter suggestions from discovery (§11)\u003c/strong\u003e are applied through \u003cstrong\u003emarker-safe mutators\u003c/strong\u003e that never destroy hand-curated content (hand-authored \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e is only filled within \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;!-- okf:generated:index --\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e fences; \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e is append-only). In the early design the default is to write these to a sidecar \u003ccode\u003eokf-suggestions.json\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e# Citations\u003c/code\u003e-style \u003ccode\u003eokf-suggestions.md\u003c/code\u003e) plus an agent-readable diff for review; in the current design the managing agent applies them \u003cstrong\u003edirectly\u003c/strong\u003e through those same safe mutators (\u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/spec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e §10). Either way the SPEC §9 permissiveness contract and hand-curated content are preserved.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA \u003ccode\u003e--frozen\u003c/code\u003e mode for CI: regeneration that \u003cem\u003ewould\u003c/em\u003e write a hand-authored file fails loudly instead.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhy these mechanisms:\u003c/strong\u003e markers (comment-fences + \u003ccode\u003egenerated:\u003c/code\u003e frontmatter) are the lightest weight, survive \u003ccode\u003ecat\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003egit diff\u003c/code\u003e (spec's \"readable without tooling\"), and are already a proven pattern (Region markers in literate tools; Quartz's \"index.md override\"). A capability registry + namespaced extensions is how typed relations/custom sections can grow \u003cem\u003ewithout\u003c/em\u003e a spec change (already legal under §4.1/§9). Migrations-as-transformers reuses the core pipeline rather than inventing a parallel system.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"appendix\"\u003eAppendix\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"a-source-grounding-discrepancies\"\u003eA. Source grounding \u0026amp; discrepancies\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOKF SPEC.md v0.1 — Draft\u003c/strong\u003e (fetched from \u003ccode\u003eGoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog\u003c/code\u003e \u003ccode\u003eokf/SPEC.md\u003c/code\u003e, 451 lines) — the binding rules cited as \u003ccode\u003eSPEC §N\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eviz.html\u003c/code\u003e does not exist\u003c/strong\u003e in the current upstream \u003ccode\u003eokf/\u003c/code\u003e tree (only \u003ccode\u003eSPEC.md\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebundles/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esamples/{crypto_bitcoin,ga4_merch_store,stackoverflow}\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esrc/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etests/\u003c/code\u003e). The \"Cytoscape.js + marked, bundle-as-JSON single HTML\" design in §15 is treated as a \u003cem\u003ereference pattern to evaluate\u003c/em\u003e, not an existing file. If/when upstream adds a viewer, reconcile with Section B.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"b-default-recommended-capability-set-proposed\"\u003eB. Default recommended capability set (proposed)\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecore\u003c/code\u003e: \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.frontmatter\u003c/code\u003e (parse + alias-collapse), \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.links\u003c/code\u003e (absolute/relative resolution + broken-link tolerance), \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.index_md\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.log_md\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.listings\u003c/code\u003e (folder/tag pages), \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.search_lexical\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.graph\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.backlinks\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003erecommended\u003c/code\u003e: \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.search_hybrid\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.popovers\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.discovery_mentions\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.log_timeline\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003eoptional\u003c/code\u003e: \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.typed_relations\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.embeddings\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.discovery_ner\u003c/code\u003e (GLiNER), \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.discovery_llm\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.diataxis_types\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.jsonld_export\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.multi_bundle\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"c-section-index\"\u003eC. Section index\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSystems (§1–§15) → Synthesis (A Search, B Viewer, C Forward-compat) → Appendix (A grounding, B capability set, C this index).\u003c/p\u003e", "explanation/what_is_okf": "\u003ch2 id=\"what-okf-is-for\"\u003eWhat OKF is for\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis essay explains \u003cem\u003ewhy\u003c/em\u003e the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) exists, what problem it picks, and which problems it deliberately leaves to other tools. It is not a reference for the format's keys — that is \u003ca href=\"/reference/frontmatter.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003efrontmatter.md\u003c/a\u003e — nor a tutorial for writing your first file — that is \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e. It is the reasoning behind both.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe current okf-loom contract lives in the \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003ecurrent specification\u003c/a\u003e. The upstream OKF SPEC v0.1 remains the base wire-format reference okf-loom implements.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"the-problem-okf-picks\"\u003eThe problem OKF picks\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eMost knowledge that surrounds code and data — the metadata, the context, the schemas, the relationships, the playbooks, the decisions — does not have a natural home. It ends up scattered across a wiki, a data catalog, a set of design docs, some tickets, some chat threads, and a great deal of tribal memory that lives only in people's heads.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach of those homes optimises for one audience. A data catalog is optimised for a governance team and a query engine. A wiki is optimised for a human clicking through pages. A design doc is optimised for a reader absorbing one long argument. None of them is optimised for \u003cem\u003eall\u003c/em\u003e of the audiences that actually need the same knowledge today: a human browsing it, a reviewer diffing it, and an agent reading and editing it in collaboration with a human.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOKF picks the problem of representing that knowledge in a form that serves all three audiences at once, with the smallest possible mechanism. Its answer is deliberately unsexy: \u003cstrong\u003ea directory tree of plain markdown files with YAML frontmatter, linked into a graph by ordinary markdown links.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"knowledge-as-files\"\u003eKnowledge as files\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe founding bet is that \u003cem\u003efiles\u003c/em\u003e are the right unit of knowledge.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA file is readable by a human without any tooling — \u003ccode\u003ecat\u003c/code\u003e works. It is parseable by an agent without an SDK — the frontmatter is YAML and the body is markdown, both of which a language model can read and write directly. And it is diffable in git, which means knowledge becomes a normal software-engineering artefact: versioned, reviewed, branched, blamed, and reverted with the same commands you already use for code.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eConsider a single concept file:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: BigQuery Table\ntitle: Customer Orders\ndescription: One row per completed customer order across all channels.\nresource: https://example.com/path/to/asset\ntags: [sales, orders, revenue]\ntimestamp: \"2026-05-28T14:30:00Z\"\n---\n\n# Schema\n\n| Column        | Type    | Description |\n|---------------|---------|-------------|\n| `order_id`    | STRING  | Globally unique order identifier. |\n| `customer_id` | STRING  | FK to [customers](/tables/customers.md). |\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEvery one of those audiences reads the same artefact. A human opens it in their editor. A reviewer runs \u003ccode\u003egit diff\u003c/code\u003e and sees exactly which row changed. An agent reads the YAML and the table, reasons about them, and writes the next link — without a database, without a query layer, without a serialisation format it has to learn.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe SPEC is intentionally minimal: a bundle is conformant if every non-reserved file has parseable frontmatter with a non-empty \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e, and the reserved files follow their structure. Everything else is soft guidance. The format optimises for \u003cem\u003enever rejecting knowledge\u003c/em\u003e, not for \u003cem\u003eenforcing a schema\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is also why the only hard-required key is \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e. A string that names the \u003cem\u003ekind of thing\u003c/em\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eBigQuery Table\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ePlaybook\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eAPI Endpoint\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTutorial\u003c/code\u003e) is enough for a consumer to route the concept without demanding a registry the producer has to satisfy. Recommended keys (\u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eresource\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e) are encouraged but never enforced; producers may add any further keys, and consumers must preserve them round-trip.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"three-audiences-one-artefact\"\u003eThree audiences, one artefact\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe format is shaped by serving three readers from the same file.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eAudience\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhat they need\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eHow a plain markdown file serves them\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA human browsing\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eReadable text, navigation, search\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eMarkdown renders to HTML; links are navigable.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA reviewer / auditor\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eDiffable, blameable history\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne file per concept; \u003ccode\u003egit diff\u003c/code\u003e shows the change.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAn agent (LLM)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eParseable, editable, no SDK\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYAML + markdown are directly readable and writable.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe third row is the one that most prior formats ignored. A wiki stores its pages in a database; a data catalog stores its entries behind an API; a design-doc system renders from a proprietary source. In each case an agent that wants to \u003cem\u003eedit\u003c/em\u003e the knowledge has to learn a toolchain, hold an API token, or round-trip through an exporter. OKF makes the agent a first-class author: it reads the file, reasons, and writes the file back, exactly as a human would in their editor.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is not a theoretical benefit. okf-loom's whole live studio is built on it — the agent authors \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e files through ordinary mutator commands, and a watcher pushes the change to every open surface. See \u003ca href=\"live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhy the live studio exists\u003c/a\u003e for that model.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"a-graph-not-just-a-tree\"\u003eA graph, not just a tree\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA directory tree alone is not enough, because knowledge is not hierarchical. \u003ccode\u003etables/orders\u003c/code\u003e relates to \u003ccode\u003etables/customers\u003c/code\u003e (a foreign key), to \u003ccode\u003eservices/checkout\u003c/code\u003e (the writer), to \u003ccode\u003eplaybooks/refund_flow\u003c/code\u003e (a consumer), and to \u003ccode\u003eglossary/revenue\u003c/code\u003e (a definition). None of those relationships fits neatly under one parent directory.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOKF resolves this the way the wider notes-and-knowledge community resolved it: ordinary markdown links between files, turning the tree into a graph. A link in the body of one concept to another is not just decoration for a human — it is a first-class \u003cem\u003egraph edge\u003c/em\u003e that okf-loom extracts, indexes, and renders.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e| `customer_id` | STRING | FK to [customers](/tables/customers.md). |\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThat \u003ccode\u003e[customers](/tables/customers.md)\u003c/code\u003e is, simultaneously: a clickable link for a human; a relationship the discovery pass can reason about; an edge in the force-directed graph view; and a backlink on the target concept's page. One syntactic choice, four consumers served.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe link extractor recognises both forms the SPEC permits — absolute bundle-relative (\u003ccode\u003e/tables/customers.md\u003c/code\u003e, recommended and stable when files move within a subdirectory) and relative (\u003ccode\u003e./customers.md\u003c/code\u003e, for tightly-coupled siblings) — plus Obsidian-style wikilinks (\u003ccode\u003e[[customers]]\u003c/code\u003e) as a soft input. The full link model is documented in \u003ca href=\"/reference/links.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003elinks.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"vendor-neutral-and-lock-in-free\"\u003eVendor-neutral and lock-in-free\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA bundle is a directory. That is the entire deployment story. There is no server you must run, no account you must hold, no proprietary cache directory, and no schema registry your bundle is coupled to. You can \u003ccode\u003etar\u003c/code\u003e a bundle, email it, drop it in a repository, open it from \u003ccode\u003efile://\u003c/code\u003e, or mount several of them together.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe okf-loom runtime that consumes a bundle is also vendor-neutral. It is \u003cstrong\u003eharness-agnostic\u003c/strong\u003e: the same checkout runtime runs as a standalone CLI, as a Python library, or as a long-running viewer embedded inside any agent harness (opencode, Claude Code, Codex, a custom pipeline). It does not assume which agent framework consumes it, and it does not run an LLM itself — the server emits events and runs mechanical operations; the agent does the thinking externally and writes back through ordinary mutator calls. See \u003ca href=\"/how-to/embed_in_harness.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eEmbed the viewer in an agent harness\u003c/a\u003e and the deep \u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/embedding_guide.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e for the wiring shapes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eLock-in-freedom has a concrete consequence: \u003cstrong\u003ebecause a bundle is just files, the worst case is that you stop using okf-loom and read the files with something else.\u003c/strong\u003e The format is the contract, not the tool. \u003ccode\u003ecat\u003c/code\u003e is a fully supported OKF viewer.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"how-okf-compares-to-the-neighbours\"\u003eHow OKF compares to the neighbours\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom's \u003ca href=\"/explanation/research.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/explanation/research.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e surveys the best-of-breed tools OKF learned from. The short version, framed by the problem each one solves:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eNeighbour\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhat it optimises\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhy OKF does not collapse into it\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eObsidian / Logseq\u003c/strong\u003e (local markdown vaults)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA rich personal reading + authoring UX\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eProprietary binary cache, desktop GUI, wikilink-first syntax. OKF keeps standard markdown links as canonical and is a format + a harness-agnostic toolkit, not an app.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQuartz\u003c/strong\u003e (publish an Obsidian vault)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA static site from a folder of interlinked markdown\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe closest analog. OKF borrows Quartz's \"one content index feeds many features\" lesson, but adds SPEC-conformance validation, agent-authorable mutators, and a live collaborative studio rather than only a publish step.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMkDocs Material\u003c/strong\u003e (docs site)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA polished, server-rendered, searchable docs site\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSingle-page-at-a-time, no client graph, linear \u003ccode\u003enav\u003c/code\u003e. OKF is graph-first; MkDocs-style server-rendered HTML is one of okf-loom's \u003cem\u003ebuild targets\u003c/em\u003e, not its identity.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA data catalog\u003c/strong\u003e (DataHub, Amundsen, OpenMetadata)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eGoverned metadata + a query layer for a data org\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBacked by a database, schema-registry-coupled, optimised for governance. OKF has no schema registry, no database, and optimises for diffable, agent-editable files. A catalog can \u003cem\u003eexport\u003c/em\u003e to OKF; OKF does not try to be one.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA wiki / Notion\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCapture and browse unstructured team knowledge\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eHosted, block-graph-in-a-database, not portable, not diffable, not git-friendly. OKF is the opposite on every one of those axes.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA design doc\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne long argument a reader absorbs\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA single artefact with no machine-parseable structure or cross-links. OKF \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e a good home for design docs (each doc is a concept), but adds frontmatter, links, and graph relationships.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe pattern: OKF does not compete with these tools on the axis each one optimises. It competes on the axis none of them optimise — \u003cem\u003eone artefact, three audiences, no toolchain lock-in\u003c/em\u003e — and it is happy to sit alongside them. A bundle can be generated \u003cem\u003efrom\u003c/em\u003e a catalog and \u003cem\u003erendered into\u003c/em\u003e a docs site.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-okf-deliberately-is-not\"\u003eWhat OKF deliberately is NOT\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNaming the boundaries is as important as naming the goals.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"it-is-not-a-content-management-system\"\u003eIt is not a content management system\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOKF has no account system, no permissions model, no workflow state machine, and no review queue. The live studio is single-user local-admin by design: one human owns the bundle and the agent that works for them, and the studio never gates that human. (Constraints a user wants to impose on \u003cem\u003etheir own\u003c/em\u003e agent are an opt-in, never a default — see the trust model discussion in \u003ca href=\"live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003elive_studio_design.md\u003c/a\u003e.)\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"it-is-not-a-database\"\u003eIt is not a database\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThere is no query language, no indexing engine you must run, and no storage layer that is not the filesystem. okf-loom computes a graph and a content index lazily, in memory, memoised on the \u003ccode\u003eBundle\u003c/code\u003e object, and thrown away when the bundle is garbage-collected. If you want rich ad-hoc queries over history you project the append-only change feed into your own SQLite in your own module; okf-loom does not impose that complexity on core. (See \u003ca href=\"/reference/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/architecture.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e § \"Performance characteristics\".)\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"it-is-not-a-render-only-format\"\u003eIt is not a render-only format\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e files are the source of truth, not a render target. Unlike a system where you author in a rich editor and export to markdown, with OKF you author \u003cem\u003ein\u003c/em\u003e markdown, and the renders (live HTTP server, single-file HTML, multi-file static site, SPA) are projections of the same canonical model. This is what makes the agent a first-class author: it edits the source, not a rendered shadow.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIt is also not the case that the format \u003cem\u003erequires\u003c/em\u003e okf-loom to be useful. okf-loom is the production layer — it validates, searches, discovers, updates, and renders — but the format stands on its own. Anything that reads markdown and YAML can read an OKF bundle.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"why-minimal-is-the-feature\"\u003eWhy \"minimal\" is the feature\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe temptation for any knowledge format is to grow: to add a type registry, a relation vocabulary, an indexing schema, a query language. OKF resists all of those at the spec level and instead offers them as \u003cem\u003eoptional, recognised-if-present\u003c/em\u003e extensions behind a capability registry. Typed relations, entities, aliases, citations, and the Diátaxis content-type vocabulary are all available to a bundle that wants them — and invisible to a bundle that does not. See \u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003ecapabilities.md\u003c/a\u003e for the catalogue.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe payoff is that a producer never has to satisfy the format to contribute knowledge, and a consumer never has to understand the whole format to read some of it. The floor is \u003ccode\u003etype: something\u003c/code\u003e; everything above it is opt-in. That is the whole point: a format that \u003cem\u003egets out of the way\u003c/em\u003e of capturing knowledge, so the knowledge actually gets captured.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2
