choices.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/explanation/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eExplanation\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "explanation/zero_dependencies": "\u003ch2 id=\"dependency-light-philosophy\"\u003eDependency-light philosophy\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis essay explains why okf-loom keeps the primary runtime path free of install steps. PyYAML is preferred when present, and the checked-in runtime ships a conservative built-in YAML fallback for normal docs validation when it is not. It is not the clone/setup guide (that is \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/install.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eUse okf-loom from a clone\u003c/a\u003e) nor the search reference (that is \u003ca href=\"/reference/search_modes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eSearch modes\u003c/a\u003e); it is the reasoning that connects the two.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe runtime path is the checked-in \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom\u003c/code\u003e helper. Everything else okf-loom does — validating, searching, discovering, rendering, and the live collaborative studio — is built on the Python standard library plus PyYAML when it is available. Without PyYAML, the bundled fallback accepts the YAML subset used by OKF docs/config and fails closed on unsupported advanced YAML such as anchors, aliases, tags, directives, merge keys, and multi-document streams.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"why-it-matters\"\u003eWhy it matters\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA dependency-light baseline earns three properties that a richer dependency set would erode.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"embeddability\"\u003eEmbeddability\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe same checkout runtime runs in a CI runner, a meta-agent's subprocess, an air-gapped notebook, and a long-running viewer inside another agent harness. None of those environments is guaranteed to have a C toolchain, network access, or an environment that can resolve a deep dependency tree. A toolkit whose normal source-checkout path does not require a primary install step fits everywhere; a toolkit that pulls in a markdown library, a search engine, a web framework, and an embedding backend fits only where those resolve cleanly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is also what makes okf-loom \u003cstrong\u003eharness-agnostic\u003c/strong\u003e. The three integration shapes — shell out to the CLI, import the library, or run a long-lived server in a daemon thread (see \u003ca href=\"/how-to/embed_in_harness.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eEmbed the viewer in an agent harness\u003c/a\u003e) — all work without the host having to accommodate okf-loom's dependencies. The embedding contract is one checkout plus \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"source-checkout-usability\"\u003eSource-checkout usability\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA dependency-light checkout is fast, deterministic, and reproducible. There is no dependency conflict to debug, no transitive package to pin, and no surprise platform wheel that fails to build. For a tool whose primary audience includes agents cloning it into a sandbox and loading the local skill resources, that friction matters: every failed setup is a failed task.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"audit-surface\"\u003eAudit surface\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEvery hard dependency is code the user is trusting. A smaller dependency tree is a smaller attack surface and a smaller review surface. For a tool whose job includes \u003cem\u003econsuming bundles produced by arbitrary third parties\u003c/em\u003e (see \u003ca href=\"what_is_okf.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhat OKF is for\u003c/a\u003e), keeping the trust boundary narrow is a deliberate stance: okf-loom reads untrusted markdown and YAML, using PyYAML when present or the conservative fallback otherwise, plus its own containment guards (\u003ccode\u003epaths.path_within_bundle\u003c/code\u003e) rather than a stack of third-party libraries each of which would need its own audit.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe constraint is stated as a hard rule in the agent brief (\u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e): do not reintroduce package publishing or primary dependency installs as the normal runtime path. New features must keep \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom\u003c/code\u003e usable from a checkout.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-the-constraint-costs\"\u003eWhat the constraint costs\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eDependency-light design is not free. Three costs are worth naming honestly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"no-rich-markdown-library\"\u003eNo rich markdown library\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom renders markdown with its own small stdlib renderer (\u003ccode\u003eviewer/markdown.py\u003c/code\u003e) rather than a battle-tested library like \u003ccode\u003emarkdown\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emistune\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003emarked\u003c/code\u003e. That renderer handles the common cases — headings, tables, fenced code, links in both forms, wikilinks — but it is not a full CommonMark implementation, and edge cases that a mature library would handle for free have to be handled by hand.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"no-native-search-index\"\u003eNo native search index\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThere is no SQLite FTS table, no LanceDB store, no Pagefind shard. The search corpus lives in memory and is scanned per query, which is fine up to roughly ten thousand concepts in a single process and degrades gracefully beyond that (see \u003ca href=\"/reference/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/architecture.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e § \"Performance characteristics\"). A user with a much larger corpus is expected to swap in a custom \u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e — the seam exists by design.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"no-local-embedding-backend\"\u003eNo local embedding backend\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe most consequential cost: there is no \u003ccode\u003esentence-transformers\u003c/code\u003e, no local vector store, no on-device embedding model. A dense/vector search backend would normally be the way to get true semantic retrieval, and okf-loom ships without one.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"how-okf-loom-works-around-each-cost\"\u003eHow okf-loom works around each cost\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach cost is met with a workaround that preserves the constraint.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"a-stdlib-markdown-renderer-progressively-enhanced\"\u003eA stdlib markdown renderer, progressively enhanced\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe stdlib renderer is the source of truth for the rendered view and the \u003ccode\u003e/__preview\u003c/code\u003e endpoint, which keeps a single canonical renderer (spec §5, decision D2) rather than a second client-side engine. Rich content — mermaid diagrams, syntax highlighting (highlight.js), and KaTeX math — is added by \u003cstrong\u003eprogressive enhancement from a CDN\u003c/strong\u003e: the scripts load on demand only when a page contains an element of that kind, degrade gracefully to the raw source if the CDN is unreachable, and add zero overhead on pages that do not use them. The same renderers also run in the graph detail panel and the single-file export (pinned CDN versions; highlight.js via jsDelivr's \u003ccode\u003e+esm\u003c/code\u003e bundle).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is a deliberate trade: the canonical render path stays dependency-free and predictable, and the \u003cem\u003eoptional richness\u003c/em\u003e is layered on at the browser where a CDN miss is non-fatal. The page is always readable; the enhancement is a bonus, never a requirement.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"lexical-search-in-pure-python\"\u003eLexical search in pure Python\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003eLexicalBackend\u003c/code\u003e is a field-weighted BM25 over title (5x) \u0026gt; headings (3x) \u0026gt; description (2x) \u0026gt; body (1x) \u0026gt; tags (1x), implemented in pure Python with no dependencies. It satisfies the common case — \"search by term\" — without an index file, a build step, or a running process. See \u003ca href=\"/reference/search_modes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003esearch_modes.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"semanticlite-a-zero-dependency-fuzzy-semantic-layer\"\u003eSemanticLite: a zero-dependency fuzzy-semantic layer\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe most interesting workaround is \u003ccode\u003eSemanticLiteBackend\u003c/code\u003e. True semantic search normally means embeddings; okf-loom ships a \u003cstrong\u003efuzzy-semantic\u003c/strong\u003e layer that needs none. It builds a per-concept profile (title ×3, description ×2, type, headings, tags, entity labels and aliases) and scores similarity as:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode\u003escore = α · cosine(tokens)  +  (1 − α) · cosine(char-trigrams),   α = 0.6\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe trigram half is what makes it robust to typos and morphology — \u003ccode\u003eorders\u003c/code\u003e scores close to \u003ccode\u003eorder\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecustomer\u003c/code\u003e close to \u003ccode\u003ecustomers\u003c/code\u003e. It is not a dense embedding, and it does not pretend to be; it is a cheap fuzzy-semantic layer that helps the agent find candidates, and it costs zero dependencies. The \u003ccode\u003eHybridBackend\u003c/code\u003e fuses lexical and SemanticLite by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), again dependency-free.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"the-agent-is-the-true-semantic-engine\"\u003eThe agent is the true semantic engine\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe deepest workaround is structural rather than algorithmic. okf-loom assumes that \u003cem\u003ethe agent itself\u003c/em\u003e — an LLM running in opencode / Claude Code / Codex / a custom harness — is the best true-semantic engine available. The agent reads the bundle, reasons about it, and writes back; a local embedding backend would be redundant next to a model that already understands the content.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis is the key insight from \u003ca href=\"/explanation/research.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/explanation/research.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e: a local dense-embedding backend was prototyped and then \u003cstrong\u003eremoved\u003c/strong\u003e, because the agent is itself the semantic engine. SemanticLite stays as a cheap candidate-finder; the heavy semantic work happens in the agent, not in okf-loom.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is also why the \u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e Protocol exists: a user who genuinely needs a local embedding backend (an air-gapped deployment with no agent, a very large corpus, a specific retrieval task) can implement one behind the same \u003ccode\u003e--mode\u003c/code\u003e dispatch and register it. The constraint is on the \u003cem\u003edefault\u003c/em\u003e, not on the \u003cem\u003ecapability\u003c/em\u003e. See \u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003ecapabilities.md\u003c/a\u003e for the extension model.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"where-the-one-optional-extra-fits\"\u003eWhere the one optional extra fits\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThere is exactly one optional extra, and it is narrowly scoped: explicit browser-proof dependencies, which install Playwright. They exist for a single purpose — capturing browser-end-to-end proof that the live wiki actually renders: the graph mounts, concept pages load, search returns results, and backlinks show. Without it, those tests skip cleanly so the default suite stays dependency-light.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003epython -m pip install playwright\nplaywright install chromium\npytest tests/test_viewer_browser.py        # e2e; skips cleanly without the extra\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is the model okf-loom uses for anything that genuinely cannot be done with the standard library: it goes behind an \u003cem\u003eoptional extra\u003c/em\u003e that is strictly additive, degrades cleanly when absent, and never enters the default install or the default test run. Browser proof is the only thing that earns that treatment today; if a future feature needed a native search index or a rich markdown library, the same pattern (optional extra, clean skip, no default impact) is how it would land.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"why-the-constraint-is-a-feature-not-a-limitation\"\u003eWhy the constraint is a feature, not a limitation\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIt is tempting to read \"dependency-light\" as \"missing features.\" okf-loom's stance is the opposite: the constraint is what makes the features it \u003cem\u003edoes\u003c/em\u003e have portable, trustworthy, and combinable. A richer dependency set would buy a more polished markdown render and a native search index at the cost of an install that fails in exactly the environments — air-gapped, sandboxed, agent-spawned — where okf-loom is most useful.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe workaround for each cost is also a feature in disguise. The stdlib markdown renderer plus CDN progressive enhancement gives a single canonical render path. SemanticLite plus the agent gives a semantic search story that needs no model download. The \u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e Protocol gives an escape hatch for users who need more, without imposing it on users who do not. In every case the constraint forced a design that is simpler to reason about than the dependency-rich alternative would have been — and that is the real reason okf-loom keeps it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/tutorials/install.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eUse okf-loom from a clone\u003c/a\u003e — the clone-first setup and your first \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/search_modes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eSearch modes\u003c/a\u003e — the six modes, their backends, and the \u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e Protocol.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCapability registry\u003c/a\u003e — how optional extensions land without a spec change or a new dependency.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/embed_in_harness.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eEmbed the viewer in an agent harness\u003c/a\u003e — the three integration shapes the constraint enables.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/research.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/explanation/research.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e — the comparative survey, including the note on why the local embedding backend was prototyped and then removed.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/architecture.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e — the module map, including the performance characteristics of the dependency-free search path.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/explanation/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eExplanation\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/archive_threads": "\u003ch2 id=\"archive-and-resolve-comment-threads\"\u003eArchive and resolve comment threads\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide walks you through clearing the studio's comment panel by archiving resolved threads, and bringing them back when work resumes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already know how to drive the comment loop end to end. If you do not, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/a\u003e covers the \u003ccode\u003ewait\u003c/code\u003e, claim, and resolve flow.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"the-archive-model-read-this-first\"\u003eThe archive model (read this first)\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eArchive is a \u003cstrong\u003eseparate boolean field\u003c/strong\u003e next to \u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eField\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eValues\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eMeaning\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eopen\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003edismissed\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe lifecycle of the work.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earchived\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhether the panel soft-hides the thread.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eArchiving a resolved comment keeps it resolved. Unarchiving restores the prior visibility without flipping \u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e. Compatibility records with \u003ccode\u003estate == \"archived\"\u003c/code\u003e are normalised on read to \u003ccode\u003earchived=true, state=\"open\"\u003c/code\u003e (best-effort migration, automatic).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-resolve-every-comment-in-the-thread\"\u003eStep 1: Resolve every comment in the thread\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eArchive is server-enforced gated on the \u003cstrong\u003ewhole\u003c/strong\u003e thread being resolved. The agent resolves its comments via the CLI; the user resolves theirs via the panel.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-resolve path/to/bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n  --activity 01JABED5K7,01JABED5K8 \\\n  --reply \"Done — added depends_on + Order entity\" \\\n  --summary \"done: link + entity added\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf the thread has replies, every reply must also be resolved before the root can be archived.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-archive-the-thread-from-the-panel\"\u003eStep 2: Archive the thread from the panel\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn the studio's right-hand \u003cstrong\u003eComments\u003c/strong\u003e panel, open the thread you want to clear.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOn the root card, click \u003cstrong\u003eArchive thread\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe button is only enabled when every comment in the thread is \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e. Before that, it is disabled with a tooltip explaining the gate.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe thread disappears from the default panel view; its lifecycle state is untouched.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eToggle \u003cstrong\u003eShow archived\u003c/strong\u003e in the panel toolbar to see archived threads again.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-archive-the-thread-via-the-http-endpoint\"\u003eStep 3: Archive the thread via the HTTP endpoint\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf you are driving the studio from a script, POST to \u003ccode\u003e/__comment-update\u003c/code\u003e with the root id and the archive flag.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003eTOKEN=$(scripts/okf-loom token path/to/bundle)\n\ncurl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/__comment-update \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -H \"X-OKF-Token: $TOKEN\" \\\n  -d '{\"id\": \"01JABED9K0\", \"archived\": true}'\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA successful response returns the updated comment object with \u003ccode\u003earchived: true\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-handle-the-archive-guards\"\u003eStep 4: Handle the archive guards\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe server enforces three rules.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eRule\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eStatus\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eBody\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eArchive is root-only. Replies cannot be archived independently.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e400\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{\"error\": \"archive is only available on the top-level comment of a thread\"}\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eArchive requires every comment in the thread to be \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e409\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{\"error\": \"...\", \"unresolved_ids\": [\"01J...\", \"01J...\"]}\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eDismiss is rejected on a \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e comment (agent is mid-flight).\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e409\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{\"error\": \"cannot dismiss a claimed comment\"}\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen you get a \u003ccode\u003e409\u003c/code\u003e with \u003ccode\u003eunresolved_ids\u003c/code\u003e, resolve each listed comment and retry.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-unarchive-a-thread\"\u003eStep 5: Unarchive a thread\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUnarchive from the panel by clicking \u003cstrong\u003eUnarchive\u003c/strong\u003e on the archived root card (visible with \u003cstrong\u003eShow archived\u003c/strong\u003e on).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOr POST the same endpoint with \u003ccode\u003earchived: false\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003ecurl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/__comment-update \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -H \"X-OKF-Token: $TOKEN\" \\\n  -d '{\"id\": \"01JABED9K0\", \"archived\": false}'\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUnarchiving restores the prior visibility without changing \u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e. A resolved thread comes back resolved; an open thread comes back open.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-let-a-reply-auto-unarchive\"\u003eStep 6: Let a reply auto-unarchive\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReplying to an archived thread \u003cstrong\u003eauto-unarchives the parent\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is enforced server-side in \u003ccode\u003eStudio.post_comment\u003c/code\u003e: the moment you add to a thread, it reopens for business. Archive is a soft hide, not a closed state.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn the panel, clicking \u003cstrong\u003eReply\u003c/strong\u003e on an archived thread and submitting a reply both unarchives the thread and posts the reply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-list-comments-with-the-archive-flag\"\u003eStep 7: List comments with the archive flag\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecomment-list\u003c/code\u003e shows every directive and each row carries \u003ccode\u003earchived: bool\u003c/code\u003e independent of state.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-list path/to/bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFilter by state with \u003ccode\u003e--state open|claimed|resolved|dismissed\u003c/code\u003e; the archive flag is an independent column you read alongside it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"end-state\"\u003eEnd state\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou can now keep the comment panel focused on open work by archiving resolved threads, while keeping them one click away when work resumes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/a\u003e — the full claim → write → resolve loop.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eComment lifecycle and archive rules\u003c/a\u003e — the canonical state + archive reference.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHTTP server routes\u003c/a\u003e — every studio endpoint.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — \u003ccode\u003ecomment-list\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-claim\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-resolve\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etoken\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhy the live studio exists\u003c/a\u003e — why comments are the user's directing surface.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/how-to/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/author_with_verbs": "\u003ch2 id=\"author-concepts-via-cli-verbs\"\u003eAuthor concepts via CLI verbs\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide shows you how to edit concept files from the command line without hand-writing a JSON update plan.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already know what a concept looks like and have run validation at least once. If you do not, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e walks you through the basics.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-create-or-update-a-concept\"\u003eStep 1: Create or update a concept\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003ewrite-concept\u003c/code\u003e creates a concept if it is missing, or merges frontmatter into an existing one.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom write-concept --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --type \"Table\" \\\n  --title \"Orders\" \\\n  --description \"One row per completed order.\" \\\n  --tag analytics --tag checkout \\\n  --body-file ./orders_body.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFlags worth knowing:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eFlag\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eEffect\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--type\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRequired (matches SPEC §9: \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e is the only hard-required key).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--title\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--description\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--resource\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--timestamp\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSet the corresponding frontmatter key.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--tag\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRepeatable; appends to \u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--body\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--body-file\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSet the body. Replacing a non-empty body requires \u003ccode\u003e--force\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--force\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAllow overwriting an existing body.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUpdating an existing concept only touches the keys you pass; unknown keys are preserved.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-set-a-single-frontmatter-key\"\u003eStep 2: Set a single frontmatter key\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a one-key edit, \u003ccode\u003eset-frontmatter\u003c/code\u003e is thinner than \u003ccode\u003ewrite-concept\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom set-frontmatter --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --key owner --value team-checkout\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor lists or objects, pass \u003ccode\u003e--json-value\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom set-frontmatter --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --key tags --value '[\"analytics\",\"checkout\"]' --json-value\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--dry-run\u003c/code\u003e previews the change without writing.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-add-a-link-and-optionally-a-typed-relation\"\u003eStep 3: Add a link (and optionally a typed relation)\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003elink-add\u003c/code\u003e appends a markdown link in the absolute \u003ccode\u003e/tables/customers.md\u003c/code\u003e form recommended by SPEC §5.1.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# Plain body link\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target tables/customers \\\n  --label \"customers\" --section \"Schema\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAdd \u003ccode\u003e--relation TYPE\u003c/code\u003e to also append a typed relation; \u003ccode\u003e--evidence\u003c/code\u003e becomes the relation \u003ccode\u003edetail\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target services/checkout \\\n  --relation written_by --evidence \"POST handler in checkout service\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBy default the verb refuses to write a link whose target does not exist. Pass \u003ccode\u003e--allow-forward-reference\u003c/code\u003e to write a deliberate forward reference (SPEC §5.3 tolerates it; see \u003ca href=\"/reference/links.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eLink forms\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-add-an-entity\"\u003eStep 4: Add an entity\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eentity-add\u003c/code\u003e appends an entity object to the concept's \u003ccode\u003eentities:\u003c/code\u003e frontmatter list.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom entity-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --label \"Order\" --kind business_entity \\\n  --entity-id entity/order \\\n  --alias \"Sales Order\" --alias \"Order Record\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIt is idempotent on \u003ccode\u003e(label, kind)\u003c/code\u003e, so re-running the same command does not duplicate the entity. Aliases are repeatable; they also feed entity and semantic search once present.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-group-writes-for-one-click-undo\"\u003eStep 5: Group writes for one-click undo\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePass the same \u003ccode\u003e--group-id\u003c/code\u003e to every verb in a logical pass and the studio collapses them into one undoable change.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target tables/customers \\\n  --relation depends_on --group-id PASS1\n\nscripts/okf-loom entity-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders --label \"Order\" --kind Table \\\n  --group-id PASS1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn the change list, \u003ccode\u003ePASS1\u003c/code\u003e appears as a single entry with a one-click group-undo button. Without a live studio session the flag is accepted but has no visible effect — the writes still land atomically.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-attribute-writes-to-an-actor\"\u003eStep 6: Attribute writes to an actor\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--actor NAME\u003c/code\u003e sets the attribution shown in the change list (default \u003ccode\u003eagent\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target tables/customers \\\n  --group-id PASS1 --actor curator-alice\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUse this when a human or a named workflow is doing the curation, so the change list reads as a real activity log.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-run-a-worked-multi-verb-curation-pass\"\u003eStep 7: Run a worked multi-verb curation pass\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis sequence is the typical \"wire up one concept end to end\" pass you will run dozens of times.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003eBUNDLE=path/to/bundle\nGROUP=curate-orders-$(date +%s)\n\n# 1. Make sure the concept exists with rich metadata\nscripts/okf-loom write-concept --bundle \"$BUNDLE\" \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --type \"Table\" \\\n  --title \"Orders\" \\\n  --description \"One row per completed customer order.\" \\\n  --tag analytics --tag checkout \\\n  --group-id \"$GROUP\" --actor curator-alice\n\n# 2. Backfill an owner key\nscripts/okf-loom set-frontmatter --bundle \"$BUNDLE\" \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --key owner --value team-checkout \\\n  --group-id \"$GROUP\" --actor curator-alice\n\n# 3. Link to the customer table + add a typed relation\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle \"$BUNDLE\" \\\n  --source tables/orders --target tables/customers \\\n  --label \"customers\" --section \"Schema\" \\\n  --relation depends_on --evidence \"FK customer_id\" \\\n  --group-id \"$GROUP\" --actor curator-alice\n\n# 4. Register the Order entity with aliases\nscripts/okf-loom entity-add --bundle \"$BUNDLE\" \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --label \"Order\" --kind business_entity \\\n  --entity-id entity/order \\\n  --alias \"Sales Order\" --alias \"Order Record\" \\\n  --group-id \"$GROUP\" --actor curator-alice\n\n# 5. Re-validate\nscripts/okf-loom validate \"$BUNDLE\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEvery write in that pass shares \u003ccode\u003e\"$GROUP\"\u003c/code\u003e, so the whole curation is a single undo in the studio.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"when-to-use-the-verbs-vs-a-plan\"\u003eWhen to use the verbs vs a plan\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUse the verbs for one-off edits while authoring: create a concept, fix a frontmatter typo, wire up a single link or entity.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUse \u003ccode\u003eplan\u003c/code\u003e plus \u003ccode\u003eupdate\u003c/code\u003e for batch curation produced by \u003ccode\u003ediscover\u003c/code\u003e — many ops on many concepts, reviewable as one JSON document.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBoth paths share the same \u003ccode\u003eparse_document\u003c/code\u003e → modify → \u003ccode\u003eserialize_document\u003c/code\u003e pipeline, so file-level behaviour is identical.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/how-to/discover_and_fix_gaps.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFind and fix bundle gaps\u003c/a\u003e for the batch path.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/discover_and_fix_gaps.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFind and fix bundle gaps\u003c/a\u003e — turn discovery suggestions into a reviewable plan.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/a\u003e — the same verbs inside the comment-driven studio loop.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every flag on every verb.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/frontmatter.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFrontmatter contract\u003c/a\u003e — required vs recommended keys.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhy the live studio exists\u003c/a\u003e — why mutators attribute and undo.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/how-to/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/build_static_site": "\u003ch2 id=\"build-a-static-site\"\u003eBuild a static site\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide takes a bundle on disk and ships it as a static site you can host anywhere — GitHub Pages, Netlify, an intranet, or a \u003ccode\u003efile://\u003c/code\u003e URL.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already have a bundle that passes validation. If you do not, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e gets you there.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-choose-a-build-target\"\u003eStep 1: Choose a build target\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe build command ships three targets, each tuned for a different shipping context.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eTarget\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhen to use\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003espa\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eQuartz-style default for a published reading experience. Client-side rendering; richest interactions.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estatic\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eServer-rendered, JS-optional, printable, SEO- and airgapped-friendly.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esingle-file\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne self-contained HTML with everything embedded. Email it, attach to a ticket, open from \u003ccode\u003efile://\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePick \u003ccode\u003estatic\u003c/code\u003e when you want a hostable site that still works without JavaScript. Pick \u003ccode\u003espa\u003c/code\u003e when you want the smoothest reading experience and do not mind requiring JS. Pick \u003ccode\u003esingle-file\u003c/code\u003e when the artifact has to travel as one file.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-build-the-site\"\u003eStep 2: Build the site\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun the checkout-local build command with the target and an output directory.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom build path/to/bundle --target static --out dist/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003edist/\u003c/code\u003e directory now contains the full site: rendered HTML pages, a copy of the graph data, and the viewer assets.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe other targets take the same flags:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom build path/to/bundle --target spa --out dist/\nscripts/okf-loom build path/to/bundle --target single-file --out dist/viz.html\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-preview-the-build-locally\"\u003eStep 3: Preview the build locally\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAny static file server works.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003epython3 -m http.server --directory dist 8000\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOpen \u003ccode\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8000/\u003c/code\u003e and click around to confirm the render before you ship.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a quick single-file preview, \u003ccode\u003erender\u003c/code\u003e writes one self-contained \u003ccode\u003eviz.html\u003c/code\u003e without invoking the full build pipeline.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom render path/to/bundle --out viz.html\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003erender\u003c/code\u003e is the right tool when you want one portable artifact and do not need the multi-file site.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-handle-active-code-overrides-and-plugins\"\u003eStep 4: Handle active code (overrides and plugins)\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf the bundle ships viewer overrides or plugins that run JavaScript — custom templates, a \u003ccode\u003eViewerPlugin\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003eviewer.allow_active_code: true\u003c/code\u003e in \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e — the build refuses to execute them unless you give operator consent.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom build path/to/bundle --target spa --out dist/ --allow-active-code\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe two-layer gate is intentional: the bundle declares it wants active code, and the operator explicitly allows it at build time. Without consent, the build still succeeds but the overrides and plugins are inert.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSet \u003ccode\u003eOKF_LOOM_ALLOW_ACTIVE_CODE=1\u003c/code\u003e in the build environment to consent non-interactively, for example in a CI job.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-ship-the-site\"\u003eStep 5: Ship the site\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003edist/\u003c/code\u003e directory is fully self-contained; copy it anywhere.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor GitHub Pages, drop it into the \u003ccode\u003egh-pages\u003c/code\u003e branch or point Pages at the build output of your CI workflow. For Netlify or Vercel, point the deploy command at \u003ccode\u003edist/\u003c/code\u003e. For an airgapped intranet, copy the directory onto the static file server of your choice.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBecause the \u003ccode\u003estatic\u003c/code\u003e target is JS-optional, the site renders legibly even in a restricted browser.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-embed-the-site-inside-another-site\"\u003eStep 6: Embed the site inside another site\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003esingle-file\u003c/code\u003e target is the easiest embed: drop the \u003ccode\u003eviz.html\u003c/code\u003e into an \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;iframe\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e on your existing docs site.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-html\"\u003e\u0026lt;iframe src=\"/okf/viz.html\" width=\"100%\" height=\"800\" frameborder=\"0\"\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/iframe\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a deeper integration — your own chrome around the viewer, a custom build step, or running the live server inside another process — see \u003ca href=\"/how-to/embed_in_harness.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eEmbed the viewer in an agent harness\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-automate-the-build-in-ci\"\u003eStep 7: Automate the build in CI\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePair the build with the validate gate so a broken bundle never ships.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e# .github/workflows/okf-build.yml\nname: OKF build\non:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n    paths: ['docs-bundle/**']\njobs:\n  build:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n        with:\n          python-version: '3.11'\n      - run: scripts/okf-loom validate docs-bundle --strict --profile producer\n      - run: scripts/okf-loom build docs-bundle --target static --out dist/\n      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3\n        with:\n          path: dist/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/how-to/validate_in_ci.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/a\u003e for the full validate workflow.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"end-state\"\u003eEnd state\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have a repeatable build that:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eTurns a bundle into a hostable site in one command.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePicks the right target for the shipping context.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eHonours the active-code gate when overrides or plugins are present.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/validate_in_ci.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/a\u003e — gate the build behind strict validation.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/embed_in_harness.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eEmbed the viewer in an agent harness\u003c/a\u003e — deeper integration shapes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every flag on \u003ccode\u003ebuild\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003erender\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHTTP server routes\u003c/a\u003e — the routes the live server and SPA share.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eokf-loom architecture\u003c/a\u003e — why one content model renders to many targets.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/how-to/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/discover_and_fix_gaps": "\u003ch2 id=\"find-and-fix-bundle-gaps\"\u003eFind and fix bundle gaps\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide walks you through finding the curation gaps a strict validate cannot see — unlinked mentions, missing indexes, thin descriptions — and turning them into edits on disk.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already know how to author a concept and run validation. If you do not, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e covers the basics.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-run-discovery-over-the-whole-bundle\"\u003eStep 1: Run discovery over the whole bundle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003ediscover\u003c/code\u003e emits a structured report with one row per suggestion.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom discover path/to/bundle --out suggestions.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e--out\u003c/code\u003e file is a JSON list you can read in an editor or pipe into a downstream consumer.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWithout \u003ccode\u003e--out\u003c/code\u003e, the report prints to stdout in human-readable form.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-read-the-rule-taxonomy\"\u003eStep 2: Read the rule taxonomy\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach suggestion carries a \u003ccode\u003erule\u003c/code\u003e field drawn from a fixed taxonomy.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eRule\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eFires when…\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eunlinked_mentions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept body mentions another concept's title but does not link to it.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emissing_indexes\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA directory contains concepts but has no \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emissing_descriptions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept's \u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e is empty or missing.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ebroken_links\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAn internal link target does not exist (re-surfaces the validator's findings).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emissing_relations_hint\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA \u003ccode\u003e# Schema\u003c/code\u003e column says \"FK to\" or \"references\" but has no outgoing link.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eorphan_concepts\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept has no incoming and no outgoing internal edges.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe severity on each row tells you whether to fix-now or to triage.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-triage-the-suggestions\"\u003eStep 3: Triage the suggestions\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRead the report and decide per row whether to apply, defer, or dismiss.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-json\"\u003e[\n  {\n    \"rule\": \"unlinked_mentions\",\n    \"severity\": \"warning\",\n    \"concept\": \"tables/orders\",\n    \"target\": \"tables/customers\",\n    \"message\": \"mentions 'customers' without a link\",\n    \"action\": \"add a link from tables/orders to tables/customers\"\n  }\n]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA useful triage order is: fix \u003ccode\u003ebroken_links\u003c/code\u003e first, then \u003ccode\u003emissing_descriptions\u003c/code\u003e, then \u003ccode\u003eunlinked_mentions\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003emissing_relations_hint\u003c/code\u003e, and treat \u003ccode\u003eorphan_concepts\u003c/code\u003e as a signal to merge or cross-link.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003emissing_indexes\u003c/code\u003e is mechanical — it always makes sense to add an \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e when a directory has more than a few concepts.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-apply-fixes-directly-via-the-mutators\"\u003eStep 4: Apply fixes directly via the mutators\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a handful of suggestions, the authoring verbs are the fastest path.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# unlinked_mentions: add a body link from orders to customers\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target tables/customers \\\n  --label \"customers\" --section \"Schema\"\n\n# missing_relations_hint: add a typed relation too\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target tables/customers \\\n  --relation depends_on --evidence \"FK customer_id\"\n\n# missing_descriptions: backfill a one-liner\nscripts/okf-loom set-frontmatter --bundle path/to/bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders \\\n  --key description --value \"One row per completed order.\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach verb is idempotent and goes through the same atomic write path as a plan.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen a live studio session is running, the verbs also flow through \u003ccode\u003eStudio.save_concept\u003c/code\u003e, so each edit is attributed, undoable, and pushed live over SSE.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/how-to/author_with_verbs.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor concepts via CLI verbs\u003c/a\u003e for the full verb catalogue.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-apply-many-fixes-via-an-action-plan\"\u003eStep 5: Apply many fixes via an action plan\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor batch curation, turn the suggestions into an executable plan and apply it in one reviewable pass.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# Build a plan from discovery + index staleness + relation mirroring\nscripts/okf-loom plan path/to/bundle --out plan.json\n\n# Preview the changes without writing\nscripts/okf-loom update path/to/bundle --plan plan.json --dry-run\n\n# Apply\nscripts/okf-loom update path/to/bundle --plan plan.json\n\n# Re-check\nscripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eplan\u003c/code\u003e adds two sources beyond raw discovery: stale \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e regeneration and typed-relation mirroring (writing a body markdown link for each \u003ccode\u003erelations:\u003c/code\u003e entry that lacks one).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe plan is idempotent — re-applying it reports \u003ccode\u003eapplied:0, skipped:N\u003c/code\u003e with reasons like \u003ccode\u003ealready_linked\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003esection_exists\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-scope-discovery-to-a-subgraph\"\u003eStep 6: Scope discovery to a subgraph\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen you only touched one concept, run a scoped pass instead of rescanning the whole bundle.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# Only the named concept\nscripts/okf-loom discover path/to/bundle --scope tables/orders --out scoped.json\n\n# The named concept plus its 1-hop neighbours (in + out edges)\nscripts/okf-loom discover path/to/bundle --scope tables/orders --neighbors --out scoped.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eplan\u003c/code\u003e accepts the same \u003ccode\u003e--scope\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e--neighbors\u003c/code\u003e flags, so a per-change enrichment pass is fast.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe watch loop in the live studio uses exactly this scoped shape to enrich on every save.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-run-mechanical-repairs-in-one-go\"\u003eStep 7: Run mechanical repairs in one go\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSome suggestions — stale indexes and missing relation mirrors — are always safe to apply without judgement.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom repair path/to/bundle --apply\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--apply --indexes\u003c/code\u003e regenerates only \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e files; \u003ccode\u003e--apply --mirror-relations\u003c/code\u003e only writes the body links for typed relations.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRelation mirroring runs before index regen so the regenerated indexes reflect the new links.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"end-state\"\u003eEnd state\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have a workflow that:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eSurfaces every curation gap in a structured report.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eApplies fixes either one-by-one through the verbs or in batch through a plan.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRe-runs cheaply on every change via scoped discovery.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/author_with_verbs.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor concepts via CLI verbs\u003c/a\u003e — the per-suggestion verbs used above.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/validate_in_ci.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/a\u003e — strict conformance as a CI gate.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every flag on \u003ccode\u003ediscover\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eplan\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupdate\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erepair\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCapability registry\u003c/a\u003e — what \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.typed_relations\u003c/code\u003e and friends unlock.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhy the live studio exists\u003c/a\u003e — how scoped discovery powers proactive enrichment.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/how-to/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/embed_in_harness": "\u003ch2 id=\"embed-the-viewer-in-an-agent-harness\"\u003eEmbed the viewer in an agent harness\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide shows the three integration shapes okf-loom supports and when to reach for each.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already have a bundle and a harness that wants to read or enrich it. If you do not have a bundle yet, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e gets you started.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-pick-an-integration-shape\"\u003eStep 1: Pick an integration shape\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eShape\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhen to use\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCLI shell-out\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYour harness already runs shell commands and parses JSON. Simplest; no Python import.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePython library\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYour harness is Python and wants in-process objects.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eLong-running server\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYour harness wants a live URL (browser, scraper, or a long-running studio).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAll three read the same bundle directory and produce the same answers; pick by what your harness already speaks.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-embed-as-a-cli-shell-out\"\u003eStep 2: Embed as a CLI shell-out\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe simplest shape: shell out to the checkout-local CLI and parse the JSON.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --format json\nscripts/okf-loom discover path/to/bundle --out /tmp/plan.json\nscripts/okf-loom update  path/to/bundle --plan /tmp/plan.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUse command-specific JSON/report flags where the command exposes them; a thin wrapper that captures stdout and \u003ccode\u003ejson.loads\u003c/code\u003e it is enough for those report commands.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is the shape most agent harnesses start with — it needs no Python dependency in the harness itself.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor the harness-specific recipes (opencode, Claude Code, Codex, LangGraph, custom), see \u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/embedding_guide.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-embed-as-a-python-library\"\u003eStep 3: Embed as a Python library\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen the harness is Python, import okf-loom directly and skip the process boundary.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003efrom okf_loom import Bundle\nfrom okf_loom.validate import validate_bundle\nfrom okf_loom.discover import discover_suggestions\nfrom okf_loom.update import load_plan, apply_plan\n\nbundle = Bundle.load(\"/path/to/bundle\")\n\n# Validate\nreport = validate_bundle(bundle)\nprint(\"Conformant:\", report.ok, \"Warnings:\", len(report.warnings))\n\n# Discover gaps\nsuggestions = discover_suggestions(bundle, rules=[\"unlinked_mentions\"])\n\n# Apply a plan (idempotent)\nplan = load_plan(\"/tmp/plan.json\")\napply_plan(bundle, plan)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe library surface is the same pipeline the CLI uses, so behaviour is identical between the two shapes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eKeep one \u003ccode\u003eBundle\u003c/code\u003e instance per harness; call \u003ccode\u003ebundle.invalidate()\u003c/code\u003e to evict the search caches when you reload the underlying files.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-embed-as-a-long-running-server\"\u003eStep 4: Embed as a long-running server\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a live URL — a browser pointed at the viewer, a scraper, or a long-running studio — embed the HTTP server in a daemon thread inside the harness.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003eimport threading\nfrom http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer\nfrom okf_loom import Bundle\nfrom okf_loom.server import OKFWikiHandler\n\nbundle = Bundle.load(\"/path/to/bundle\")\nhttpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((\"127.0.0.1\", 8787), OKFWikiHandler)\nhttpd.bundle = bundle\nthreading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe harness can now point a browser at \u003ccode\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8787/\u003c/code\u003e, or fetch the JSON data routes directly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSwap the bundle at runtime by reassigning \u003ccode\u003ehttpd.bundle\u003c/code\u003e; the next request picks it up.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-point-a-browser-at-the-live-studio\"\u003eStep 5: Point a browser at the live studio\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen you want the full collaborative studio — comments, presence, live SSE updates — run \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e instead of the bare server.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom serve path/to/bundle --no-open\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe harness hands the user \u003ccode\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8787/\u003c/code\u003e and then drives the comment loop via the CLI mutators.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/a\u003e for the canonical wait → claim → write → resolve flow, and \u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/embedding_guide.md\u003c/a\u003e for harness-specific wiring.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-read-the-csrf-token-when-you-must-post-directly\"\u003eStep 6: Read the CSRF token when you must POST directly\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe CLI mutators attach the per-session CSRF token for you. If you POST to \u003ccode\u003e/__apply\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/__undo\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/__presence\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003e/__comment\u003c/code\u003e over HTTP yourself, read the token the studio wrote on boot.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom serve path/to/bundle --no-open \u0026amp;\nTOKEN=$(scripts/okf-loom token path/to/bundle)\n\ncurl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/__presence \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -H \"X-OKF-Token: $TOKEN\" \\\n  -d '{\"state\": \"watching\", \"actor\": \"agent\"}'\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe token is per-session, mode \u003ccode\u003e0600\u003c/code\u003e, lives only in \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/.token\u003c/code\u003e, and is readable only by the user that launched \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003etoken\u003c/code\u003e exits non-zero with a clear message if no session exists.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"end-state\"\u003eEnd state\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have okf-loom wired into your harness in the shape that fits it best, and you know where to deepen the integration when you need the live studio or the library API.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eEmbedding guide\u003c/a\u003e — harness-specific recipes for opencode, Claude Code, Codex, LangGraph.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/a\u003e — the comment-driven studio loop.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/build_static_site.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eBuild a static site\u003c/a\u003e — ship a bundle as a hostable site when you do not need a live server.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every command the shell-out shape can call.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHTTP server routes\u003c/a\u003e — every route the server shape exposes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eokf-loom architecture\u003c/a\u003e — why okf-loom is harness-agnostic by design.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/how-to/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/migrate_spec_version": "\u003ch2 id=\"migrate-across-spec-versions\"\u003eMigrate across spec versions\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide walks you through moving a bundle across OKF spec versions safely, with preview, idempotent application, and no hand-editing of files.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already have a bundle and have run validation against it. If you do not, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e covers the basics.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-declare-the-bundles-spec-version\"\u003eStep 1: Declare the bundle's spec version\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe bundle declares its spec version in the \u003cstrong\u003eroot\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e frontmatter, and only there (SPEC §6, §11).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e---\nokf_version: \"0.1\"\nokf_extensions:\n  - okf.cap.typed_relations\n  - okf.cap.entities\ngenerated: true\n---\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eQuote the version string so YAML keeps it as a string rather than parsing it as a float — the same rule that applies to \u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf the declared version differs from okf-loom's \u003ccode\u003eSPEC_VERSION\u003c/code\u003e, the validator emits a warning and okf-loom does best-effort consumption (SPEC §11 mandate).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNon-root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e files MUST NOT carry frontmatter (see \u003ca href=\"/reference/frontmatter.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFrontmatter contract\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-preview-pending-migrations\"\u003eStep 2: Preview pending migrations\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eupgrade --check\u003c/code\u003e prints the migrations that would run against the bundle, without writing anything.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom upgrade --check path/to/bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRead the preview before applying. Each migration is an idempotent transformer that reuses the same \u003ccode\u003eparse_document\u003c/code\u003e → modify → \u003ccode\u003eserialize_document\u003c/code\u003e pipeline as the authoring verbs, so frontmatter key order and unknown keys are preserved.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-apply-the-migrations\"\u003eStep 3: Apply the migrations\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eupgrade --apply\u003c/code\u003e runs every pending migration in order.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom upgrade --apply path/to/bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRe-running it is a no-op: migrations are idempotent and skip work they have already done.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-target-a-specific-spec-version\"\u003eStep 4: Target a specific spec version\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePass \u003ccode\u003e--to-spec\u003c/code\u003e to migrate toward a specific spec version rather than the latest okf-loom knows.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom upgrade --check --to-spec \"NEXT_SPEC\" path/to/bundle\nscripts/okf-loom upgrade --apply  --to-spec \"NEXT_SPEC\" path/to/bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eQuote the version string so the shell does not interpret it as a flag.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-re-validate-after-the-migration\"\u003eStep 5: Re-validate after the migration\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun the validator to confirm the bundle still conforms after the migration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --strict --profile producer\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCommit the migration as one change so the diff reads as a clean version bump. If anything looks wrong, \u003ccode\u003egit revert\u003c/code\u003e brings the bundle back to its pre-migration state; the migration itself never destroys hand-curated content.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/how-to/validate_in_ci.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/a\u003e for wiring that re-validation into CI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-know-what-v01-migrations-exist\"\u003eStep 6: Know what v0.1 migrations exist\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eToday, \u003cstrong\u003eno migrations are defined for spec v0.1\u003c/strong\u003e — it is the baseline.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eupgrade --check\u003c/code\u003e on a v0.1 bundle therefore reports nothing to do. The command and flags above are forward-looking: when a future spec version ships migrations, the same workflow applies them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis is by design. okf-loom features such as typed relations, entities, the live studio, and archive tracks are optional capability-gated or config-gated additions; the wire format remains SPEC v0.1, so a v0.1 bundle needs no migration to use them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCapability registry\u003c/a\u003e for how optional features activate without a spec bump.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"end-state\"\u003eEnd state\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have a workflow that:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eDeclares the bundle's spec version in the root index.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePreviews migrations before applying them.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eApplies them idempotently and re-validates after.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"see-also\"\u003eSee also\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/validate_in_ci.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/a\u003e — gate migrations behind strict validation.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCapability registry\u003c/a\u003e — how optional features activate without a spec bump.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every flag on \u003ccode\u003eupgrade\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/frontmatter.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFrontmatter contract\u003c/a\u003e — required vs recommended keys, including \u003ccode\u003eokf_version\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/explanation/zero_dependencies.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDependency-light philosophy\u003c/a\u003e — why the wire format and runtime setup stay minimal.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/how-to/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHow-to guides\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "how-to/validate_in_ci": "\u003ch2 id=\"validate-a-bundle-in-ci\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide turns validation into a CI gate that fails a pull request or merge request the moment a concept breaks conformance or a recommended key goes missing.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou already have a bundle on disk and a cloned okf-loom checkout with a working \u003ccode\u003eokf\u003c/code\u003e command or source-checkout invocation. If you do not, start with \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/install.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eUse okf-loom from a clone\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-pick-a-validation-profile\"\u003eStep 1: Pick a validation profile\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe validator ships three profiles that remap finding severities for different audiences without changing the wire format.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eProfile\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhen to use\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhat it does\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003espec\u003c/code\u003e (default)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eLightweight gate, spec conformance only.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOnly \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e is required; everything else is a warning.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eproducer\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eProducer-side CI that wants rich metadata enforced.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003espec\u003c/code\u003e plus \u003ccode\u003econcept.missing_recommended_keys\u003c/code\u003e promoted to ERROR.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eloose\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eIngesting incomplete docs that lack \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept.missing_type\u003c/code\u003e downgraded to WARNING.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a documentation bundle that you fully own, \u003ccode\u003eproducer\u003c/code\u003e is usually the right choice: it keeps titles, descriptions, and timestamps honest.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a bundle that ingests third-party markdown, \u003ccode\u003eloose\u003c/code\u003e lets the pipeline land before you backfill \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-decide-on-the-broken-link-policy\"\u003eStep 2: Decide on the broken-link policy\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--fail-on-broken-links\u003c/code\u003e is orthogonal to the profile and promotes \u003ccode\u003elink.broken\u003c/code\u003e findings to ERROR.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUse it when you want to block a release on dangling links, and leave it off when you treat forward references as not-yet-written knowledge (see \u003ca href=\"/reference/links.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eLink forms\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-verify-the-exit-codes-locally\"\u003eStep 3: Verify the exit codes locally\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe validator exits \u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e for conformant, \u003ccode\u003e1\u003c/code\u003e for conformance failure, and \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e for strict failure.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --strict --profile producer --fail-on-broken-links\necho \"exit code: $?\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe exit codes you will see:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eCode\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eMeaning\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eConformant; no errors.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eConformance failure (a concept is missing \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e, or frontmatter is unparseable).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eStrict failure (\u003ccode\u003e--strict\u003c/code\u003e was passed and warnings were promoted to errors).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCI only needs to fail on non-zero, so any of \u003ccode\u003e1\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e blocks the pipeline.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-wire-it-into-github-actions\"\u003eStep 4: Wire it into GitHub Actions\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePut the bundle path and the validate command in a workflow under \u003ccode\u003e.github/workflows/\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e# .github/workflows/okf-validate.yml\nname: OKF validate\non:\n  pull_request:\n    paths:\n      - 'docs-bundle/**'\n      - '.github/workflows/okf-validate.yml'\njobs:\n  validate:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5\n        with:\n          python-version: '3.11'\n      - name: Validate bundle\n        run: |\n          scripts/okf-loom validate docs-bundle \\\n
