The work unifies theme state and configuration, fixes confirmed responsive and accessibility defects, strengthens visual reliability, repairs proof tooling, and completes the optional polish identified during the branch review.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"baseline-and-scope\"\u003eBaseline and scope\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eImplementation branch:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003efeature/editorial-workbench-hardening\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eReviewed source range:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003e2066013a87d9a06ee523bac2cc7b00b874d1e353...b7d7cb1465d6d07ef2a22fc82d476974cdffd84f\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePrimary surfaces:\u003c/strong\u003e concept, index, search, graph, studio, static build, and single-file build.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTheme matrix:\u003c/strong\u003e Swiss Light, Swiss Dark, Technical Light, Technical Dark, plus Auto mode, Soft Contrast, and Border On/Muted/Off.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eProduct contract:\u003c/strong\u003e preserve the Editorial Workbench visual system and the runtime/build behavior described by the \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003ecurrent specification\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003elive studio design\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"findings-driving-the-plan\"\u003eFindings driving the plan\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"theme-and-configuration-state\"\u003eTheme and configuration state\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eA configured initial theme is emitted by Python but can be discarded by client boot when no saved preference exists.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAuto mode and theme family do not have one authoritative state model. Wiki does not follow OS changes, graph can freeze Auto after the first change, and Technical plus Auto does not persist across navigation.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eYAML, viewer JSON, runtime allow-lists, and public documentation disagree about valid theme values and legacy migration.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eInvalid viewer JSON configuration silently falls back instead of returning actionable diagnostics.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"responsive-and-accessibility-behavior\"\u003eResponsive and accessibility behavior\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe Appearance popover is clipped within the topbar scroller at widths through 900px.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAppearance radiogroups and Studio tabs do not implement composite-widget keyboard behavior.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe full-screen mobile Studio panel does not take modal focus ownership or make the obscured page inert.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMobile Studio footer actions and graph topbar controls overflow their containers.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eStatus glyphs use foreground colors that do not maintain sufficient contrast in dark themes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"rendering-and-maintainability\"\u003eRendering and maintainability\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eGraph legends cover canvas content in current Map and Bridges captures.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePlatform-dependent rail glyphs render as replacement boxes in the capture environment.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMermaid output does not update after a light/dark Appearance change.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eCapture tooling and README media do not prove Swiss-first, mobile, static, or single-file parity.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eTheme lists, glyphs, migration maps, and graph palette contracts are duplicated without an automated parity check.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePublic docs and handover references are stale.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"quality-risk-classification\"\u003eQuality risk classification\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ctable Legacy values are migrated once through the same canonical resolver.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"implementation-phases\"\u003eImplementation phases\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"phase-1-contract-and-test-scaffolding\"\u003ePhase 1: Contract and test scaffolding\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eEncode the state contract in tests before broad implementation.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAdd parity checks for all theme names, glyphs, migration values, configuration documentation, and renderer contexts.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAdd invalid-input coverage for malformed JSON, non-object JSON, unknown keys, wrong types, unsupported themes/layouts, empty values, and legacy values.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAdd branch/base stress proof for the Studio readiness race and replace the premature readiness signal with a post-boot contract if confirmed.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAcceptance proof:\u003c/strong\u003e focused tests fail on the reviewed implementation and describe the intended state transitions without relying on implementation details.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"phase-2-theme-and-configuration-correctness\"\u003ePhase 2: Theme and configuration correctness\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eIntroduce one shared theme preference/resolution contract usable by wiki, graph, studio, static, and single-file contexts.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePersist family independently from mode; never persist the resolved light/dark value while Auto is selected.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eObserve \u003ccode\u003eprefers-color-scheme\u003c/code\u003e changes on every live surface while Auto is active.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePreserve validated configured defaults when no user preference exists.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMake storage-denied behavior deterministic.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eReject invalid viewer configuration with contextual diagnostics and provide explicit legacy migration guidance.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eReconcile YAML, JSON, generated markup, documentation, and runtime values.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAcceptance proof:\u003c/strong\u003e browser tests cover every family/mode combination, reload/navigation, two OS changes, storage denial, legacy migration, configured defaults, and static/single-file boot.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"phase-3-responsive-and-accessibility-stabilization\"\u003ePhase 3: Responsive and accessibility stabilization\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eRender or position the Appearance popover outside the horizontal controls scroller.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eImplement roving tabindex, arrow keys, Home/End where appropriate, checked/selected state, Escape behavior, and focus restoration for Appearance and Studio tabs.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eGive the mobile Studio panel dialog semantics, focus containment, inert background behavior, and safe close restoration while retaining non-modal desktop behavior.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eContain or wrap Studio footer actions without document-level overflow.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eGive the graph topbar a coherent mobile layout rather than combining wrapped controls with a fixed single-row height.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePreserve native browser/editable behavior and visible focus in every theme/modifier.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAcceptance proof:\u003c/strong\u003e keyboard-only workflows and geometry checks at 320, 390, 768, 900, 901, and 1280 pixels, plus 200% and 400% zoom/reflow.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"phase-4-visual-hardening\"\u003ePhase 4: Visual hardening\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eAdd semantic foreground-on-status tokens for success, warning, and error surfaces.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eReplace font-dependent rail glyphs with deterministic inline SVG or CSS-mask icons and preserve accessible names.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eReserve a collision-free graph legend region or provide a reliably collapsible legend.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMeasure representative prose/search widths, then apply a 65–75ch reading measure with explicit wide-content escape hatches where evidence supports it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMeasure dark-graph, search metadata, focus, disabled, and modifier contrast in all four themes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePrevent Border Off from removing the only state cue.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAcceptance proof:\u003c/strong\u003e computed contrast assertions, zoom/reflow checks, and fresh screenshots for all four themes plus Soft Contrast and Border Off.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"phase-5-distribution-and-capture-parity\"\u003ePhase 5: Distribution and capture parity\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eBrowser-test live, static, and single-file outputs with the same theme-state matrix.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRepair capture scripts to resolve an available browser, accept external output directories, and wait on semantic readiness rather than \u003ccode\u003enetworkidle\u003c/code\u003e or unconditional sleeps.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRefresh README media with explicit route, theme, viewport, and revision metadata.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAdd semantic diagnostics for hidden, unreadable, unavailable, not-ready, and valid-but-uniform capture states.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRun the complete test suite cleanly.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAcceptance proof:\u003c/strong\u003e a capture manifest and current artifacts covering desktop/mobile, Swiss/Technical, light/dark, no-JS fallback, reduced motion, forced colors, and static/single-file parity.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"phase-6-optional-polish\"\u003ePhase 6: Optional polish\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eTokenize Mermaid styling and rerender diagrams after light/dark changes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eImprove graph edge disclosure, label collision handling, category restraint, and focused-neighborhood legibility without removing the complete Map lens.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMake graph Contrast/Border modifier scope coherent or explain the deliberate limitation in Appearance help.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRefine duplicate-title handling, reading/search composition, selected-comment context, and split-action clarity where live proof confirms the issue.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAdd versioned viewer asset URLs or an equivalent cache-busting contract.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eKeep every refinement within the existing Swiss-first Editorial Workbench language.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"parallelization-and-ownership\"\u003eParallelization and ownership\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eTheme/config state and its tests are one hot integration surface and should remain time.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eCapture tooling and documentation are parallel-safe until their final parity tests consume completed runtime behavior.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eVisual polish follows correctness and must use fresh captures from the final runtime, not the pre-hardening media.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"definition-of-done\"\u003eDefinition of "reference/architecture": "\u003ch2 id=\"architecture\"\u003eArchitecture\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis document is the developer-facing reference for okf-loom: the module map, the data flow, the extension points, the forward-compatibility mechanisms, and the rationale. For best-of-breed research see \u003ca href=\"/explanation/research.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresearch.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e; for harness-specific wiring see \u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eembedding-guide.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"design-philosophy-in-one-paragraph\"\u003eDesign philosophy (in one paragraph)\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOKF is intentionally minimal (SPEC §9). okf-loom mirrors that philosophy: it is \u003cstrong\u003epermissive\u003c/strong\u003e (load never hard-fails on soft issues), \u003cstrong\u003elayered\u003c/strong\u003e (cheap core, optional extras), and \u003cstrong\u003esingle-source-of-truth\u003c/strong\u003e (one canonical \u003ccode\u003eContentIndex\u003c/code\u003e that every consumer reads). It is \u003cstrong\u003eharness-agnostic\u003c/strong\u003e (no opinion on which agent framework consumes it) and \u003cstrong\u003eforward-compatible\u003c/strong\u003e (a capability registry lets bundles opt into optional extensions without spec changes). It is \u003cstrong\u003edependency-light by default\u003c/strong\u003e (PyYAML is preferred when present, with a conservative built-in fallback) so the same checkout runtime runs in a CI runner, a meta-agent's subprocess, or an air-gapped notebook.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"module-map\"\u003eModule map\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf_loom/\n├── __init__.py        — public API + versioning constants (SPEC_VERSION, RESERVED_FILENAMES, …)\n├── __main__.py        — module entry used by the `scripts/okf-loom` helper\n├── exceptions.py      — OKFError hierarchy\n├── paths.py           — ConceptId = tuple[str,...]; segment validation; path\u0026lt;-\u0026gt;id; reserved-name check; path_within_bundle symlink-containment guard\n├── parse.py           — frontmatter parse + serialize; link extraction (BOTH forms + wikilinks); markdown-\u0026gt;text\n├── model.py           — Bundle, Concept, IndexFile, LogFile, Link, Graph, ContentIndex, Heading; has_wikilinks\n├── ignore.py          — gitignore-style exclusion for bundle scanning (stdlib-only leaf): default excludes (hidden dirs, node_modules, nested git repos), .gitignore respect, bundle.exclude patterns, bundle.include add-backs (revive/reach/force semantics); iter_markdown_files pruning walker used by Bundle.load / serve watcher / import\n├── validate.py        — SPEC §9 conformance + warnings; CheckSpec; ValidationReport (with profile); Finding\n├── search.py          — SearchBackend Protocol; LexicalBackend (BM25) + SemanticLiteBackend + HybridBackend (RRF, all zero-dep); ENTITY/RELATION modes\n├── discover.py        — 6 discovery rules; Suggestion; DiscoveryReport\n├── plan.py            — PlannedAction/Plan; executable action-envelope planner (discovery + index staleness + relation mirroring)\n├── update.py          — UpdatePlan/UpdateOp; 8 idempotent op kinds (incl. add_entity); safe round-trip via parse/serialize; accepts studio/actor/origin/group_id and threads them through every concept write (single-funnel attribution)\n├── index.py           — SPEC §6 index.md regeneration; marker-safe; frozen CI mode; current spec §8 derived artifacts (emit_json)\n├── log.py             — SPEC §7 log.md append-only helper\n├── config.py          — okf-loom.config.yaml loader (bundle/viewer/search/validate/studio defaults); fail-closed bool + enum validation\n├── bootstrap.py       — init / bootstrap / import scaffolding\n├── extensions.py      — CapabilityRegistry + 25 built-in okf.cap.* capabilities (incl. aliases/provenance/citations/wikilinks/search_hybrid)\n├── cli.py             — argparse dispatcher (one cmd_* function per subcommand); includes wait, token, comment-claim, comment-resolve, comment-list, presence; mutators carry --group-id / --actor and route through the live studio funnel when a session exists\n├── render.py          — render_single_file + build_site (spa/static/single-file)\n├── server.py          — live HTTP wiki server (stdlib only); OKFWikiHandler; mtime watcher (log-and-retry); SSE /__events, EventBus, /__comment, /__apply (with 409 conflict), /__undo, /__preview, /__diff, /__presence, /__data/{doc,events}, per-session CSRF + Origin/Host allow-list, --public ack gate, --no-watch-ui server-side enforcement\n├── studio.py          — studio core: EventBus (subscribe/publish), Studio (single write funnel save_concept), presence, comments (claim/resolve), undo + group-undo, events.jsonl rotation, cross-process dedup; current spec §10-§13 library API (save_concept, post_presence, post_comment, resolve_comment, record_activity, events_append, post_suggestion)\n├── watch.py           — scripts/okf-loom watch headless change feed (reuses _BundleWatcher)\n└── viewer/\n    ├── __init__.py    — lazy public re-exports\n    ├── assets.py      — template/static/config/palette loaders (4 override points); two-layer active-code gate\n    ├── markdown.py    — small stdlib Markdown renderer + internal-link rewriter\n    ├── plugins.py     — entry-point ViewerPlugin loader (group okf_loom.viewer_plugins); CompositeViewerPlugin\n    ├── OVERRIDES.md   — concrete examples of every override point\n    ├── templates/     — single_file.html, concept_page.html, index_page.html, search_page.html, graph_page.html\n    └── static/        — wiki.{css,js}, graph.{css,js}, live.js (SSE + patching), studio.{css,js} (views/comments/collab UI), static-search.js, renderers.js (progressive mermaid/KaTeX/highlight.js enhancement, shared by wiki pages, the graph detail panel, and the single-file export)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"data-flow\"\u003eData flow\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"mermaid\"\u003eflowchart TB\n    Disk[(\"disk\")]\n    Load[\"Bundle.load(root)\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;model.py\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Concepts[concepts]\n    Indexes[indexes / logs]\n    Graph[\"Graph\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;model.py\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    CI[ContentIndex]\n\n    Load --\u0026gt; Concepts \u0026amp; Indexes\n    Concepts --\u0026gt; Graph \u0026amp; CI\n\n    Search[\"search_bundle\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;search.py\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Validate[\"validate_bundle\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;validate.py\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Discover[\"discover_suggestions\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;discover.py\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    CI --\u0026gt; Search \u0026amp; Validate \u0026amp; Discover\n\n    Backends[\"SearchBackend(s)\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;LexicalBackend always;\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;SemanticLite / Hybrid zero-dep\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Report[\"ValidationReport\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;errors / warnings / info\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Apply[\"apply_plan\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;update.py\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Mutated[(\"mutated concept files\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;round-trip safe\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\")]\n    Search --\u0026gt; Backends\n    Validate --\u0026gt; Report\n    Discover --\u0026gt; Apply --\u0026gt; Mutated\n\n    Viewer[\"viewer (render.py / server.py)\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;reads ContentIndex + Graph →\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;single-file HTML / live HTTP /\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;static site / SPA\"]\n    Mutated --\u0026gt; Viewer\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThree properties fall out of this:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCheap to load.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eBundle.load\u003c/code\u003e parses frontmatter and headings; it does not build the graph or the content index. Those are computed lazily and memoized on the Bundle instance (\u003ccode\u003ebundle.graph()\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebundle.content_index()\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOne canonical model.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eContentIndex\u003c/code\u003e is the Quartz lesson (see \u003ccode\u003eresearch.md\u003c/code\u003e §A): search, graph, listings, and the viewer all read the same in-memory object. There is no second index for the viewer.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMutations are round-trip.\u003c/strong\u003e Every writer (update.py, index.py, log.py) goes through \u003ccode\u003eparse_document → modify → serialize_document\u003c/code\u003e so unknown frontmatter keys and key order are preserved.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"extension-points-five\"\u003eExtension points (five)\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom is extensible without forking. The five override surfaces:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCapability registry\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eextensions.py\u003c/code\u003e). 25 built-in \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.*\u003c/code\u003e capabilities (core/recommended/optional tiers), including the governed-key caps (\u003ccode\u003ealiases\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eprovenance\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecitations\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eentities\u003c/code\u003e) and \u003ccode\u003ewikilinks\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003esearch_hybrid\u003c/code\u003e (auto-activate on \u003ccode\u003e[[…]]\u003c/code\u003e use / a hybrid search run). Bundles opt in via \u003ccode\u003eokf_extensions:\u003c/code\u003e in root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e frontmatter or by using the governed keys (auto-activation). Plugins add capabilities at import time via \u003ccode\u003edefault_registry().register(Capability(...))\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSearch backends\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003esearch.py\u003c/code\u003e). \u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e Protocol. The \u003ccode\u003eLexicalBackend\u003c/code\u003e (BM25), \u003ccode\u003eSemanticLiteBackend\u003c/code\u003e (trigram+token TF cosine), and \u003ccode\u003eHybridBackend\u003c/code\u003e (RRF fusion of the two) all ship dependency-free. There is no local embedding backend: the agent (an LLM in opencode / Claude Code / Codex) is itself the best true-semantic engine, so a dense/vector backend would be redundant. The CLI \u003ccode\u003e--mode\u003c/code\u003e flag dispatches to the matching backend.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eViewer template / static / palette / config overrides\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eviewer/assets.py\u003c/code\u003e). A bundle drops files under \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/viewer/{templates,static}/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/viewer/palette.json\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/viewer/config.json\u003c/code\u003e to customise rendering without code. Palette overrides are gated on the active-code gate AND validated against a strict CSS-color allowlist. See \u003ccode\u003eviewer/OVERRIDES.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eViewerPlugin hook\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eviewer/plugins.py\u003c/code\u003e, current spec §15). \u003ccode\u003eon_concept_render(concept, html) -\u0026gt; html\u003c/code\u003e (plus optional \u003ccode\u003eon_index_render\u003c/code\u003e). Plugins are discovered via the \u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.viewer_plugins\u003c/code\u003e entry-point group and called in registration order; raising plugins are logged and skipped. The two-layer active-code gate (bundle \u003ccode\u003eviewer.allow_active_code\u003c/code\u003e AND operator \u003ccode\u003e--allow-active-code\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eOKF_LOOM_ALLOW_ACTIVE_CODE\u003c/code\u003e) governs whether discovery runs at all. See \u003ccode\u003eviewer/OVERRIDES.md\u003c/code\u003e §5.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDiscovery rules\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003ediscover.py\u003c/code\u003e). The six built-in rules (\u003ccode\u003eunlinked_mentions\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emissing_indexes\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emissing_descriptions\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebroken_links\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emissing_relations_hint\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eorphan_concepts\u003c/code\u003e) are module-level functions taking a \u003ccode\u003eBundle\u003c/code\u003e and returning \u003ccode\u003elist[Suggestion]\u003c/code\u003e. Adding a rule = adding a function and a key in the \u003ccode\u003e_RULES\u003c/code\u003e registry.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"forward-compatibility\"\u003eForward compatibility\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom must stay correct as the spec moves (v0.1 → 0.x → 1.0) and let bundles extend without breaking. Four mechanisms:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSpec-version tracking.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eSPEC_VERSION = \"0.1\"\u003c/code\u003e is the single constant. On load, the bundle's declared \u003ccode\u003eokf_version\u003c/code\u003e is read; if it differs okf-loom does best-effort consumption and emits a warning (SPEC §11 mandate). The validator's \u003ccode\u003espec_version_check\u003c/code\u003e rule makes this visible.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCapability registry.\u003c/strong\u003e Optional behaviors live behind named capabilities (\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.typed_relations\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.entities\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.aliases\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.provenance\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.citations\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.wikilinks\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.search_hybrid\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.embeddings\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.discovery_ner\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.diataxis_types\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.jsonld_export\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.multi_bundle\u003c/code\u003e, … — 25 built-in total). They are recognised-if-present, never required. \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.wikilinks\u003c/code\u003e auto-activates on \u003ccode\u003e[[…]]\u003c/code\u003e body syntax (\u003ccode\u003ebundle.has_wikilinks\u003c/code\u003e); \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.search_hybrid\u003c/code\u003e activates when a hybrid search runs; the rest activate on their governed frontmatter keys. User-defined capabilities use a custom namespace (\u003ccode\u003eacme.x\u003c/code\u003e) and a JSON-schema fragment for the keys they introduce.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMigration hooks.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom upgrade --check\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--apply\u003c/code\u003e runs idempotent \u003ccode\u003emigrate(old -\u0026gt; new, bundle)\u003c/code\u003e transformers reusing the same pipeline. No migrations are defined for v0.1 (it is the baseline).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSafe auto-update of bundle structure.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e regeneration skips hand-authored files (or rewrites only inside \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;!-- okf:generated:index begin/end --\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e markers, or replaces files with \u003ccode\u003egenerated: true\u003c/code\u003e frontmatter). \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e updates are always append-only. Discovery finds gaps and emits a structured plan; the agent that manages the bundle applies its edits directly through the mutators (the CLI also offers a reviewable-plan workflow, but \u003ccode\u003eapply_plan\u003c/code\u003e itself never auto-runs from inside discovery — it is always called explicitly by the agent or user). A \u003ccode\u003e--frozen\u003c/code\u003e mode for CI fails loudly rather than writing to hand-authored files.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"performance-characteristics\"\u003ePerformance characteristics\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLoad.\u003c/strong\u003e O(N) over files; one YAML parse per file; no graph or content index is built. Suitable for thousand-concept bundles in well under a second.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGraph / ContentIndex.\u003c/strong\u003e Computed lazily on first call; memoized on the \u003ccode\u003eBundle\u003c/code\u003e instance. Cheap to rebuild by re-loading the bundle.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSearch (lexical).\u003c/strong\u003e O(N) per query over the in-memory corpus. Suitable up to ~10k concepts in a single process; beyond that, swap in a sqlite-vec- or API-embedding-backed custom \u003ccode\u003eSearchBackend\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eViewer (live server).\u003c/strong\u003e Per-request markdown render is O(body size). Bundle reload on file change is O(N); the watcher polls mtime every 1s.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAll writes are atomic.\u003c/strong\u003e tmp file + \u003ccode\u003eos.replace\u003c/code\u003e; no partial state visible to concurrent readers.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"the-live-collaborative-studio-layer\"\u003eThe live collaborative studio layer\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e runs a \u003cstrong\u003elive collaborative studio\u003c/strong\u003e: the user reads and \u003cstrong\u003edirects via comments\u003c/strong\u003e; an \u003cstrong\u003eexternal agent authors\u003c/strong\u003e the OKF files in real time through the same mutators it always uses. Every change appears live, in place, with no full-page refresh. The full current design lives in \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003espec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e; this section is the developer map. Three new modules (\u003ccode\u003estudio.py\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ewatch.py\u003c/code\u003e, plus extensions to \u003ccode\u003eserver.py\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003ecli.py\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eupdate.py\u003c/code\u003e) carry it; the wire format stays OKF SPEC v0.1.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"studio-layer-studiopy\"\u003eStudio layer — \u003ccode\u003estudio.py\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTwo classes carry the in-process studio:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eEventBus\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — thread-safe fan-out. Each subscriber gets a bounded \u003ccode\u003equeue.Queue\u003c/code\u003e (default 64); \u003ccode\u003epublish(event)\u003c/code\u003e enqueues to every subscriber in registration order; a slow subscriber drops deltas and gets one \u003ccode\u003eresync\u003c/code\u003e event so it never blocks the publisher. \u003ccode\u003esubscribe()\u003c/code\u003e takes an optional callback (the in-process embedding shape, §17) or returns the queue for the caller to poll. \u003ccode\u003eclient_count()\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eunsubscribe(sub)\u003c/code\u003e manage lifecycle.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eStudio\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — the per-bundle studio handle. Constructed via \u003ccode\u003eStudio.for_bundle(bundle_root, *, session_rel=\".okf-loom/session\", log_edits=True, bundle_name=\"\", max_queue=64)\u003c/code\u003e; \u003ccode\u003eensure_session()\u003c/code\u003e creates the session dir + the per-session CSRF token (\u003ccode\u003e.token\u003c/code\u003e, 0600).\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch5 id=\"single-internal-write-funnel-studiosave-concept\"\u003eSingle internal write funnel — \u003ccode\u003eStudio.save_concept(...)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/h5\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003esave_concept\u003c/code\u003e is the \u003cstrong\u003esingle internal atomic write path\u003c/strong\u003e every concept write goes through, whoever the caller is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"mermaid\"\u003eflowchart TB\n    CLI[\"CLI mutators\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;link-add / entity-add / update /\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;set-frontmatter / repair\"]\n    Lib[\"library\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;apply_plan (update.py)\"]\n    HTTP[\"HTTP\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;POST /__apply, POST /__undo\"]\n    Save[\"Studio.save_concept(concept_id, raw, actor,\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;action, origin, group_id, expected_rev, …)\"]\n    CLI --\u0026gt; Save\n    Lib --\u0026gt; Save\n    HTTP --\u0026gt; Save\n    Save --\u0026gt; Steps\n\n    subgraph Steps [\"save_concept pipeline (single write funnel)\"]\n        direction TB\n        S1[\"1. validate-before-write\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;never persist an unparseable file\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n        S2[\"2. expected_rev check\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;→ 409 Conflict on mismatch (§9.3/9.4)\"]\n        S3[\"3. snapshot for undo\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;→ .okf-loom/session/history/\u0026amp;lt;cid\u0026amp;gt;/\u0026amp;lt;rev\u0026amp;gt;.md\"]\n        S4[\"4. atomic_write_text\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;tmp + rename invariant preserved\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n        S5[\"5. events_append\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;→ .okf-loom/session/events.jsonl\"]\n        S6[\"6. bus.publish('changed')\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;→ SSE fan-out (+ 'graph' if edges moved)\"]\n        S7[\"7. (opt) log.md append\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;when studio.log_edits=true\"]\n        S1 --\u0026gt; S2 --\u0026gt; S3 --\u0026gt; S4 --\u0026gt; S5 --\u0026gt; S6 --\u0026gt; S7\n    end\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBecause every writer goes through the same funnel, \u003cstrong\u003eattribution is exact\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eactor\u003c/code\u003e + \u003ccode\u003eorigin\u003c/code\u003e), \u003cstrong\u003eundo is always available\u003c/strong\u003e (snapshot + optional group manifest under \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/history/\u0026lt;group_id\u0026gt;/\u003c/code\u003e), and the \u003cstrong\u003echange list is complete\u003c/strong\u003e (one \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e row per write). There is no duplicated bookkeeping between the CLI and HTTP paths.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eapply_plan\u003c/code\u003e (update.py) accepts \u003ccode\u003estudio\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eactor\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eorigin\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003egroup_id\u003c/code\u003e and threads them through every op, so a multi-op pass is one group-undoable unit. \u003ccode\u003e_handle_apply\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e_handle_undo\u003c/code\u003e in \u003ccode\u003eserver.py\u003c/code\u003e call \u003ccode\u003esave_concept\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003erestore_snapshot\u003c/code\u003e directly — the HTTP layer stays a thin wrapper over the same funnel (current spec §10/§13).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCLI mutators detect a live session via \u003ccode\u003e_maybe_studio_for_bundle\u003c/code\u003e and route through \u003ccode\u003e_studio_aware_apply\u003c/code\u003e. \u003cstrong\u003eWithout\u003c/strong\u003e a session (no \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e) they fall back to the non-studio atomic write path — same data-safety, but no attribution / undo / events / SSE.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"session-storage-bundleokf-loomsession\"\u003eSession storage — \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAll session state lives under \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e (configurable via \u003ccode\u003estudio.session_dir\u003c/code\u003e). It is \u003cstrong\u003eephemeral\u003c/strong\u003e (recommend \u003ccode\u003e.gitignore\u003c/code\u003e); deleting it loses only the live feed + undo, never the content or the permanent \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eFile / dir\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003ePurpose\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eLifetime\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe single change/event log (current spec §11/§13). One JSON-line event per write. Powers the change list, the SSE stream, and \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch --since\u003c/code\u003e. Rotates at the cap (default 8 MiB) to \u003ccode\u003eevents-YYYYMMDD-NN.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edirectives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUser comments / asks (current spec §12). One JSON-line directive per comment. \u003ccode\u003eopen\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003edismissed\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003epresence.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAgent presence (current spec §12): \u003ccode\u003e{actor, state, focus, ts}\u003c/code\u003e. State ∈ \u003ccode\u003eidle\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ewatching\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ethinking\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eediting\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.token\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePer-session CSRF token (\u003ccode\u003eX-OKF-Token\u003c/code\u003e), written 0600 on \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e boot. Read by \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom token\u003c/code\u003e and attached by the studio's own JS.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eper-session\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.last-logged.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCross-process dedup index (current spec §13). Maps the most-recent \u003ccode\u003erev\u003c/code\u003e logged per concept so the watcher's disk-backfill never double-logs a write that already logged itself.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehistory/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUndo snapshots (current spec §13). \u003ccode\u003ehistory/\u0026lt;cid\u0026gt;/\u0026lt;rev\u0026gt;.md\u003c/code\u003e is a capped ring per concept; \u003ccode\u003ehistory/\u0026lt;group_id\u0026gt;/\u003c/code\u003e carries the group manifest for one-click group undo.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e_groups/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eGroup-undo manifests (one per \u003ccode\u003e--group-id\u003c/code\u003e pass): the concept ids + revs to restore.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eproposals.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOnly under a user's opt-in \u003ccode\u003epropose_only\u003c/code\u003e constraint\u003c/strong\u003e (current spec §10): the agent appends \u003ccode\u003ePlannedAction\u003c/code\u003e envelopes here for review. Absent by default.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eephemeral\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"the-agent-loop-current-spec-12\"\u003eThe agent loop (current spec §12)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe agent is the \u003cstrong\u003eprocessor\u003c/strong\u003e; it does not run a background daemon. The canonical foreground loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"mermaid\"\u003eflowchart TB\n    Serve[\"scripts/okf-loom serve \u0026amp;lt;bundle\u0026amp;gt; --no-open \u0026amp;amp;\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;writes .okf-loom/session/.token (0600)\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Wait[\"scripts/okf-loom wait \u0026amp;lt;bundle\u0026amp;gt;\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;foreground block-once → one work item\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;(comment / change)\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Claim[\"scripts/okf-loom comment-claim \u0026amp;lt;bundle\u0026amp;gt; \u0026amp;lt;id\u0026amp;gt;\"]\n    Presence[\"scripts/okf-loom presence \u0026amp;lt;bundle\u0026amp;gt;\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;--state editing --focus \u0026amp;lt;id\u0026amp;gt;\"]\n    Mutate[\"scripts/okf-loom link-add … --group-id PASS1\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;scripts/okf-loom entity-add … --group-id PASS1\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;\u0026lt;i\u0026gt;routes through save_concept:\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;attributed + undoable + events + SSE\u0026lt;/i\u0026gt;\"]\n    Resolve[\"scripts/okf-loom comment-resolve \u0026amp;lt;bundle\u0026amp;gt; \u0026amp;lt;id\u0026amp;gt;\u0026lt;br/\u0026gt;--activity \u0026amp;lt;id\u0026amp;gt;,… --reply '…'\"]\n\n    Serve --\u0026gt; Wait\n    Wait --\u0026gt; Claim --\u0026gt; Presence --\u0026gt; Mutate --\u0026gt; Resolve\n    Resolve -.-\u0026gt;|\"loop\"| Wait\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait --for comment\u003c/code\u003e (default) blocks for the next \u003ccode\u003eopen\u003c/code\u003e user comment; \u003ccode\u003e--for change\u003c/code\u003e for proactive enrichment; \u003ccode\u003e--for comment change\u003c/code\u003e for whichever arrives first. \u003cstrong\u003eRun it in the agent foreground\u003c/strong\u003e (you are the processor); backgrounding it (\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait \u0026amp;\u003c/code\u003e) leaves returned work unconsumed. \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e is the continuous-tail counterpart for piping the feed to a long-running external consumer.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"cross-process-dedup-model-current-spec-13\"\u003eCross-process dedup model (current spec §13)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSeveral writers can mutate the bundle concurrently — the agent's CLI mutator calls, \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch --auto-repair\u003c/code\u003e, the user editing files in their own editor, and direct CLI. Each appends its own fully-attributed event through one helper, \u003ccode\u003eStudio.events_append(event)\u003c/code\u003e, under a short advisory file lock (\u003ccode\u003efcntl.flock\u003c/code\u003e POSIX / \u003ccode\u003emsvcrt.locking\u003c/code\u003e Windows; the fallback is a single-line \u003ccode\u003eO_APPEND\u003c/code\u003e write, which is atomic for small records on POSIX). For changes that \u003cstrong\u003eweren't\u003c/strong\u003e logged by a studio writer (the user's editor, any outside tool), the \u003ccode\u003e_BundleWatcher\u003c/code\u003e detects the mtime change, diffs the \u003ccode\u003eContentIndex\u003c/code\u003e, and appends an \u003ccode\u003eorigin:\"disk\"\u003c/code\u003e event; \u003ccode\u003e.last-logged.json\u003c/code\u003e de-dupes by \u003ccode\u003erev\u003c/code\u003e so the watcher never double-logs a write that already logged itself. The feed is therefore complete regardless of which path produced the change.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"trust-model-single-user-local-admin-current-spec-14\"\u003eTrust model — single-user local admin (current spec §14)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe user is the admin and is \u003cstrong\u003enever gated\u003c/strong\u003e. The studio keeps exactly the protections that cost the user zero friction and defend against things that are not the user:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLoopback by default.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e binds \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e. Exposing the port to a network (\u003ccode\u003e--public\u003c/code\u003e, or a non-loopback \u003ccode\u003e--host\u003c/code\u003e) requires either \u003ccode\u003e--public-ack\u003c/code\u003e (non-interactive, CI) or an interactive \u003ccode\u003ey/N\u003c/code\u003e ack; the server refuses to start otherwise (exit 2). Closes the warn-only gap on a non-loopback bind (current spec §14).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePer-session CSRF token\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eX-OKF-Token\u003c/code\u003e). Written to \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/.token\u003c/code\u003e (mode 0600) on boot, embedded in the served page, auto-attached by the studio's own JS to mutating requests. Read it with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom token \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e when you must POST over HTTP directly.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOrigin AND Host allow-list.\u003c/strong\u003e Every mutating endpoint (\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e/__apply\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e/__undo\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e/__presence\u003c/code\u003e) checks \u003cstrong\u003eboth\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eOrigin\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eHost\u003c/code\u003e against \u003ccode\u003eallowed_hosts\u003c/code\u003e (default \u003ccode\u003e[127.0.0.1, localhost]\u003c/code\u003e; never empty). The Host check (current spec §14) closes a DNS-rebinding hole that forging only the \u003ccode\u003eOrigin\u003c/code\u003e could exploit.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--no-watch-ui\u003c/code\u003e enforced server-side (current spec §11/§14).\u003c/strong\u003e When SSE / live UI is off, \u003ccode\u003e/__events\u003c/code\u003e returns \u003ccode\u003e503\u003c/code\u003e and the watcher is skipped entirely — not just hidden on the client.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--no-edit\u003c/code\u003e refuses writes at the route layer.\u003c/strong\u003e Live reads stay available; all \u003ccode\u003ePOST\u003c/code\u003e endpoints are disabled.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMalicious-bundle code is still gated\u003c/strong\u003e behind the existing two-layer active-code gate (bundle \u003ccode\u003eviewer.allow_active_code: true\u003c/code\u003e AND operator \u003ccode\u003e--allow-active-code\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eOKF_LOOM_ALLOW_ACTIVE_CODE\u003c/code\u003e). Editing / saving / watching are explicitly \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e behind this gate.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eData-safety invariants\u003c/strong\u003e (correctness, not permission): validate before write (never persist an unparseable file), the \u003ccode\u003eparse.py\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003emarkdown.py\u003c/code\u003e DoS caps (including the nested-list recursion cap on \u003ccode\u003e/__preview\u003c/code\u003e), \u003ccode\u003epaths.path_within_bundle\u003c/code\u003e containment, atomic writes (tmp + rename), optimistic per-doc \u003ccode\u003erev\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003e/__apply\u003c/code\u003e mapping ids → known \u003ccode\u003eUpdateOp\u003c/code\u003es (never a shell/argv string). \u003ccode\u003erev\u003c/code\u003e + \u003ccode\u003egroup_id\u003c/code\u003e are validated against \u003ccode\u003e_SAFE_PATH_TOKEN_RE\u003c/code\u003e before any filesystem op under \u003ccode\u003ehistory/\u003c/code\u003e (§9.5).\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSummary:\u003c/strong\u003e the studio gates the port and the bundle's code, never the user or their agent. The user's safety net for agent-authored edits is the \u003cstrong\u003elive change list + (group) undo\u003c/strong\u003e, not an approval step.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"conflict-handling-93-94\"\u003eConflict handling (§9.3 / §9.4)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBecause the agent is the sole writer of \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e files through the studio, there is no user↔agent merge problem day-to-day. \u003ccode\u003erev = sha1(raw)[:12]\u003c/code\u003e per-doc keeps live updates coherent. The one real collision — the user editing a file directly on disk at the same moment the agent writes it — surfaces non-destructively: \u003ccode\u003ePOST /__apply\u003c/code\u003e with a stale \u003ccode\u003eexpected_rev\u003c/code\u003e returns \u003ccode\u003e409\u003c/code\u003e with \u003ccode\u003e{conflict, expected_rev, current_rev}\u003c/code\u003e (no silent clobber), and \u003ccode\u003eGET /__diff?id=\u0026amp;from=\u0026amp;to=\u003c/code\u003e returns a line diff for the banner's \"View diff\" affordance.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"test-suite\"\u003eTest suite\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etests/test_\u0026lt;module\u0026gt;.py\u003c/code\u003e per source module.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etests/fixtures/{tiny_good,tiny_bad,empty_bundle}/\u003c/code\u003e cover the format surface (both link forms, typed relations, generated index, log.md, missing-description case, broken-link case, malformed frontmatter).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etests/test_integration.py\u003c/code\u003e runs full load → validate → discover → plan → apply → re-validate loops against the upstream \u003ccode\u003ega4\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003estackoverflow\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ecrypto_bitcoin\u003c/code\u003e bundles (marked \u003ccode\u003e@pytest.mark.integration\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRun the suite: \u003ccode\u003ecd okf-loom \u0026amp;\u0026amp; python -m pytest\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eFast subset: \u003ccode\u003epython -m pytest -m \"not integration\"\u003c/code\u003e (≈1.5s).\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"what-okf-loom-deliberately-is-not\"\u003eWhat okf-loom deliberately is NOT\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eIt is not a producer/enrichment agent. Upstream's \u003ccode\u003ereference_agent\u003c/code\u003e writes bundles by crawling BigQuery + the web; okf-loom consumes, validates, curates, and renders bundles produced by anyone.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eIt is not a replacement for the upstream base wire-format spec. \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/spec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e governs current okf-loom behavior on top of upstream OKF SPEC v0.1.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eIt is not a hosted service. The viewer is a static-site / live-dev server; it does not assume a database, an account system, or a network.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eIt is not coupled to any specific agent framework. See \u003ccode\u003eembedding_guide.md\u003c/code\u003e for wiring recipes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"references\"\u003eReferences\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eCurrent okf-loom spec: \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/spec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eUpstream base OKF SPEC v0.1: \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003ehttps://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eUpstream reference implementation: the upstream OKF SPEC repository (external)\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eBest-of-breed research: \u003ccode\u003edocs-bundle/explanation/research.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eHarness wiring: \u003ccode\u003edocs-bundle/reference/embedding_guide.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eOverride examples: \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf_loom/viewer/OVERRIDES.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e", "reference/capabilities": "\u003ch2 id=\"capability-registry\"\u003eCapability registry\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCapabilities are okf-loom's forward-compatibility mechanism. SPEC §9 mandates that producers MAY add arbitrary frontmatter keys and consumers MUST preserve them round-trip; the capability registry is how okf-loom makes those arbitrary keys \u003cstrong\u003emeaningful\u003c/strong\u003e without requiring a spec change.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA capability is a named, versioned declaration of an OPTIONAL behaviour okf-loom recognises. Format primitives okf-loom could not function without.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUnconditional.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003erecommended\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eShips with opt-in.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eActivate on declaration or on observed use of governed keys.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA capability is Non-root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e files are pure listings and cannot declare extensions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"auto-activation\"\u003eAuto-activation\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA capability auto-activates the moment any of its governed \u003ccode\u003efrontmatter_keys\u003c/code\u003e appears in any concept, or any of its \u003ccode\u003ebody_sections\u003c/code\u003e appears as a heading. No declaration is required.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eExample: adding \u003ccode\u003eentities:\u003c/code\u003e to a single concept activates \u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.entities\u003c/code\u003e for the whole bundle; entity search and the SemanticLite profile (which weights entity labels + aliases) begin honouring it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"special-case-activations\"\u003eSpecial-case activations\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eCapability\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eSpecial activation\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.search_hybrid\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eActivated on the first hybrid query that produces at least one match (\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom search … --mode hybrid\u003c/code\u003e). A zero-match query does NOT activate.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.wikilinks\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBody syntax only. \u003ccode\u003eis_active(cap_id)\u003c/code\u003e is the per-capability check.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"validation\"\u003eValidation\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eCheck\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eSeverity\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhen it fires\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecapability.undeclared\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWARNING\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA declared id is not in the registry.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecapability.inactive_use\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eINFO\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept uses a governed key without the capability declared (auto-activated).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --checks capability_declarations\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"defining-a-custom-capability\"\u003eDefining a custom capability\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003efrom okf_loom.extensions import Capability, default_registry\n\ndefault_registry().register(Capability(\n    id=\"acme.custom_taxonomy\",\n    tier=\"optional\",\n    description=\"Recognise Acme's internal concept taxonomy.\",\n    frontmatter_keys=(\"acme_kind\", \"acme_domain\"),\n    body_sections=(\"Acceptance Criteria\",),\n))\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe id must be namespaced (e.g. \u003ccode\u003eacme.x\u003c/code\u003e); bare names without a dot are rejected at registration time.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA plugin that wants to \u003cstrong\u003eact\u003c/strong\u003e on the capability should register a transformer/emitter (for viewer behaviour) or check \u003ccode\u003eresolved.is_active(\"acme.custom_taxonomy\")\u003c/code\u003e in its own code.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRuntime third-party plugin loading is wired through the \u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.viewer_plugins\u003c/code\u003e entry-point group;
