"\u003ch2 id=\"embedding-okf-loom-in-an-agent-harness\"\u003eEmbedding okf-loom in an Agent Harness\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis guide shows how to wire okf-loom into any agent / meta-harness. okf-loom is \u003cstrong\u003eharness-agnostic by design\u003c/strong\u003e: no agent-framework code lives in this repository. The intended audience is \u003cstrong\u003eagents in opencode / Claude Code / Codex that point at the \u003ccode\u003eokf\u003c/code\u003e CLI\u003c/strong\u003e — so Shape 1 (CLI subprocess) is the primary path. Shape 2 (Python library import) and Shape 3 (embedded HTTP server) are advanced seams for harness authors who need them. Shape 4 covers the \u003cstrong\u003elive studio\u003c/strong\u003e agent loop (built on shapes 1–3).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePick the shape that matches how your harness already works:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eShape\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhen to use\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003ePros\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCons\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e1. CLI subprocess\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cem\u003e(primary)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYour harness already shells out to CLIs (most do — including opencode, Claude Code, Codex)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eZero coupling; JSON I/O; language-agnostic\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eProcess-spawn latency per call\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2. Python library\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cem\u003e(advanced)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYour harness is Python and you want in-process caching / the full API without subprocess overhead\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eNo subprocess; in-process caching; full API\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCouples to Python\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Embedded server\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYou want a long-running wiki the harness can point a browser at\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eInteractive; hot-reload; same process as the agent\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne server per bundle\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e4. Live studio \u0026amp; agent loop\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYou want the collaborative studio: user directs via comments, agent authors the bundle live\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eReal-time collaboration; headless \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e feed; in-process event bus\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne server per bundle; agent must watch + write via mutators\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRead \u003ca href=\"../../SKILL.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e first\u003c/strong\u003e if you are an agent — it is the loadable skill entrypoint. Focused skill resources live under \u003ca href=\"../../resources/\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresources/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"shape-1-cli-subprocess\"\u003eShape 1 — CLI subprocess\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe simplest integration. Your agent constructs a command, runs it, and parses JSON on stdout. Most harnesses already do this for \u003ccode\u003egit\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erg\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003enpm\u003c/code\u003e, etc.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003eOKF_REPO=/path/to/okf-loom\n\n# Validate (returns 0 ok / 1 conformance fail / 2 strict fail)\n\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" validate /path/to/bundle --format json\n\n# Inspect\n\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" info /path/to/bundle --format json\n\n# Find gaps (writes a JSON report)\n\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" discover /path/to/bundle --out /tmp/plan.json\n\n# Apply an update plan (idempotent)\n\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" update /path/to/bundle --plan /tmp/plan.json --format json\n\n# Stand up the viewer (blocks; the harness can run it in a side-thread or background process)\n\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" serve /path/to/bundle --port 8787 --no-open\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReport commands document their JSON mode in \u003ccode\u003e$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom \u0026lt;cmd\u0026gt; --help\u003c/code\u003e; server/watch/render/build commands expose command-specific output flags instead. This shape is \u003cstrong\u003elanguage-agnostic\u003c/strong\u003e — a Node, Go, or Rust agent can use okf-loom identically.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"discovery-update-loop-the-typical-agent-task\"\u003eDiscovery → Update loop (the typical agent task)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# 1. Find what's missing\nscripts/okf-loom discover /path/to/bundle --format json \u0026gt; /tmp/discovery.json\n# (the agent reads discovery.json, decides which suggestions to accept,\n#  and writes /tmp/plan.json with the matching UpdateOp entries — see\n#  docs-bundle/reference/cli.md and resources/advanced-operations.md for the op-kind reference)\n\n# 2. Preview\nscripts/okf-loom update /path/to/bundle --plan /tmp/plan.json --dry-run\n\n# 3. Apply\nscripts/okf-loom update /path/to/bundle --plan /tmp/plan.json\n\n# 4. Re-validate\nscripts/okf-loom validate /path/to/bundle --format json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"shape-2-python-library-advanced\"\u003eShape 2 — Python library \u003cem\u003e(advanced)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis is an \u003cstrong\u003eadvanced seam\u003c/strong\u003e for harness authors building a dedicated Python integration that wants in-process caching or the full library API without subprocess overhead. The primary embedding path for agents in opencode / Claude Code / Codex is \u003cstrong\u003eShape 1 (CLI subprocess)\u003c/strong\u003e above — those agents use the \u003ccode\u003eokf\u003c/code\u003e CLI, they do not \u003ccode\u003eimport okf_loom\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor Python harnesses (LangGraph tools, custom agents) that need it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003efrom okf_loom import Bundle\nfrom okf_loom.validate import validate_bundle\nfrom okf_loom.discover import discover_suggestions\nfrom okf_loom.update import load_plan, apply_plan\nfrom okf_loom.search import search_bundle, SearchMode\n\nbundle = Bundle.load(\"/path/to/bundle\")\n\n# Validate\nreport = validate_bundle(bundle)\nif not report.ok:\n    for f in report.errors:\n        print(f.path, f.code, f.message)\n\n# Discover gaps\ndiscovery = discover_suggestions(bundle, rules=[\"unlinked_mentions\", \"orphan_concepts\"])\nfor s in discovery.suggestions:\n    print(s.rule, s.concept_id, s.action, s.message)\n\n# (your code converts accepted suggestions to UpdateOp entries and\n#  writes a plan file — see docs-bundle/reference/cli.md and resources/advanced-operations.md)\n\n# Apply a plan\nplan = load_plan(\"/tmp/plan.json\")\nsummary = apply_plan(bundle, plan)\nprint(summary[\"applied\"], \"applied;\", summary[\"skipped\"], \"skipped\")\n\n# Search\nfor r in search_bundle(bundle, \"customer order\", mode=SearchMode.LEXICAL, limit=5):\n    print(r.score, r.concept_id, r.title)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCache invalidation.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eBundle.graph()\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eBundle.content_index()\u003c/code\u003e memoize on the instance. After mutating the bundle via \u003ccode\u003eapply_plan\u003c/code\u003e, reload: \u003ccode\u003ebundle = Bundle.load(bundle.root)\u003c/code\u003e. The lexical search backend caches on the \u003ccode\u003eBundle\u003c/code\u003e instance itself; long-running servers that reload bundles evict it by reloading the bundle or calling \u003ccode\u003ebundle.invalidate()\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.search.clear_search_cache()\u003c/code\u003e is a deprecated no-op kept for import compatibility.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"shape-3-embedded-http-server\"\u003eShape 3 — Embedded HTTP server\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun the live viewer inside the agent process so a browser (the user, a scraper, an MCP browser tool) can navigate the bundle while the agent works on it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003eimport threading\nfrom http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer\nfrom okf_loom import Bundle\nfrom okf_loom.server import OKFWikiHandler\n\nbundle = Bundle.load(\"/path/to/bundle\")\nhttpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((\"127.0.0.1\", 8787), OKFWikiHandler)\nhttpd.bundle = bundle                       # the handler reads this attribute\nthreading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()\n\n# Later, after the agent has mutated the bundle on disk:\nhttpd.bundle = Bundle.load(\"/path/to/bundle\")  # hot-swap; next request sees it\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRoutes are documented in \u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHTTP routes\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"../../resources/advanced-operations.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eadvanced operations\u003c/a\u003e. The most useful for agents:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/\u0026lt;concept_id\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e — rendered concept page.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/__raw/\u0026lt;concept_id\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e — raw markdown body (for the agent to read into its own context).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/__data/graph.json\u003c/code\u003e — the link graph as JSON (for the agent to reason about structure).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/__data/content.json\u003c/code\u003e — the full content index as JSON.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/__search?q=…\u0026amp;format=json\u003c/code\u003e — search-as-you-type results.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"shape-4-live-studio-the-agent-loop\"\u003eShape 4 — Live studio \u0026amp; the agent loop\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e runs a \u003cstrong\u003elive collaborative studio\u003c/strong\u003e: the user \u003cstrong\u003edirects\u003c/strong\u003e (reads + comments) and an \u003cstrong\u003eexternal agent authors\u003c/strong\u003e the OKF files in real time. The server stays LLM-free — it emits events and runs mechanical ops; the agent (in opencode / Claude Code / Codex / any harness) does the thinking and writes back through the \u003cstrong\u003eexisting mutators\u003c/strong\u003e. This shape is how an agent harness wires into that loop. See \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/reference/spec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e §10 for the posture and the bring-up \"watch\" question.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBring-up (§3).\u003c/strong\u003e When you open the studio for the user, ask one courtesy question: \u003cem\u003e\"I've opened the live studio for \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e. Want me to \u003cstrong\u003ewatch it and keep it enriched\u003c/strong\u003e — proactively adding links, entities, relations, indexes, and descriptions as it changes? Either way I'll do whatever you ask via comments.\"\u003c/em\u003e This is a collaboration choice, \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e a permission gate — the agent is free to edit the OKF files regardless (current spec §10).\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"4a-headless-feed-with-scriptsokf-loom-watch-continuous-tail\"\u003e4a — Headless feed with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e (continuous tail)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e reuses the bundle watcher and prints one event per line (the §7.2 schema) for a long-running consumer to pipe to the agent. No HTTP server needed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# Tail every change to the bundle as JSON Lines\nscripts/okf-loom watch /path/to/bundle --emit jsonl\n\n# Reconnect-safe: replay missed events from an id, then tail live\nscripts/okf-loom watch /path/to/bundle --emit jsonl --since 01JABED5K7\n\n# Let okf-loom run mechanical repairs on change (debounced), debounced 600ms\nscripts/okf-loom watch /path/to/bundle --auto-repair --debounce-ms 600\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ewatch\u003c/code\u003e both append the durable, replayable \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/events.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e — the audit trail and how a headless agent \"sees\" the user's saves.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"4a-foreground-block-once-with-scriptsokf-loom-wait-the-primary-agent-loop\"\u003e4a′ — Foreground block-once with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e (the primary agent loop)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen \u003cstrong\u003ethe agent itself is the consumer\u003c/strong\u003e (the common case in opencode / Claude Code / Codex), prefer \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e over \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e. It \u003cstrong\u003eblocks until there is work\u003c/strong\u003e (a new open comment and/or a change event), prints that one item as JSON, and exits — so the agent wakes, acts, and re-waits in a clean foreground loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# Blocks until a new OPEN user comment, prints it, exits 0. AWAIT this —\n# do NOT background it (you are the processor; a backgrounded wait has no\n# consumer, so comments would sit open forever).\nscripts/okf-loom wait /path/to/bundle --for comment\n\n# Wait for comments OR proactive-enrichment changes (whichever first):\nscripts/okf-loom wait /path/to/bundle --for comment change --timeout 600\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eLibrary equivalent: \u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.studio.wait_for_work(bundle_root, kinds=..., since=..., timeout=..., interval=...)\u003c/code\u003e. The loop is: \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e → read JSON → reason → edit via mutators (\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eupdate\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eentity-add\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003erepair\u003c/code\u003e) → resolve the comment → \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e again.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"4b-the-comment-claim-write-resolve-flow\"\u003e4b — The comment → claim → write → resolve flow\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe user's only studio writes are \u003cstrong\u003ecomments / asks\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment\u003c/code\u003e), which land in \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/directives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e. The agent's loop (run \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e in your foreground — you are the processor):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# 0. Studio must be up so the session dir + .token exist.\nscripts/okf-loom serve /path/to/bundle --no-open \u0026amp;\n\n# 1. Block-once for the next OPEN comment.\nscripts/okf-loom wait /path/to/bundle --for comment      # → {id, concept, anchor, body, …}\n\n# 2. Claim it + announce presence.\nscripts/okf-loom comment-claim /path/to/bundle 01JABED9K0\nscripts/okf-loom presence     /path/to/bundle --state editing --focus tables/orders\n\n# 3. Author via the mutators. With a live session the CLI routes through\n#    Studio.save_concept — each op is attributed (actor=agent, origin=mutator),\n#    undoable, and emits 'changed' + 'graph'. --group-id groups the pass for\n#    one-click group undo (§12.5).\nscripts/okf-loom plan     /path/to/bundle --scope tables/orders --neighbors --out /tmp/p.json\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle /path/to/bundle --source tables/orders \\\n             --target tables/customers --relation depends_on --group-id PASS1\nscripts/okf-loom entity-add --bundle /path/to/bundle --id tables/orders \\\n               --label \"Order\" --kind Table --group-id PASS1\nscripts/okf-loom update   /path/to/bundle --plan /tmp/p.json --group-id PASS1\n\n# 4. Resolve the comment, linking the activity ids the writes produced.\nscripts/okf-loom comment-resolve /path/to/bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n    --activity 01JABED5K7,01JABED5K8 --reply \"Done - added depends_on + Order entity\"\n\n# 5. Loop: scripts/okf-loom wait again.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach write flows file → \u003ccode\u003eStudio.save_concept\u003c/code\u003e → watcher → live update (SSE) + a change-list entry + an undo snapshot — the user sees it appear in place, with a highlight, no full refresh.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe per-session CSRF token (\u003ccode\u003eX-OKF-Token\u003c/code\u003e) and Origin/Host allow-list guard every mutating endpoint (current spec §14). The CLI mutators and the \u003ccode\u003ecomment-*\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003epresence\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003etoken\u003c/code\u003e commands attach the token for you. If you must POST to \u003ccode\u003e/__apply\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e/__undo\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e/__presence\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e/__comment\u003c/code\u003e over HTTP directly, read the token via \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom token /path/to/bundle\u003c/code\u003e (it reads \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/.token\u003c/code\u003e, mode 0600, set on \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e boot) — never hand-copy it:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003eTOKEN=$(scripts/okf-loom token /path/to/bundle)\ncurl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/__presence \\\n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n     -H \"X-OKF-Token: $TOKEN\" \\\n     -d '{\"actor\":\"agent\",\"state\":\"editing\",\"focus\":\"tables/orders\"}'\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a fully headless integration (no \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e running), the CLI mutators fall back to the non-studio atomic write path: same data-safety, but no attribution / undo / live push. To get the live collaboration surface, run \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e (or any process that creates \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e) before invoking the mutators.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"4c-embedding-the-studio-in-process-python\"\u003e4c — Embedding the studio in-process (Python)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a Python harness that wants the studio, the event bus, and the watcher \u003cstrong\u003ein the same process\u003c/strong\u003e (no subprocess, no HTTP round-trip):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003eimport threading, queue\nfrom okf_loom.studio import Studio\nfrom okf_loom.watch import run_watch\n\n# 1. Construct (or reuse) the studio handle for a bundle.\nstudio = Studio.for_bundle(\n    \"/path/to/bundle\",\n    session_rel=\".okf-loom/session\",   # default\n    log_edits=True,               # append a SPEC §7 log.md entry per write\n    bundle_name=\"My Bundle\",\n    max_queue=64,\n)\nstudio.ensure_session()\n\n# 2. Subscribe to in-process events (returns a bounded queue.Queue you poll).\nbus_q: queue.Queue = studio.bus.subscribe()\ndef _drain():\n    while True:\n        event = bus_q.get()        # blocks until an event arrives\n        print(\"studio event:\", event)   # {type, rev, ids, actor, ...} (§7.2)\nthreading.Thread(target=_drain, daemon=True).start()\n\n# 3. Publish from your own code if you drive the bundle programmatically:\nstudio.bus.publish({\"type\": \"presence\", \"actor\": \"agent\", \"state\": \"watching\"})\n\n# 4. Headless feed as a library call (same loop `scripts/okf-loom watch` runs):\n#    run_watch(\"/path/to/bundle\", emit=\"jsonl\", since=None,\n#              auto_repair=False, debounce_ms=600)  # -\u0026gt; exit code (blocks)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003erun_server(..., studio_edit=True, studio_live=True)\u003c/code\u003e (see Shape 3) attaches \u003ccode\u003eserver.studio\u003c/code\u003e — the \u003ccode\u003eStudio\u003c/code\u003e instance (or \u003ccode\u003eNone\u003c/code\u003e if both are off) — so a daemon-thread embedder can reach \u003ccode\u003ehttpd.studio.bus.subscribe()\u003c/code\u003e for events without launching \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e separately.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch5 id=\"eventbussubscribecallback-the-in-process-fan-out-shape-17\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eEventBus.subscribe(callback)\u003c/code\u003e — the in-process fan-out shape (§17)\u003c/h5\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003esubscribe()\u003c/code\u003e also takes an optional \u003cstrong\u003ecallback\u003c/strong\u003e for the simplest in-process embedding — no queue to poll, no thread to spawn:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003efrom okf_loom.studio import Studio\n\nstudio = Studio.for_bundle(\"/path/to/bundle\")\nstudio.ensure_session()\n\n# One subscription = one callback invoked per published event from any writer\n# (the CLI mutators in this process, the watcher's disk-backfill, your own\n# publish() calls). Returns an opaque sub handle you pass to unsubscribe().\nsub = studio.bus.subscribe(callback=lambda ev: print(\"event:\", ev))\n\n# ... later, when you no longer care:\nstudio.bus.unsubscribe(sub)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe callback runs on the publisher's thread, so keep it cheap (hand off to a worker queue if you do heavy work). The bus delivers events in publish order; a slow callback does not block other subscribers (they each have their own bounded queue, and a callback subscriber that lags gets a \u003ccode\u003eresync\u003c/code\u003e event).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch5 id=\"eventbussubscribecallback-trust-boundary-p3-12-sec2-007\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eEventBus.subscribe(callback)\u003c/code\u003e trust boundary (P3-12 / SEC2-007)\u003c/h5\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003esubscribe(callback)\u003c/code\u003e runs the \u003cstrong\u003ecaller-supplied Python callable inside the server process\u003c/strong\u003e. This is intentional — it is the §17 in-process embedding seam — but it is also a \u003cstrong\u003etrust boundary equivalent to the bundle \u003ccode\u003eactive-code\u003c/code\u003e gate\u003c/strong\u003e (§15.4):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBundle active-code\u003c/strong\u003e (the \u003ccode\u003e{{ ... }}\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003e{% ... %}\u003c/code\u003e template blocks a bundle can embed) is sandboxed to the bundle directory and gated by the operator-consent flag. A bundle cannot reach \u003ccode\u003eEventBus.subscribe\u003c/code\u003e from inside the server — the bundle has no Python import surface, only rendered markdown.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eEventBus.subscribe(callback)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e is the harness-author surface. A callback you register has the \u003cstrong\u003efull privilege of the server process\u003c/strong\u003e: it can \u003ccode\u003eimport\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eopen()\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esubprocess.run\u003c/code\u003e, read \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/.token\u003c/code\u003e, and write to the bundle. The CSRF token, Origin/Host allow-list, and \u003ccode\u003e--public\u003c/code\u003e ack gate that protect the HTTP surface do \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e constrain a callback registered through this seam — they guard the \u003cem\u003enetwork\u003c/em\u003e boundary, and the callback is \u003cem\u003ein-process\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePractical implications:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA malicious harness extension can execute arbitrary Python in the server process.\u003c/strong\u003e Treat any code that calls \u003ccode\u003estudio.bus.subscribe(cb)\u003c/code\u003e the same way you would treat code that calls \u003ccode\u003eeval()\u003c/code\u003e on the server: only register callbacks from code you trust. okf-loom does not sandbox the callback for you.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWhen embedding in a larger harness\u003c/strong\u003e (opencode / Claude Code / Codex / LangGraph / a custom agent), do \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e forward untrusted network input directly into a callback. If you need to expose bus events to an untrusted consumer, use the queue form (\u003ccode\u003ebus.subscribe()\u003c/code\u003e with no callback) and serialize events over a boundary you control (a pipe, a file, an HTTP endpoint with its own auth).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSandbox if possible.\u003c/strong\u003e If you have a reason to register an untrusted callback (e.g. a user-supplied plugin), run it in a subprocess or a \u003ccode\u003emultiprocessing\u003c/code\u003e-isolated worker and proxy events to it. Do not rely on Python's \"no real sandbox\" \u003ccode\u003eexec\u003c/code\u003e restrictions.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eException behavior.\u003c/strong\u003e The worker thread that invokes your callback \u003cstrong\u003eswallows exceptions by design\u003c/strong\u003e — a buggy callback must never kill the event bus (§13.8 robustness). Swallowed exceptions are logged to \u003cstrong\u003estderr\u003c/strong\u003e with the prefix \u003ccode\u003e[okf-callback]\u003c/code\u003e so they are not silent. Redirect the server process's stderr to your log collector to capture them:\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e   scripts/okf-loom serve /path/to/bundle 2\u0026gt;\u0026gt;/var/log/okf-callbacks.log\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf you want exceptions to surface more aggressively (e.g. fail a test suite), wrap your callback:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003e   _seen = []\n   def safe_cb(event):\n       try:\n           my_logic(event)\n       except Exception as e:\n           _seen.append(e)   # assert on _seen in your test\n\n   sub = studio.bus.subscribe(callback=safe_cb)\n   # ... after the test:\n   assert not _seen, f\"callback raised: {_seen}\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe single-source guarantee is: \u003cstrong\u003ethe bundle cannot register a callback (it has no Python surface in the server); only the harness that owns the server process can.\u003c/strong\u003e If you trust the harness, you trust its callbacks.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch5 id=\"the-17-library-api-all-names-implemented\"\u003eThe §17 library API (all names implemented)\u003c/h5\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe HTTP layer is a thin wrapper over these — one implementation, whoever the caller is. Use them when you embed the studio in-process instead of shelling out to the CLI:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eMethod\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eHTTP equivalent\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003ePurpose\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.save_concept(*, concept_id, raw, actor=\"agent\", action=\"write_concept\", origin=\"mutator\", group_id=None, expected_rev=None, summary=None, detail=None, undoable=True, emit_graph=None, path=None, publish=True) -\u0026gt; WriteResult\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__apply\u003c/code\u003e (per-op)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe single internal atomic write path.\u003c/strong\u003e Validates before write, snapshots for undo, atomically writes, appends a row to \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e, broadcasts \u003ccode\u003echanged\u003c/code\u003e (+ \u003ccode\u003egraph\u003c/code\u003e for graph-affecting ops). Raises / returns a conflict on \u003ccode\u003eexpected_rev\u003c/code\u003e mismatch (§9.3/§9.4).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.post_presence(*, actor=\"agent\", state=\"idle\", focus=None) -\u0026gt; dict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__presence\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSet agent presence (current spec §12). State ∈ \u003ccode\u003eidle\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ewatching\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ethinking\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eediting\u003c/code\u003e. Broadcasts a \u003ccode\u003epresence\u003c/code\u003e event.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.post_comment(*, concept, body, anchor=None, actor=\"user\", detail=None) -\u0026gt; dict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAppend a user comment / ask to \u003ccode\u003edirectives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e (§9). Returns the new directive.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.resolve_comment(comment_id, *, reply=None, activity_ids=None, actor=\"agent\") -\u0026gt; dict | None\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e(CLI: \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-resolve\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eMark a comment \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e with optional reply + activity links (drives group undo, §12.5).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.record_activity(*, actor, action, ids, summary, origin=\"mutator\", undoable=False, group_id=None, detail=None, emit_graph=None) -\u0026gt; dict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e(SSE \u003ccode\u003eactivity\u003c/code\u003e event)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAppend an \u003ccode\u003eactivity\u003c/code\u003e event row to \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e and broadcast it. Use for actions that don't write a concept file but should still show on the change list.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.events_append(event, *, publish=True) -\u0026gt; dict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e(writer helper)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe low-level append every other method uses. Adds the \u003ccode\u003eid\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ets\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eseq\u003c/code\u003e, takes the advisory file lock, writes one JSON line to \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e, optionally broadcasts. Use this only if you need a fully custom event.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.post_suggestion(*, concept, action, args, summary, group_id=None, actor=\"agent\") -\u0026gt; dict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e(SSE \u003ccode\u003esuggestions\u003c/code\u003e event)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOnly under a user's opt-in \u003ccode\u003epropose_only\u003c/code\u003e constraint\u003c/strong\u003e (§12.3). Appends a \u003ccode\u003ePlannedAction\u003c/code\u003e envelope to \u003ccode\u003eproposals.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e instead of writing. Absent by default.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePlus \u003ccode\u003estudio.list_comments(...)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.get_comment(id)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.update_comment(id, …)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.set_presence(...)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.get_presence()\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.read_events(since=None, limit=None, actor=None, concept=None)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.snapshot_for_undo(...)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.restore_snapshot(...)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.undo_group(group_id)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.mark_logged(id)\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estudio.current_rev(cid)\u003c/code\u003e, and the module-level \u003ccode\u003ewait_for_work(bundle_root, *, kinds=..., since=..., timeout=..., interval=...)\u003c/code\u003e (the same loop \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e runs).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch5 id=\"client-side-extension-windowokfloomstudioregisterkind-config\"\u003eClient-side extension: \u003ccode\u003ewindow.okfLoomStudio.register(kind, config)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/h5\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe browser studio exposes an additive, CSP-safe JavaScript extension seam (current spec §15) mirroring the server \u003ccode\u003eViewerPlugin\u003c/code\u003e intent but running fully client-side after the page boots. \u003ccode\u003epanel\u003c/code\u003e (add a slide-over panel + studio-bar toggle; the built-in Comments / Changes / Agent activity panels use it) and \u003ccode\u003eviewMode\u003c/code\u003e (add a button to the Rendered/Source/Split switch) ship wired; \u003ccode\u003etoolbar\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egraphDecorator\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003esuggestionRenderer\u003c/code\u003e are reserved (accepted + \u003ccode\u003econsole.warn\u003c/code\u003e, not wired). Load a \u003ccode\u003eregister(...)\u003c/code\u003e extension from a \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/viewer/static/*.js\u003c/code\u003e override or eval it from your harness after the studio boots. See \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf_loom/viewer/OVERRIDES.md\u003c/code\u003e §6 for the full API and worked panel/view-mode examples.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch5 id=\"the-bundle-on-disk-is-the-bus\"\u003eThe bundle-on-disk is the bus\u003c/h5\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio is \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e the source of truth — the \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e files are. The studio is the \u003cstrong\u003efan-out + attribution + undo\u003c/strong\u003e layer over them. Every write goes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode\u003eyour code ──▶ studio.save_concept ──▶ atomic write of \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/\u0026lt;id\u0026gt;.md\n                                       │\n                                       ▼\n                            .okf-loom/session/events.jsonl  (one row per write)\n                                       │\n                            ┌──────────┴───────────┐\n                            ▼                      ▼\n                    EventBus.publish        _BundleWatcher detects\n                            │                mtime change, diffs the\n                            ▼                ContentIndex, and (if the\n                    SSE /__events           write didn't log itself)\n                    fan-out to every         appends an origin:\"disk\"\n                    open tab + every         event — so the feed is\n                    in-process               complete regardless of\n                    subscriber                which path produced it.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor an embedded harness this means: writes via \u003ccode\u003esave_concept\u003c/code\u003e (or the CLI mutators) → \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e → SSE + \u003ccode\u003eEventBus\u003c/code\u003e fan-out, all from the same files a \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e would tail. A second harness process embedding the same bundle sees the same events through the file bus — no IPC beyond the filesystem. This is what keeps the studio headless-friendly (§1.9 of the current spec) and lets the agent run externally while the studio runs in-process for the user's browser.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"4d-what-to-expose-for-the-agent-loop\"\u003e4d — What to expose for the agent loop\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAt minimum, expose for the studio loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt; --no-open\u003c/code\u003e — bring up the live studio (hand the user the URL).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt; --emit jsonl [--auto-repair]\u003c/code\u003e — the headless change feed that drives proactive enrichment (§11).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe mutators (\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eentity-add\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003eupdate\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003erepair\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003ewrite-concept\u003c/code\u003e) — how the agent actually authors files in response to comments and the watch feed.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__presence\u003c/code\u003e (or a write to \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/presence.json\u003c/code\u003e) — so the user can see what their teammate is doing.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"harness-specific-recipes\"\u003eHarness-specific recipes\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"opencode\"\u003eopencode\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://opencode.ai\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003eopencode\u003c/a\u003e discovers project-scoped agents and skills under \u003ccode\u003e.opencode/\u003c/code\u003e and an \u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e at the repo root. To wire okf-loom into an opencode project:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClone or vendor this repository\u003c/strong\u003e into the agent's workspace. The repo skill layout is the artifact; do not depend on package installation.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExpose the root skill\u003c/strong\u003e under \u003ccode\u003e.opencode/skill/okf-loom/\u003c/code\u003e (or keep the vendored checkout there). The skill directory must include \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eresources/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003escripts/\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003edocs-bundle/\u003c/code\u003e together:\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode\u003e   .opencode/skill/okf-loom/\n   ├── SKILL.md\n   ├── resources/\n   ├── scripts/\n   └── docs-bundle/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eopencode's skill loader will surface it; the resolver matches on the \u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e triggers (e.g. \"okf\", \"validate okf\", \"knowledge bundle\").\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCopy or include \u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e from this repository to your project root only if your harness starts from AGENTS files. It points back to \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eScope a subagent\u003c/strong\u003e for OKF work (\u003ccode\u003e.opencode/agent/okf-curator.md\u003c/code\u003e):\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e   ---\n   description: Curates, validates, and updates OKF bundles. Use for\n     \"okf\", \"validate knowledge\", \"discover missing links\", \"update\n     okf bundle\", \"stand up okf viewer\".\n   mode: subagent\n   tools:\n     bash: true\n     read: true\n     write: true\n     edit: true\n   ---\n   You are the OKF curator. Always load `okf-loom/SKILL.md` first,\n   then read the focused resource for the task (`resources/format-basics.md`,\n   `resources/authoring.md`, `resources/advanced-operations.md`, or\n   `resources/studio-agent-loop.md`). Use the checked-in helper:\n   `/path/to/okf-loom/scripts/okf-loom`.\n   Run `scripts/okf-loom validate` from inside the checkout, or `okf-loom/scripts/okf-loom validate` from a parent workspace, before claiming completion; run `discover` to find\n   gaps; apply suggestions via `update --plan`. Never bulk-convert existing\n   content without user confirmation.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePermission scoping\u003c/strong\u003e (opencode \u003ccode\u003epermission.bash\u003c/code\u003e patterns):\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-json\"\u003e   {\n     \"permission\": {\n       \"bash\": {\n         \"scripts/okf-loom validate *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom info *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom discover *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom graph *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom search *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom capabilities *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom render *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom build *\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom index * --dry-run\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom index *\": \"ask\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom log * --dry-run\": \"allow\",\n          \"scripts/okf-loom log *\": \"ask\",\n         \"scripts/okf-loom update * --dry-run\": \"allow\",\n         \"scripts/okf-loom update *\": \"ask\",\n         \"scripts/okf-loom serve *\": \"ask\"\n       }\n     }\n   }\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"claude-code\"\u003eClaude Code\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eClaude Code reads \u003ccode\u003eCLAUDE.md\u003c/code\u003e at the repo root and skills under \u003ccode\u003e.claude/skills/\u003c/code\u003e. The shape mirrors opencode:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eCopy or symlink root \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e into the harness skill directory.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eCopy the \u003ccode\u003eresources/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003escripts/\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003edocs-bundle/\u003c/code\u003e folders alongside it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eClaude Code's skill/resource discovery will surface the skill when the user mentions OKF / \"knowledge bundle\" / \"validate okf\" etc.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"codex-openai\"\u003eCodex (OpenAI)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCodex reads \u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e at the repo root (the same file opencode uses). Skill conventions vary; the simplest path:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e at repo root (already in this repository; copy verbatim).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eReference \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e from \u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e so Codex reads the root skill and resources when relevant. If auto-discovery is unavailable, an explicit \u003ccode\u003eload okf-loom/SKILL.md when the user asks about OKF\u003c/code\u003e line works well.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"langgraph\"\u003eLangGraph\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWrap the CLI in tool functions:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-python\"\u003efrom langchain_core.tools import tool\nimport subprocess, json, pathlib\n\ndef _okf(*args):\n    # The repo ships no installed console script; shell out to the checkout path.\n    r = subprocess.run([\"okf-loom/scripts/okf-loom\", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)\n    return r.stdout\n\n@tool\ndef okf_validate(bundle_path: str) -\u0026gt; dict:\n    \"\"\"Validate an OKF bundle. Returns conformance report JSON.\"\"\"\n    return json.loads(_okf(\"validate\", bundle_path, \"--format\", \"json\"))\n\n@tool\ndef okf_discover(bundle_path: str) -\u0026gt; dict:\n    \"\"\"Find missing links/indexes/descriptions/relations/orphans in an OKF bundle.\"\"\"\n    return json.loads(_okf(\"discover\", bundle_path, \"--format\", \"json\"))\n\n@tool\ndef okf_update(bundle_path: str, plan_path: str, dry_run: bool = False) -\u0026gt; dict:\n    \"\"\"Apply an OKF update plan (add link/tag/relation/section). Idempotent.\"\"\"\n    args = [\"update\", bundle_path, \"--plan\", plan_path, \"--format\", \"json\"]\n    if dry_run:\n        args.append(\"--dry-run\")\n    return json.loads(_okf(*args))\n\n@tool\ndef okf_search(bundle_path: str, query: str, mode: str = \"lexical\", limit: int = 10) -\u0026gt; list:\n    \"\"\"Search an OKF bundle. mode ∈ {lexical, semantic, hybrid, tag}.\"\"\"\n    return json.loads(_okf(\"search\", bundle_path, query, \"--mode\", mode,\n                           \"--limit\", str(limit), \"--format\", \"json\"))\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWire these into your graph's tools list. The agent will reach for them when the user mentions knowledge / docs / catalogs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"mcp-server-model-context-protocol\"\u003eMCP server (model context protocol)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe CLI is shaped for an MCP wrapper. A minimal MCP server exposes \u003ccode\u003eokf_validate\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf_discover\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf_update\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf_search\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf_render\u003c/code\u003e as tools. The \u003ccode\u003e--format json\u003c/code\u003e outputs are already JSON-serialisable. (There is no in-repo MCP server today; wrap the CLI as shown.)\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch4 id=\"custom-agent-any-language\"\u003eCustom agent (any language)\u003c/h4\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a non-Python agent, the \u003cstrong\u003eCLI subprocess\u003c/strong\u003e shape works from any language. Construct the argv, run, parse \u003ccode\u003e--format json\u003c/code\u003e stdout. Treat okf-loom like \u003ccode\u003egit\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003erg\u003c/code\u003e: a standard Unix CLI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr /\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"what-to-expose-to-your-agent\"\u003eWhat to expose to your agent\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAt minimum, expose these five commands as agent-callable tools (the \"trigger list\" the agent uses to decide when OKF is relevant):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate\u003c/code\u003e — for any \"validate / check / lint\" intent.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom discover\u003c/code\u003e — for any \"what's missing / find gaps / improve\" intent.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom update\u003c/code\u003e — for applying the agent's proposed fixes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom search\u003c/code\u003e — for any \"find / show me / where is\" intent over the knowledge.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e — for any \"show me / browse / open the wiki\" intent.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe agent note (\u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e) is the routing layer — it tells the agent WHEN to reach for OKF (the trigger list) and points to the skills for HOW.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"testing-your-embedding\"\u003eTesting your embedding\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhatever shape you pick, verify:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRound-trip safety.\u003c/strong\u003e Apply a no-op update plan to a bundle; the bundle's content should be unchanged (modulo YAML whitespace).\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIdempotency.\u003c/strong\u003e Apply the same plan twice; the second run reports \u003ccode\u003eapplied:0, skipped:N\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStrict mode in CI.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate --strict\u003c/code\u003e should fail the build on warnings.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHot-swap.\u003c/strong\u003e In Shape 3, mutate the bundle on disk, swap \u003ccode\u003ehttpd.bundle\u003c/code\u003e, hit \u003ccode\u003e/\u003c/code\u003e again; the new content should appear.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003esamples/demo_bundle/\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003esamples/showcase/\u003c/code\u003e directories are good test corpora.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"reference\"\u003eReference\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eCurrent okf-loom spec: \u003ca href=\"/reference/spec.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003espec.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eUpstream base OKF SPEC v0.1: \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003ehttps://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAgent note: \u003ca href=\"../../AGENTS.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e../../AGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eSkill resources: \u003ca href=\"../../resources/\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e../../resources/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eArchitecture: \u003ca href=\"/reference/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003earchitecture.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eResearch: \u003ca href=\"/explanation/research.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresearch.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eOverride examples: \u003ca href=\"../../scripts/okf_loom/viewer/OVERRIDES.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e../../scripts/okf_loom/viewer/OVERRIDES.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e", "reference/frontmatter": "\u003ch2 id=\"frontmatter-contract\"\u003eFrontmatter contract\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEvery OKF concept is a markdown file whose body is preceded by a YAML frontmatter block delimited by \u003ccode\u003e---\u003c/code\u003e lines. The contract is defined by SPEC §4.1 and enforced by \u003ca href=\"cli.md#validate\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e. See \u003ca href=\"/reference/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eindex.md\u003c/a\u003e for the rest of the reference quadrant.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA minimal conformant concept:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: Reference\n---\n\n# Body\n\nFree markdown.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThat is the entire hard requirement: parseable YAML and a non-empty \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e. Everything else in this document is recommendation or convention.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"keys\"\u003eKeys\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"required\"\u003eRequired\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eKey\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eType\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eNotes\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003estring\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eREQUIRED by SPEC §9.\u003c/strong\u003e Short string naming the kind of thing (e.g. \u003ccode\u003eTable\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eAPI Endpoint\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTutorial\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eReference\u003c/code\u003e). Not centrally registered; consumers tolerate unknown types. The only hard-required key.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"recommended\"\u003eRecommended\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eKey\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eType\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eDefault\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eNotes\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003estring\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003efilename stem (underscores → spaces)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eHuman display name. Index generators and the viewer use it.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003estring\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eempty\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne-line summary. Used by index generators and search snippets.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresource\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003estring (URI)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eabsent\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCanonical URI of the underlying asset. Absent for abstract concepts.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003elist of strings\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eempty\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCross-cutting themes. Must be a YAML list.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003estring (ISO 8601)\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eabsent\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eLast-modified datetime. Quote it (see YAML gotchas).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eMissing recommended keys surface as \u003ccode\u003eWARNING\u003c/code\u003e findings under the default \u003ccode\u003espec\u003c/code\u003e profile; they become \u003ccode\u003eERROR\u003c/code\u003e under the \u003ccode\u003eproducer\u003c/code\u003e profile (see \u003ca href=\"cli.md#validate\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003ecli.md § validate\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"custom-keys-spec-2-round-trip\"\u003eCustom keys (SPEC §2 round-trip)\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eProducers MAY add arbitrary keys. Consumers — including okf-loom — MUST preserve them verbatim on round-trip. okf-loom preserves frontmatter key order and unknown keys through every parse → modify → serialize cycle.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSeveral custom keys are recognised by the \u003ca href=\"capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003ecapability registry\u003c/a\u003e and activate capabilities by their presence (auto-activation):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eCustom key\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eActivates\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003erelations\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.typed_relations\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eentities\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.entities\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ealiases\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.aliases\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eprovenance\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.provenance\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecitations\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf.cap.citations\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eExample combining recommended + custom keys:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e---\ntype: API Endpoint\ntitle: Create Order\ndescription: POST a new order to the checkout service.\nresource: https://api.example.com/v2/orders\ntags: [checkout, write-api, v2]\ntimestamp: \"2026-06-15T10:00:00Z\"\nrelations:\n  - target: services/checkout\n    type: implemented_by\n    detail: POST handler in checkout service\nentities:\n  - id: entity/order\n    label: Order\n    kind: business_entity\n    aliases: [purchase, transaction]\ncitations:\n  - id: \"1\"\n    text: \"Internal data dictionary\"\n    url: https://wiki.example.com/data/orders\nowner: team-checkout\nsla_tier: \"1\"\n---\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"reserved-filename-frontmatter\"\u003eReserved filename frontmatter\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eFile\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eFrontmatter allowed?\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBundle-root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYes — but only \u003ccode\u003eokf_version\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eokf_extensions\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egenerated\u003c/code\u003e. SPEC §6 / §11.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eNon-root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo.\u003c/strong\u003e Pure directory listing.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo.\u003c/strong\u003e SPEC §7 structure only.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAny other \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eYes — the full frontmatter contract applies.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA bundle-root \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e declaring capabilities:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e---\nokf_version: \"0.1\"\nokf_extensions:\n  - okf.cap.typed_relations\n  - okf.cap.entities\ngenerated: true\n---\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"links.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003elinks.md\u003c/a\u003e for the link contract and \u003ca href=\"capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003ecapabilities.md\u003c/a\u003e for the opt-in mechanisms.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"yaml-gotchas\"\u003eYAML gotchas\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYAML 1.1 (the dialect PyYAML implements by default) silently coerces unquoted scalars. okf-loom's validator downgrades \u003ccode\u003etimestamp_validity\u003c/code\u003e findings to WARNING, but the underlying parse is still lossy. Quote the following:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"timestamps\"\u003eTimestamps\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYAML parses unquoted ISO dates as \u003ccode\u003edatetime.datetime\u003c/code\u003e, not as a string.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e# BAD — parses as datetime, not a string; round-trip may reformat it.\ntimestamp: 2026-06-29T00:00:00Z\n\n# GOOD — preserved as a literal string.\ntimestamp: \"2026-06-29T00:00:00Z\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis applies to any key carrying a datetime: \u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupdated_at\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecreated_at\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eprovenance.collected_at\u003c/code\u003e, etc.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"version-like-strings\"\u003eVersion-like strings\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYAML parses \u003ccode\u003e1.10\u003c/code\u003e as float \u003ccode\u003e1.1\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e3.0\u003c/code\u003e as float \u003ccode\u003e3.0\u003c/code\u003e. Quote anything that must round-trip verbatim.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e# BAD — `1.10` becomes `1.1`; `3.0` becomes `3.0` (lossy on round-trip).\nversion: 1.10\nbigquery_dataset_version: 3.0\n\n# GOOD\nversion: \"1.10\"\nbigquery_dataset_version: \"3.0\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe same applies to numeric ids (\u003ccode\u003eid: \"0007\"\u003c/code\u003e) and SLA tiers (\u003ccode\u003esla_tier: \"1\"\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"booleans\"\u003eBooleans\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYAML 1.1 treats \u003ccode\u003eyes\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eno\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eon\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eoff\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e (case-insensitive) as booleans. A tag literally named \u003ccode\u003eno\u003c/code\u003e becomes \u003ccode\u003eFalse\u003c/code\u003e. Quote any string that coincides with a boolean token if you mean it as text.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e# BAD — `no` becomes boolean False.\ntags: [yes, no, maybe]\n\n# GOOD\ntags: [\"yes\", \"no\", \"maybe\"]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNote: \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e accepts the boolean tokens for genuine boolean fields (see \u003ca href=\"config_yaml.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003econfig_yaml.md\u003c/a\u003e § Boolean coercion), but the same rule does not apply to free-form frontmatter strings.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"tags-must-be-a-list\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e must be a list\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSPEC §4.1 implies a list. okf-loom tolerates a scalar tag, but the canonical form is a YAML list.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e# BAD — a comma-separated string. Parses as one tag named \"a, b, c\".\ntags: a, b, c\n\n# GOOD — flow form.\ntags: [a, b, c]\n\n# GOOD — block form.\ntags:\n  - a\n  - b\n  - c\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"trailing-whitespace-and-newlines\"\u003eTrailing whitespace and newlines\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom normalises trailing whitespace to a single trailing newline on write. Do not expect byte-identical round-trip if you hand-format YAML; semantic identity is preserved.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"aliases-and-merge-keys\"\u003eAliases and merge keys\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom's YAML loader (\u003ccode\u003e_NodeLimitedSafeLoader\u003c/code\u003e) disables alias/anchor construction and merge keys as a DoS guard. Frontmatter must be fully materialised; you cannot \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;\u0026lt;: *base\u003c/code\u003e to share blocks.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"round-trip-guarantees\"\u003eRound-trip guarantees\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom guarantees the following through every parse → modify → serialize cycle (the \u003ccode\u003eroundtrip.py\u003c/code\u003e module):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eProperty\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eGuarantee\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUnknown keys\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePreserved verbatim.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eKey order\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePreserved (the \u003ccode\u003e_FmEntry\u003c/code\u003e ordered representation).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e value\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePreserved exactly.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRecommended keys when set\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePreserved exactly.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eList values\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOrder preserved.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eInline vs block style\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe dumper emits block style for nested structures; simple scalars stay inline.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eTrailing whitespace\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eNormalised to a single trailing newline.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"validation\"\u003eValidation\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun \u003ca href=\"cli.md#validate\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e to surface frontmatter findings. Useful check subsets:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --checks concept_required_keys,concept_recommended_keys\nscripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --checks timestamp_validity\nscripts/okf-loom validate path/to/bundle --profile producer   # recommended keys → ERROR\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe check categories that touch frontmatter:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eCheck\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCategory\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept.missing_type\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept_required_keys\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept.missing_recommended_keys\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept_recommended_keys\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept.unknown_type\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept_recommended_keys\u003c/code\u003e (WARNING)\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept.bad_timestamp\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etimestamp_validity\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econcept.tag_normalization\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etag_normalization\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"http-server-routes\"\u003eHTTP server routes\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e runs a \u003ccode\u003eThreadingHTTPServer\u003c/code\u003e with the \u003ccode\u003eOKFWikiHandler\u003c/code\u003e request handler. The handler serves read routes unconditionally and — when a studio session is live (\u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e exists) — accepts mutating POST routes behind a per-session CSRF token and an Origin/Host allow-list. See \u003ca href=\"/reference/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eindex.md\u003c/a\u003e for the rest of the reference quadrant.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eDefault bind is \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1:8787\u003c/code\u003e. A non-loopback bind (\u003ccode\u003e--public\u003c/code\u003e or a non-loopback \u003ccode\u003e--host\u003c/code\u003e) requires \u003ccode\u003e--public-ack\u003c/code\u003e or an interactive y/N ack.
