It rewrites only tool-managed root indexes or marked regions delimited by \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;!-- okf:generated:index begin --\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;!-- okf:generated:index end --\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003elog\u003c/code\u003e appends to \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e newest-first and preserves existing entries.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom init\u003c/code\u003e scaffolds a new bundle with \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom bootstrap\u003c/code\u003e scaffolds a simpler bundle without config. Both refuse unsafe destructive assumptions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eDerived JSON indexes are optional and disposable:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom index docs-bundle --emit-json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis writes generated artifacts under \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/index/\u003c/code\u003e such as \u003ccode\u003econtent.json\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003egraph.json\u003c/code\u003e. They contain no absolute host paths, carry \u003ccode\u003egenerated_by: \"okf-loom\"\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eformat_version: 1\u003c/code\u003e, and should be safe to delete and regenerate. Bundles should normally gitignore \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/index/\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"9-viewer-build-and-static-outputs\"\u003e9. Viewer, build, and static outputs\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAll viewer targets share the same \u003ccode\u003eContentIndex\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTheme defaults have one configuration contract. \u003ccode\u003estudio.theme\u003c/code\u003e in \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e accepts \u003ccode\u003eauto\u003c/code\u003e plus the concrete \u003ccode\u003eswiss-light\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eswiss-dark\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etechnical-light\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003etechnical-dark\u003c/code\u003e themes. The narrower \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/viewer/config.json\u003c/code\u003e surface accepts the four concrete themes only. Both surfaces reject retired names with contextual replacements (\u003ccode\u003elight\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003etechnical-light\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edark\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003emidnight\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003etechnical-dark\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003epastel\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003esepia\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003eswiss-light\u003c/code\u003e); returning users' saved browser preferences are migrated separately. Invalid viewer JSON never silently falls back: malformed JSON, a non-object top level, unknown keys, wrong types, empty values, and unsupported layout/theme values are errors. When both surfaces configure a theme for the same served page, the viewer JSON value — the one the server paints into \u003ccode\u003edata-theme\u003c/code\u003e — is authoritative; \u003ccode\u003estudio.theme\u003c/code\u003e applies only when the viewer surface leaves the theme unconfigured (explicit \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e equals omission), and its \u003ccode\u003eauto\u003c/code\u003e default carries no preference. A saved user preference overrides the validated configured initial value; otherwise the configured value applies, then Swiss Auto/OS fallback. The concrete resolved Auto value is derived and is not configuration or persisted preference state. Browsers persist the two orthogonal preferences under \u003ccode\u003eokf-theme-family\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eswiss\u003c/code\u003e | \u003ccode\u003etechnical\u003c/code\u003e) and \u003ccode\u003eokf-theme-mode\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eauto\u003c/code\u003e | \u003ccode\u003elight\u003c/code\u003e | \u003ccode\u003edark\u003c/code\u003e); the retired \u003ccode\u003eokf-theme\u003c/code\u003e key is migrated once and afterwards kept only as a write-only compatibility mirror of explicit concrete choices (removed while Auto). One shared client asset (\u003ccode\u003etheme.js\u003c/code\u003e) owns this state in every viewer output and announces each actual resolved change as a single \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom:themeChanged\u003c/code\u003e event.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eTarget\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCommand\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eUse\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eLive studio / server\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eInteractive browsing, comments, agent loop, SSE updates.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSPA build\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ebuild --target spa\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePublished rich reading experience.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eStatic build\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ebuild --target static\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eJS-optional, printable, SEO/air-gapped output.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSingle-file build\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ebuild --target single-file\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePortable artifact for tickets, email, or local sharing.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne-file render\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003erender\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSelf-contained viewer artifact.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eExamples:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom serve docs-bundle --no-open\nscripts/okf-loom serve docs-bundle --no-open --tunnel   # + public https URL (cloudflared)\nscripts/okf-loom build docs-bundle --target static --out /tmp/okf-docs-site\nscripts/okf-loom render docs-bundle --out /tmp/viz.html\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe current viewer surface (binding for rebuilds): the root index renders as a dashboard — hero stat chips (concepts/types/links), an Explore-the-graph entry point, and every concept as a type-grouped card with link counts and tags. Concept pages carry a type-tinted header band (icon, reading time, entity chips, typed relation chips), a full-width rendered body, connection cards for outgoing/incoming links, and a scroll-spy section rail. The graph view uses fCoSE with per-type node icons; its controls are a lens bar pinned at the top of the right-hand detail pane. Each lens answers one question with a real algorithm (see \u003ccode\u003edocs/design/graph-lenses.md\u003c/code\u003e for the evidence base): Map (deterministic Louvain communities as colour + PageRank as size), Themes (strong community grouping + ranked theme digest), Flow (dagre layered layout over directed/typed edges, falling back to directed breadthfirst), Bridges (betweenness centrality as colour/size + ranked bridgers), Recent (frontmatter-timestamp recency ramp), and Focus (neighbourhood isolation with a depth control). Every lens renders a clickable ranked summary with a one-line verdict in the detail pane; an Advanced disclosure holds spacing sliders, the type filter, a relationship-label toggle, and a 'Colour by theme' toggle (the Saket et al. 2014 escape hatch back to type colours). The selected concept's page renders beneath the bar with the same progressive renderers (mermaid/KaTeX/highlight.js) as the wiki pages. Hover previews, shift-click path tracing, keyboard navigation, clickable legend type filters, deterministic layouts, and live SSE canvas updates are part of the contract. \u003ccode\u003eserve --tunnel\u003c/code\u003e starts a Cloudflare quick tunnel, prints the public URL, and injects the tunnel hostname into the studio's runtime \u003ccode\u003eallowed_hosts\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom tunnel \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e attaches the same quick tunnel to an ALREADY RUNNING session (no restart, no lost token/undo history) by driving the token-guarded \u003ccode\u003ePOST /__tunnel\u003c/code\u003e admin route; \u003ccode\u003e--stop\u003c/code\u003e detaches it and restores the pre-tunnel allowlist, \u003ccode\u003e--status\u003c/code\u003e reports the current URL. The tunnel process always belongs to the serve process and dies with it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eActive viewer code has a two-layer gate. The bundle must declare \u003ccode\u003eviewer.allow_active_code: true\u003c/code\u003e, and the operator must also consent with \u003ccode\u003e--allow-active-code\u003c/code\u003e or a truthy \u003ccode\u003eOKF_LOOM_ALLOW_ACTIVE_CODE\u003c/code\u003e. Default is off.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"10-live-collaborative-studio-model\"\u003e10. Live collaborative studio model\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e opens the live collaborative studio by default. The studio is a local single-user admin tool. The user directs; the external agent authors.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCore posture:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe bundle on disk is the source of truth and the bus.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe browser is a rendered/source/split reading and directing surface.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe user does not directly edit Markdown in the browser by default.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe user's studio writes are comments and asks.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe server embeds no LLM and runs no agent reasoning.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe external agent watches comments/events and writes through CLI mutators or whitelisted apply paths.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThere is no per-write approval gate by default.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eTransparency, change list, validation, atomic writes, and undo are the safety net.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eOpt-in constraints belong to the user under \u003ccode\u003estudio.constraints\u003c/code\u003e; empty constraints mean a fully free agent.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe canonical bring-up loop is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom serve path/to/bundle --no-open \u0026amp;\nuntil scripts/okf-loom token path/to/bundle \u0026gt;/dev/null 2\u0026gt;\u0026amp;1; do sleep 0.2; done\nscripts/okf-loom wait path/to/bundle --for comment\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe agent then claims the comment, writes via mutators, resolves the comment, and waits again. After starting a background server, always wait for token readiness before the first mutating POST or studio-aware CLI mutator.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/live_studio_basics.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/tutorials/live_studio_basics.md\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\u003c/a\u003e, and \u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/explanation/live_studio_design.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"11-live-protocols-and-event-schema\"\u003e11. Live protocols and event schema\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe live server is stdlib HTTP plus REST and Server-Sent Events. There are no WebSockets.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eKey routes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eRoute\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003ePurpose\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /__data/doc?id=\u0026lt;concept_id\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eOne concept's \u003ccode\u003e{rev, html, raw, frontmatter, backlinks, outgoing, headings}\u003c/code\u003e for in-place patching.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /__data/events?since=\u0026amp;limit=\u0026amp;actor=\u0026amp;concept=\u0026amp;order=\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eFiltered change-list read over \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /__events\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSSE stream of live frames.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /__comments\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCanonical comment state from \u003ccode\u003edirectives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /__diff\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eToken-protected diff between saved revisions.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /\u0026lt;path\u0026gt;.\u0026lt;media ext\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBundle-local media file (image/video/PDF allowlist).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUser comment or threaded reply.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment-update\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUser-facing lifecycle/archive transition, or a body edit of a not-yet-resolved comment.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__presence\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAgent presence update (\u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003efocus\u003c/code\u003e, optional free-text \u003ccode\u003emessage\u003c/code\u003e ≤200 chars).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__apply\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhitelisted update operation.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__undo\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSingle or group undo.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__preview\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRender capped in-flight Markdown.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__tunnel\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eServer admin: attach/detach/status a quick tunnel at runtime (\u003ccode\u003eaction: start|stop|status\u003c/code\u003e). Exempt from \u003ccode\u003e--no-edit\u003c/code\u003e (sharing a kiosk is the use case) but never from the token + Origin/Host guard.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBundle-local media serving is contract-bound: only an allowlisted media extension routes to the file handler; the file must be reachable by the §5 scan (the same exclude/include/gitignore semantics as concept discovery) and its resolved path must stay inside the bundle root. Responses are sandboxed (bundle media is user content) and carry an ETag for revalidation. Static builds copy the same §5-visible media set so exports render identically to the live studio.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEvent rows are JSON objects with server-stamped \u003ccode\u003eid\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ets\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eseq\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003erev\u003c/code\u003e when persisted. Common frame types include \u003ccode\u003eready\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003echanged\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecreated\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eremoved\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egraph\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003epresence\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment_link\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eactivity\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eping\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eresync\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecomment_link\u003c/code\u003e is current behavior. When resolving a comment with activity ids, the studio appends a back-link event carrying \u003ccode\u003eactivity_id\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment_id\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003econcept\u003c/code\u003e so the change list can show which comment produced a change.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePolling fallback and replay ordering are part of the contract. \u003ccode\u003e/__data/events\u003c/code\u003e defaults to newest-first for the change list. When a client supplies \u003ccode\u003esince\u003c/code\u003e, replay must use \u003ccode\u003eorder=asc\u003c/code\u003e so missed events are consumed oldest-to-newest after the cursor. Newest-first reads are for initial history and activity panels, not cursor replay.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/http_routes.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"12-comment-lifecycle-and-agent-loop\"\u003e12. Comment lifecycle and agent loop\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eComments are directives stored in \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/directives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e. They drive the user-directs / agent-authors loop.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe lifecycle state is independent from archive visibility:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eField\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eValues\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eopen\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edismissed\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earchived\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eState ownership:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eUsers create comments with \u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAgents claim comments with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-claim\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAgents reply mid-thread with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-reply\u003c/code\u003e — the clarifying-question channel. The reply is threaded under the root, posted with \u003ccode\u003estate=resolved\u003c/code\u003e (a statement, not an ask) so \u003ccode\u003ewait\u003c/code\u003e never returns the agent its own reply, and the parent's lifecycle state is untouched: reply-without-resolve is the point.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAgents resolve comments with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-resolve\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eUsers dismiss or reopen comments with \u003ccode\u003e/__comment-update\u003c/code\u003e, and may edit the body of a not-yet-resolved comment (\u003ccode\u003e/__comment-update\u003c/code\u003e with \u003ccode\u003ebody\u003c/code\u003e); the edit bumps \u003ccode\u003eupdated_at\u003c/code\u003e (so a waiting agent re-receives the corrected ask) and re-derives \u003ccode\u003erequest_summary\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eArchive is a soft hide and never replaces lifecycle state.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCurrent comment records include \u003ccode\u003eid\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ets\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupdated_at\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003econcept\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eanchor\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eactor\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebody\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estate\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eclaimed_by\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eresolved_activity\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ereply\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esummary\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erequest_summary\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edetail\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003earchived\u003c/code\u003e, and optional \u003ccode\u003eparent_id\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003ets\u003c/code\u003e is immutable creation time. \u003ccode\u003eupdated_at\u003c/code\u003e bumps on claim, resolve, dismiss, reopen, archive, unarchive, reply, and summary updates. \u003ccode\u003esummary\u003c/code\u003e is the agent-authored done/status blurb; \u003ccode\u003erequest_summary\u003c/code\u003e is the ask summary.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThreading is capped at two displayed levels: parent, reply, reply-to-reply. Deeper nesting is hoisted to root. Archive is root-only and server-enforced: every comment in the thread must be \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e, otherwise archive fails. Replying to an archived thread auto-unarchives the parent. Compatibility records with \u003ccode\u003estate == \"archived\"\u003c/code\u003e are normalised on read to \u003ccode\u003earchived=true, state=\"open\"\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCanonical foreground agent loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom wait path/to/bundle --for comment\nscripts/okf-loom comment-claim path/to/bundle 01JABED9K0 --summary \"adding dependency link\"\nscripts/okf-loom comment-reply path/to/bundle 01JABED9K0 --body \"Did you mean orders or order_items?\"  # only when the ask is ambiguous\nscripts/okf-loom presence path/to/bundle --state editing --focus tables/orders --message \"linking 3 of 7 tables\"\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle path/to/bundle --source tables/orders --target tables/customers --group-id PASS1\nscripts/okf-loom comment-resolve path/to/bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n  --activity 01JABED5K7 \\\n  --reply \"Done - linked orders to customers.\" \\\n  --summary \"done: link added\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e is block-once and foreground. Do not background it; the caller is the consumer. The returned comment carries a \u003ccode\u003equeue\u003c/code\u003e field — \u003ccode\u003e{pending, ids}\u003c/code\u003e for the OTHER open comments still waiting — so the agent sees backlog depth without diffing \u003ccode\u003ecomment-list\u003c/code\u003e between loop turns; the one-work-item contract itself is unchanged. \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e is the continuous feed variant for a long-running consumer and can replay from \u003ccode\u003e--since\u003c/code\u003e before tailing live.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/cli.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"13-session-storage-undo-and-caps\"\u003e13. Session storage, undo, and caps\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eLive studio session state is derived/ephemeral and lives under \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt;/.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e by default. Recommended project hygiene is to keep \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e out of git unless a harness intentionally snapshots it for debugging.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCurrent session shape:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003ePath\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003ePurpose\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCap / invariant\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.token\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePer-session CSRF token, mode \u003ccode\u003e0600\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRegenerated by \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e; treat as secret.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserver.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRunning server address: \u003ccode\u003e{host, port, pid, started, url, tunnel_url}\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWritten by \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e at startup, refreshed on tunnel attach/detach, removed on clean shutdown. Lets \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom tunnel\u003c/code\u003e find the live port; stale after a crash (detected by the connect failing).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eActivity/change/comment/presence event feed.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eActive file cap from \u003ccode\u003estudio.events_max_bytes\u003c/code\u003e default 8 MiB; \u003ccode\u003estudio.events_keep\u003c/code\u003e default 7 rotated files.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edirectives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAppend-only comment/directive state.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eActive file cap 2 MiB; 3 files kept.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003epresence.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCurrent presence snapshot.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eStale presence recovers to idle after configured/default TTL.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehistory/\u0026lt;hex\u0026gt;/\u0026lt;rev\u0026gt;.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePer-concept undo snapshots.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRing-capped; pruned snapshots make undo return not-found/pruned status.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehistory/_groups/\u0026lt;group_id\u0026gt;/manifest.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eGroup undo manifest.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSafe tokenised group ids only.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.idempotency/\u0026lt;key\u0026gt;.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003ePOST retry cache for selected endpoints.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e10-minute TTL; max 10,000 files; unsafe keys ignored for caching.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.last-logged.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eCross-process write/event dedup.\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eInternal session bookkeeping.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePOST /__comment\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ePOST /__undo\u003c/code\u003e accept an optional \u003ccode\u003eIdempotency-Key\u003c/code\u003e header. Within the TTL, the same key and same body replay the original response and avoid duplicate directive or undo effects. The idempotency cache is opportunistically swept for TTL and file-count caps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eUndo is based on snapshots written before concept mutation. Mutators support \u003ccode\u003e--group-id\u003c/code\u003e so several writes can be undone as one pass. Every group id is path-token validated before it reaches history paths.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"14-trust-and-security-model\"\u003e14. Trust and security model\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe default trust boundary is loopback local use. \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e binds \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e by default. \u003ccode\u003e--public\u003c/code\u003e or a non-loopback host requires \u003ccode\u003e--public-ack\u003c/code\u003e or an interactive acknowledgement.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eGuards:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eEvery GET is public to the local server, except sensitive diff reads require the session token.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eEvery POST requires \u003ccode\u003eX-OKF-Token\u003c/code\u003e and Origin/Host allow-list acceptance.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003estudio.allowed_hosts\u003c/code\u003e defaults to \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003elocalhost\u003c/code\u003e and is never empty.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--no-edit\u003c/code\u003e makes the studio read-only; live reads stay on and mutating POST routes return \u003ccode\u003e403\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003ePOST /__tunnel\u003c/code\u003e is the one exemption (server admin, not a bundle write — sharing a read-only kiosk is its use case); it still requires the token and Origin/Host acceptance.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMutating bodies are JSON, size-capped, and schema-checked.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/__apply\u003c/code\u003e accepts whitelisted update operations, not shell or arbitrary argv.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePath-bearing config values must remain within the bundle root.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eActive viewer override/plugin code requires both bundle declaration and operator consent.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe server embeds no LLM and does not talk to remote model providers.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThese gates protect against other browser origins, DNS-rebinding-style abuse, malicious bundle code, accidental exposure, and data loss. They are not a per-action leash on the user's own agent.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"15-extension-api\"\u003e15. Extension API\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThere are three extension mechanisms:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eViewer file/template/static overrides under the configured viewer override directory.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eServer-side \u003ccode\u003eViewerPlugin\u003c/code\u003e hooks for render/build integration.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eClient-side studio extensions via \u003ccode\u003ewindow.okfLoomStudio.register(kind, config)\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe current shipped \u003ccode\u003eokfLoomStudio.register()\u003c/code\u003e kinds are exactly:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eKind\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCurrent status\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eContract\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003epanel\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eShips, wired\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAdds a slide-over panel and studio-bar toggle.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eviewMode\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eShips, wired\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAdds a read-only mode button to the Rendered/Source/Split switch.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etoolbar\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eReserved forward-compat\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAccepted and warned, not wired.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003egraphDecorator\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eReserved forward-compat\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAccepted and warned, not wired.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esuggestionRenderer\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eReserved forward-compat\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAccepted and warned, not wired.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReserved kinds must not be documented as usable current extension points. They are accepted so future-targeted extensions degrade gracefully today, but the studio logs a warning stating the kind is reserved and not wired.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eExample shipped panel extension:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-js\"\u003ewindow.okfLoomStudio.register(\"panel\", {\n  id: \"coverage\",\n  label: \"Coverage\",\n  render(container, ctx) {\n    container.textContent = \"Open comments: \" + ctx.state.comments.filter(c =\u0026gt; c.state === \"open\").length;\n  },\n});\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf_loom/viewer/OVERRIDES.md\u003c/code\u003e for the shipped extension reference.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"16-embedding-in-another-harness\"\u003e16. Embedding in another harness\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe repo is designed to be embedded by agents and harnesses without making okf-loom own the whole process. Preferred embedding pattern:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col\u003e\u003cli\u003eClone or vendor the repository.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eLoad root \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e and focused resources from \u003ccode\u003eresources/\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eRun CLI commands via source-checkout invocation.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eStart \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e only when an interactive studio is useful.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eLet the external agent consume \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/__events\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003e/__comments\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eWrite through mutators or whitelisted update/apply paths.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e ephemeral and out of normal commits.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eMinimal Python read-only server embedding is possible with \u003ccode\u003eThreadingHTTPServer\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eOKFWikiHandler\u003c/code\u003e, but mutating studio behavior requires deliberately attaching the same studio/session/token wiring that \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e creates. Embedders that bind outside loopback must make the exposure decision explicitly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/embedding_guide.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"17-verification-expectations\"\u003e17. Verification expectations\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA build-from-docs implementation must satisfy these acceptance checks:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.SPEC_VERSION == \"0.1\"\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eokf_loom.LOOM_VERSION\u003c/code\u003e matches the v1.0 runtime version printed by \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom --version\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003evalidate\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003einfo\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egraph\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esearch\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ediscover\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eplan\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupdate\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erepair\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eindex\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elog\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003einit\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebootstrap\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eimport\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etunnel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ewait\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ewatch\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etoken\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-claim\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-reply\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-resolve\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-list\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003epresence\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erender\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebuild\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecapabilities\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupgrade\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ewrite-concept\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eset-frontmatter\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elink-add\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eentity-add\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupdate-section\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003ereplace-text\u003c/code\u003e exist on the CLI surface.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eValidation profiles and \u003ccode\u003e--fail-on-broken-links\u003c/code\u003e match this spec.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eSearch modes are dependency-free and restricted to the six current modes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e fails closed on unknown enum, invalid bool, and path escape while preserving unknown keys.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eMutators preserve unknown frontmatter, write atomically, and avoid duplicate/idempotency failures.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eLive studio emits SSE/events, supports polling fallback, preserves no-refresh patching, and exposes the documented routes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecomment_link\u003c/code\u003e events are emitted when a resolve links activity ids.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003edirectives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eevents.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e, history, and idempotency caps prevent unbounded session growth.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eComment archive is a separate boolean track, root-only, gated on whole-thread-resolved, and auto-unarchives on reply.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eokfLoomStudio.register()\u003c/code\u003e ships \u003ccode\u003epanel\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eviewMode\u003c/code\u003e; other documented kinds are reserved and warned.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePublic bind, active-code, no-edit, CSRF, Origin/Host, body-size, and path-containment gates are fail-closed.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSuggested repo-local verification commands:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom --version\nscripts/okf-loom validate docs-bundle --strict\nscripts/okf-loom info docs-bundle --format json\nscripts/okf-loom search docs-bundle \"current spec\" --mode lexical --format json\nscripts/okf-loom build docs-bundle --target static --out /tmp/okf-docs-site\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"18-current-source-of-truth-references\"\u003e18. Current source-of-truth references\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis spec is intentionally self-contained for rebuilding current behavior. Concise detailed references remain separate and should be kept aligned with this file:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/cli.md\u003c/a\u003e for command flags and JSON output details.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/http_routes.md\u003c/a\u003e for route status codes and request/response shapes.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\u003c/a\u003e for comment state and archive edge cases.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/search_modes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/search_modes.md\u003c/a\u003e for ranking algorithms and result shape.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/config_yaml.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/config_yaml.md\u003c/a\u003e for config defaults and loader behavior.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/capabilities.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/capabilities.md\u003c/a\u003e for the current capability catalogue.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/architecture.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/architecture.md\u003c/a\u003e for module-level architecture.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/embedding_guide.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003e/reference/embedding_guide.md\u003c/a\u003e for harness integration.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe upstream OKF SPEC v0.1 remains the base wire-format reference. This file governs current okf-loom behavior on top of that base.\u003c/p\u003e", "tutorials/author_with_agent": "\u003ch2 id=\"direct-the-agent-loop\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial walks you through the canonical OKF agent loop: block on the next open comment, claim it, author the change through the CLI mutators, resolve the comment, and loop.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn the OKF studio the human \u003cstrong\u003edirects\u003c/strong\u003e by posting comments, and the agent \u003cstrong\u003eauthors\u003c/strong\u003e the markdown files through the mutator commands. This tutorial shows the agent side of that split — the commands that turn a comment into an applied, undoable edit.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial assumes you have finished \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/live_studio_basics.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eUse the live studio\u003c/a\u003e and have a bundle served with at least one open comment waiting.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-you-will-have-at-the-end\"\u003eWhat you will have at the end\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBy the end of this tutorial you will have:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eRun \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e as a foreground blocking call.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eClaimed a comment and announced editing presence.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eAuthored a change through the mutator verbs with a shared group id.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eResolved the comment with a reply and activity links.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eSeen the full loop and know how to repeat it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou will be able to drive the comment-to-resolve loop on your own.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"the-loop-at-a-glance\"\u003eThe loop at a glance\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe canonical loop is five moves, repeated:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003escripts/okf-loom wait        →  scripts/okf-loom comment-claim  →  mutators  →  scripts/okf-loom comment-resolve  →  loop\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eMove\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eCommand\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhat it does\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWait\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt; --for comment\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBlocks until an open comment exists, then prints it as JSON and exits.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eClaim\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-claim \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt; \u0026lt;id\u0026gt; --summary \"…\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eMarks the comment \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e and flips presence to editing.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAuthor\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom entity-add\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom write-concept\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWrites the change to the bundle files.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eResolve\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-resolve \u0026lt;bundle\u0026gt; \u0026lt;id\u0026gt; --reply \"…\" --activity … --summary \"…\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eMarks the comment \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e and links the change-list entries.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eLoop\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait …\u003c/code\u003e again\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eBlock on the next comment.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe full flag surface for each command is in \u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"a-note-on-scriptsokf-loom-wait-read-this-before-you-run-anything\"\u003eA note on scripts/okf-loom wait — read this before you run anything\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e is a \u003cstrong\u003eforeground, block-once\u003c/strong\u003e primitive. It blocks until work arrives, prints exactly one work item as JSON, and exits. You then act on that item and call \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e again.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNever background it.\u003c/strong\u003e Do not run \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait \u0026amp;\u003c/code\u003e, do not wrap it in \u003ccode\u003enohup\u003c/code\u003e, and do not detach it into a subprocess you do not immediately await.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA backgrounded \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e produces a work item that nothing consumes. The comment goes \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e (or sits \u003ccode\u003eopen\u003c/code\u003e), the user sees no progress, and the loop silently stalls. The correct shape is block → act → block, with you as the processor.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf you need a continuous tail for a long-running consumer (a different shape), use \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom watch\u003c/code\u003e instead — but for driving the comment loop, \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e is the right tool, run in your foreground.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-bring-up-the-studio\"\u003eStep 1: Bring up the studio\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe mutators detect a live studio session and route every write through it, which is what gives you attribution, undo snapshots, and live updates. So start the studio first.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn one terminal:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom serve ~/my-first-bundle --no-open\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eLeave it running. It writes a per-session token to \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/.token\u003c/code\u003e that the CLI mutators read automatically — you do not handle the token yourself.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-post-a-comment-for-the-agent\"\u003eStep 2: Post a comment for the agent\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFrom the studio's Comments panel (or a second terminal using a helper script), post a concrete directive, for example:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eAdd a typed depends_on link from tables/orders to services/checkout, and add an Order entity to tables/orders.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eConfirm it is waiting:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-list ~/my-first-bundle --state open\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNote the comment id the list returns — you will use it in the next steps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-wait-for-the-comment\"\u003eStep 3: Wait for the comment\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn your agent terminal, block on the next open comment:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom wait ~/my-first-bundle --for comment\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe command blocks until an open comment exists, then prints it as JSON and exits \u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-json\"\u003e{\"id\": \"01JABED9K0\", \"concept\": \"tables/orders\", \"body\": \"Add a typed depends_on link ...\", \"state\": \"open\"}\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCopy the \u003ccode\u003eid\u003c/code\u003e from that output. If no comment is open and you set a \u003ccode\u003e--timeout\u003c/code\u003e, the command exits \u003ccode\u003e1\u003c/code\u003e after the timeout — that is the signal to loop back or stop.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e drains the backlog first: without \u003ccode\u003e--since\u003c/code\u003e, the first call returns the oldest pre-existing open comment immediately, then subsequent calls drain the rest before settling into wait-for-new-work.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-claim-the-comment\"\u003eStep 4: Claim the comment\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eClaim the comment by its id and post a short summary that will show in the collapsed thread preview:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-claim ~/my-first-bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n  --summary \"adding depends_on link + Order entity\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eClaiming does two things at once:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eIt marks the comment \u003ccode\u003eclaimed\u003c/code\u003e so no other consumer picks it up.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eIt auto-flips the agent's presence to \u003ccode\u003eediting\u003c/code\u003e on the comment's concept, so the user immediately sees you are on it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou do not need a separate \u003ccode\u003epresence\u003c/code\u003e call after a claim. The user's Comments panel now shows your summary chip on the collapsed thread.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-author-via-the-mutators\"\u003eStep 5: Author via the mutators\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWrite the change through the mutator verbs. Pass the same \u003ccode\u003e--group-id\u003c/code\u003e to every write in this pass so the whole change is one-click group-undoable for the user:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle ~/my-first-bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target services/checkout \\\n  --relation depends_on \\\n  --evidence \"orders are appended by the checkout service\" \\\n  --group-id PASS1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom entity-add --bundle ~/my-first-bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders --label \"Order\" --kind business_entity \\\n  --entity-id entity/order --alias \"Sales Order\" \\\n  --group-id PASS1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBecause a studio session is live, each mutator routes through the studio's save funnel. That means every write is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAttributed\u003c/strong\u003e — recorded with \u003ccode\u003eactor=agent\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eorigin=mutator\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUndoable\u003c/strong\u003e — a snapshot lands under \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/history/\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVisible\u003c/strong\u003e — a row is appended to \u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/events.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e and a \u003ccode\u003echanged\u003c/code\u003e (plus \u003ccode\u003egraph\u003c/code\u003e, for link-affecting ops) event is pushed over the live channel.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach command prints the activity id of the write it just made. Collect those ids — you will link them from the resolution in the next step.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-resolve-the-comment\"\u003eStep 6: Resolve the comment\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eResolve the comment, linking the activity ids from the pass and writing both a long-form reply and a short summary:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-resolve ~/my-first-bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n  --activity 01JABED5K7,01JABED5K8 \\\n  --reply \"Done — added the depends_on link and the Order entity.\" \\\n  --summary \"done: link + entity added\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e--activity\u003c/code\u003e ids are what make the pass one-click group-undoable from the change list: a single undo reverts both writes together. The \u003ccode\u003e--reply\u003c/code\u003e is the long-form resolution message; the \u003ccode\u003e--summary\u003c/code\u003e is the one-line blurb shown in the collapsed thread preview.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAfter this command the comment is \u003ccode\u003eresolved\u003c/code\u003e, the user sees your reply, and the change-list entries are linked to the resolution.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-loop\"\u003eStep 7: Loop\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCall \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e again to block on the next comment:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom wait ~/my-first-bundle --for comment\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThat is the whole loop. Every iteration is the same five moves: wait, claim, author, resolve, repeat.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf the wait times out or you are done for the session, set presence back to idle so the user knows you have stepped away:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom presence ~/my-first-bundle --state idle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"a-worked-four-step-example\"\u003eA worked four-step example\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eHere is the loop end to end for the directive in Step 2, condensed into four copy-pasteable moves. Assume the comment id is \u003ccode\u003e01JABED9K0\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# 1. Wait for the next open comment (foreground — do not background this).\nscripts/okf-loom wait ~/my-first-bundle --for comment\n\n# 2. Claim it and announce what you are doing.\nscripts/okf-loom comment-claim ~/my-first-bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n  --summary \"adding depends_on link + Order entity\"\n\n# 3. Author the change as one undoable group.\nscripts/okf-loom link-add --bundle ~/my-first-bundle \\\n  --source tables/orders --target services/checkout \\\n  --relation depends_on \\\n  --evidence \"orders are appended by the checkout service\" \\\n  --group-id PASS1\nscripts/okf-loom entity-add --bundle ~/my-first-bundle \\\n  --id tables/orders --label \"Order\" --kind business_entity \\\n  --entity-id entity/order --alias \"Sales Order\" \\\n  --group-id PASS1\n\n# 4. Resolve the comment, linking the activity ids from step 3.\nscripts/okf-loom comment-resolve ~/my-first-bundle 01JABED9K0 \\\n  --activity 01JABED5K7,01JABED5K8 \\\n  --reply \"Done — added the depends_on link and the Order entity.\" \\\n  --summary \"done: link + entity added\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAfter step 4, call \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e again and the loop continues.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"where-to-go-next\"\u003eWhere to go next\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou can now drive the comment-to-resolve loop on your own.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen threads accumulate or you need to triage them:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/archive_threads.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eArchive and resolve comment threads\u003c/a\u003e — the archive and resolution rules.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/discover_and_fix_gaps.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFind and fix bundle gaps\u003c/a\u003e — feed discovery suggestions into the same mutators.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe machinery behind every command above is documented in:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every flag on \u003ccode\u003ewait\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-claim\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecomment-resolve\u003c/code\u003e, and the mutators.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eComment lifecycle and archive rules\u003c/a\u003e — the open → claimed → resolved state machine and the archive track.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor the design rationale behind the foreground-wait contract and the comment-driven model, see \u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhy the live studio exists\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eTutorials\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "tutorials/first_bundle": "\u003ch2 id=\"author-your-first-bundle\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial takes you from an empty directory to a small, valid OKF bundle that you scaffolded, populated, validated, and improved.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou will write the concepts by hand so you can see exactly what an OKF file looks like. Then you will let okf-loom check your work and suggest improvements.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial assumes you have finished \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/install.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eUse okf-loom from a clone\u003c/a\u003e. You need the checked-in source-checkout helper before you start.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-you-will-have-at-the-end\"\u003eWhat you will have at the end\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBy the end of this tutorial you will have:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eA bundle created with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom init\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThree hand-written concepts linked together.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA directory \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e listing your concepts.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA clean \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate\u003c/code\u003e run.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eExperience reading a discovery report and fixing one gap.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou will be able to scaffold, populate, and validate a bundle on your own.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-scaffold-with-scriptsokf-loom-init\"\u003eStep 1: Scaffold with scripts/okf-loom init\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom ships a scaffolding command that creates the three files every well-formed bundle starts with.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePick a name for your bundle and run:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom init --bundle ~/my-first-bundle --name \"My First Bundle\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom init\u003c/code\u003e refuses to run in a non-empty directory, so you get a clean slate every time. If the directory exists and has files in it, the command exits with a message — pick a fresh path and try again.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-inspect-what-init-created\"\u003eStep 2: Inspect what init created\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eMove into the new bundle and list it:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003ecd ~/my-first-bundle\nls -la\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see three files:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eindex.md\nlog.md\nokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOpen \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e. It is the bundle root index, and it is the only \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e allowed to carry frontmatter. The frontmatter declares the spec version and any optional extensions:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-yaml\"\u003e---\nokf_version: \"0.1\"\nokf_extensions:\n  - okf.cap.typed_relations\ngenerated: true\n---\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe body is a directory listing — currently empty, because you have not written any concepts yet.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOpen \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom.config.yaml\u003c/code\u003e. Every key is optional and commented; you can leave it at the defaults for now.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOpen \u003ccode\u003elog.md\u003c/code\u003e. It is an append-only update history, newest first, that okf-loom will help you maintain as the bundle grows.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-write-your-first-concept\"\u003eStep 3: Write your first concept\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCreate a directory for your first domain and add a concept.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003emkdir tables\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCreate \u003ccode\u003etables/customers.md\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: Table\ntitle: Customers\ndescription: One row per registered customer.\ntags: [customers, pii]\ntimestamp: \"2026-06-29T00:00:00Z\"\n---\n\n# Schema\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `customer_id` | STRING | Globally unique customer identifier. |\n| `email` | STRING | Verified email address. |\n| `first_seen_at` | TIMESTAMP | When the customer first appeared. |\n\n# Notes\n\nEmail is considered PII.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA few things to notice:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e is the only field the spec hard-requires; the rest are recommended but worth filling in.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e is quoted so YAML reads it as a string, not a datetime.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e is a YAML list, not a comma-separated string.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe body uses a \u003ccode\u003e# Schema\u003c/code\u003e table, which is the conventional shape for a table concept.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-add-a-second-concept-that-links-to-the-first\"\u003eStep 4: Add a second concept that links to the first\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCreate \u003ccode\u003etables/orders.md\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: Table\ntitle: Orders\ndescription: One row per completed customer order.\ntags: [orders, revenue]\ntimestamp: \"2026-06-29T00:00:00Z\"\n---\n\n# Schema\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | STRING | Globally unique order identifier. |\n| `customer_id` | STRING | FK to [customers](/tables/customers.md). |\n| `total_usd` | NUMERIC | Order total in US dollars. |\n| `placed_at` | TIMESTAMP | When the order was submitted. |\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe link \u003ccode\u003e[customers](/tables/customers.md)\u003c/code\u003e is in the absolute bundle-relative form the spec recommends. It is stable if you ever move \u003ccode\u003eorders.md\u003c/code\u003e around inside the bundle.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-add-a-third-concept-in-a-different-domain\"\u003eStep 5: Add a third concept in a different domain\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eConcepts do not all have to live in one directory. Add a service that writes to your orders table:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003emkdir services\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCreate \u003ccode\u003eservices/checkout.md\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: Service\ntitle: Checkout Service\ndescription: The order checkout API; accepts order POSTs and writes to the orders table.\ntags: [checkout, write-api]\ntimestamp: \"2026-06-29T00:00:00Z\"\n---\n\n# Overview\n\n`checkout` is the public order-submission API.\nIt validates cart state and appends a row to the [orders table](/tables/orders.md).\n\n# Endpoints\n\n| Method | Path | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| POST | `/v2/orders` | Create a new order. |\n| GET | `/v2/orders/{id}` | Fetch an order by id. |\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have three concepts across two directories, linked into a small graph.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-write-a-directory-index\"\u003eStep 6: Write a directory index\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAn \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e in any directory lets a reader (human or agent) see what is available before opening individual files.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCreate \u003ccode\u003etables/index.md\u003c/code\u003e — and note that, unlike the bundle root, this non-root index must \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e have frontmatter:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e# Tables\n\n* [Customers](customers.md) - one row per registered customer.\n* [Orders](orders.md) - one row per completed customer order.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou can also let okf-loom generate directory indexes for you with \u003ccode\u003eindex\u003c/code\u003e; hand-authoring one here shows you the shape directly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-validate-the-bundle\"\u003eStep 7: Validate the bundle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun the validator:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate ~/my-first-bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see a clean PASS:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eConformance: PASS  Strict: PASS  (errors=0 warnings=0 info=0)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf you see warnings, read them — they are almost always missing recommended keys or a typo in a link target, both easy to fix.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-8-discover-gaps\"\u003eStep 8: Discover gaps\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eValidation tells you whether the bundle is well-formed. Discovery tells you what is missing or weakly connected.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun the discovery pass and write the report to a file:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom discover ~/my-first-bundle --out ~/my-first-bundle-suggestions.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOpen the report. With three concepts you will commonly see suggestions like these:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eRule\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhat it flags\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emissing_descriptions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept whose \u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e is empty.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emissing_indexes\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA directory with concepts but no \u003ccode\u003eindex.md\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eorphan_concepts\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept with no incoming or outgoing links.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eunlinked_mentions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eA concept body that names another concept by title but does not link to it.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eDiscovery suggestions are advisory. The managing agent applies the ones that make sense and leaves the rest.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-9-fix-one-gap\"\u003eStep 9: Fix one gap\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePick one concrete gap and fix it by hand. A common one is a missing directory index for \u003ccode\u003eservices/\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eCreate \u003ccode\u003eservices/index.md\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e# Services\n\n* [Checkout Service](checkout.md) - the order checkout API.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRe-run discovery to confirm the suggestion is gone:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom discover ~/my-first-bundle --out ~/my-first-bundle-suggestions.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThen re-validate to confirm nothing regressed:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom validate ~/my-first-bundle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThat loop — write, validate, discover, fix — is the daily authoring rhythm for an OKF bundle.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"where-to-go-next\"\u003eWhere to go next\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou can now scaffold, populate, and validate a bundle on your own.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen you want to speed up authoring, the CLI mutator verbs write concepts and links for you so you do not have to hand-edit every file:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/author_with_verbs.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor concepts via CLI verbs\u003c/a\u003e — \u003ccode\u003ewrite-concept\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elink-add\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eentity-add\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/discover_and_fix_gaps.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFind and fix bundle gaps\u003c/a\u003e — turning discovery output into applied edits.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe format details behind every field above are documented in:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/frontmatter.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFrontmatter contract\u003c/a\u003e — required vs recommended keys.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/links.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eLink forms\u003c/a\u003e — absolute vs relative, and when to use each.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor the philosophy behind the format's tiny required surface, see \u003ca href=\"/explanation/what_is_okf.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhat OKF is for\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eTutorials\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "tutorials/install": "\u003ch2 id=\"use-okf-loom-from-a-clone\"\u003eUse okf-loom from a clone\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial takes you from an empty machine to a working source checkout of okf-loom, and then walks you through your very first validation against a bundle you build by hand.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe primary distribution model is this GitHub-hosted, cloneable skill repository. Agents and harnesses should clone the repo, read \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003eAGENTS.md\u003c/code\u003e if their harness starts there), load the focused resource files under \u003ccode\u003eresources/\u003c/code\u003e, and run okf-loom from the checkout.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou do not need to know anything about OKF to follow along. Every step is runnable; copy the commands in order.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-you-will-have-at-the-end\"\u003eWhat you will have at the end\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBy the end of this tutorial you will have:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eA cloned okf-loom repository.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e and the relevant focused resource loaded or identified for your harness.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA verified source-checkout command that prints okf-loom version.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA tiny two-concept bundle that passes \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eA clear mental model of what \"conformance\" means for an OKF bundle.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-check-your-python\"\u003eStep 1: Check your Python\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom requires Python 3.11 or newer. Check what you have:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003epython3 --version\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see \u003ccode\u003ePython 3.11.x\u003c/code\u003e or higher. If you see an older version, install Python 3.11+ first (\u003ca href=\"https://www.python.org/downloads/\" class=\"okf-external\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003epython.org\u003c/a\u003e or your system package manager) before continuing.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-clone-the-repository\"\u003eStep 2: Clone the repository\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eClone the repository and enter it:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003egit clone \u0026lt;repo-url\u0026gt; okf-loom\ncd okf-loom\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf you already have the repository, start from its root directory instead.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-load-the-agent-facing-skill-resources\"\u003eStep 3: Load the agent-facing skill resources\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIf you are an agent, read \u003ccode\u003eSKILL.md\u003c/code\u003e first, then load the smallest resource file that fits your task:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eResource file\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eUse\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresources/format-basics.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRead, validate, or make a small edit.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresources/authoring.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eAuthor or restructure concepts.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresources/advanced-operations.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eUse search, discovery, update plans, embedding, or the live studio.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresources/studio-agent-loop.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eDrive comment-directed live studio work.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eHumans can skim \u003ccode\u003eREADME.md\u003c/code\u003e and continue.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-create-a-virtual-environment\"\u003eStep 4: Create a virtual environment\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIt is good practice to install Python tools into a dedicated virtual environment so they do not collide with your system Python.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003epython3 -m venv .venv\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eActivate it:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e# Linux and macOS:\nsource .venv/bin/activate\n\n# Windows (PowerShell):\n.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYour shell prompt should now show \u003ccode\u003e(.venv)\u003c/code\u003e. Every Python command from here on runs inside that environment.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-run-directly-from-the-checkout\"\u003eStep 5: Run directly from the checkout\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor the most portable agent path, run directly from the checkout:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom --version\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNormal runtime and docs validation require no primary dependency install step. PyYAML is preferred when present; when it is not available, okf-loom uses a conservative built-in YAML fallback that fails closed on unsupported advanced YAML. For local test development, install test dependencies explicitly:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003epython -m pip install pytest\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis repo is not installed as a package for normal use; \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom\u003c/code\u003e is the source-checkout contract.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"optional-the-browser-proof-dependencies\"\u003eOptional: the browser-proof dependencies\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eokf-loom ships an optional browser-based end-to-end proof for the viewer (Playwright tests + a screenshot-capture script). It is \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e required to use okf-loom, the viewer, or the live studio.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eInstall it only if you want to run the viewer e2e proof:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003epython -m pip install playwright\nplaywright install chromium\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWithout these dependencies, the browser proof tests skip cleanly and everything else works exactly the same. Most readers should skip this for now and come back to it later.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-remember-the-helper-path\"\u003eStep 6: Remember the helper path\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe checked-in helper can be run from any current directory. Save the checkout path before leaving the repo:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003eexport OKF_REPO=\"$(pwd)\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eNow verify it:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" --version\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see something like:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eokf-loom 1.0.0 (SPEC v0.1)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe first number is okf-loom version; the second is the OKF spec version okf-loom implements. Both come from okf-loom itself — you do not need to set them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-build-a-tiny-scratch-bundle\"\u003eStep 7: Build a tiny scratch bundle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eAn OKF bundle is just a directory of markdown files with YAML frontmatter. You do not need the scaffolding command for this first check — two hand-written files are enough to prove the install works.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eMake a scratch directory:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003emkdir -p ~/okf-scratch/tables\ncd ~/okf-scratch\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWrite your first concept. Create \u003ccode\u003etables/customers.md\u003c/code\u003e with this content:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: Table\ntitle: Customers\ndescription: One row per registered customer.\ntags: [customers]\n---\n\n# Schema\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `customer_id` | STRING | Globally unique customer identifier. |\n| `email` | STRING | Verified email address. |\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWrite a second concept that links to the first. Create \u003ccode\u003etables/orders.md\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-markdown\"\u003e---\ntype: Table\ntitle: Orders\ndescription: One row per completed customer order.\ntags: [orders]\n---\n\n# Schema\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | STRING | Globally unique order identifier. |\n| `customer_id` | STRING | FK to [customers](/tables/customers.md). |\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have a bundle with two concepts and one link between them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-8-validate-the-scratch-bundle\"\u003eStep 8: Validate the scratch bundle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eRun the validator against the directory:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003e\"$OKF_REPO/scripts/okf-loom\" validate ~/okf-scratch\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see output ending in a clean PASS:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eConformance: PASS  Strict: PASS  (errors=0 warnings=0 info=0)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003eConformance: PASS\u003c/code\u003e line is the one that matters. It means your bundle meets every hard rule in the OKF spec.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-conformance-means\"\u003eWhat conformance means\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe OKF spec is deliberately tiny. A bundle is conformant when \u003cstrong\u003eevery\u003c/strong\u003e non-reserved markdown file has parseable YAML frontmatter with a non-empty \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e field.
