That single \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e key is the only hard-required field in the whole format.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEverything else — \u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edescription\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etimestamp\u003c/code\u003e, links — is \u003cstrong\u003erecommended\u003c/strong\u003e, not required. The validator surfaces missing recommended keys as warnings, not errors, so a bundle with a few warnings is still perfectly conformant.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis shows up in the exit codes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eCode\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eMeaning\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eConformant (no errors).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eConformance failure (a concept is missing \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e, or frontmatter is unparseable).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eStrict failure (you passed \u003ccode\u003e--strict\u003c/code\u003e and warnings were promoted to errors).\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor a quick CI gate you will usually want \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom validate --strict\u003c/code\u003e from inside \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom/\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom/scripts/okf-loom validate --strict\u003c/code\u003e from a parent workspace, which treats warnings as errors. That is a choice you make at validate time — the bundle on disk stays the same.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"where-to-go-next\"\u003eWhere to go next\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou now have a working source checkout and have validated a bundle by hand.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe natural next step is to let okf-loom scaffold a bundle for you and walk through the full authoring loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e — use \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom init\u003c/code\u003e, write concepts, validate, and discover gaps.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen you are ready to turn validation into a CI gate:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/validate_in_ci.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eValidate a bundle in CI\u003c/a\u003e — strict profiles and broken-link gates.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/build_static_site.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eBuild a static site\u003c/a\u003e — render a bundle to a portable site.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe machinery behind every command above is documented neutrally in:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — every command and flag.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/frontmatter.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eFrontmatter contract\u003c/a\u003e — required vs recommended keys.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor the bigger picture of what OKF is for, see \u003ca href=\"/explanation/what_is_okf.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eWhat OKF is for\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eReturn to \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/index.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eTutorials\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e", "tutorials/live_studio_basics": "\u003ch2 id=\"use-the-live-studio\"\u003eUse the live studio\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial brings up the OKF live studio in your browser and walks you through every reading surface it offers, then shows you how a comment you post becomes a directive the agent can act on.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio is the same viewer in every reading mode (rendered, source, split, graph, search) plus a live-update layer and a comment channel. You do not need an agent running to follow this tutorial — the studio works on its own.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThis tutorial assumes you have a small bundle to point at. If you do not, finish \u003ca href=\"/tutorials/first_bundle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eAuthor your first bundle\u003c/a\u003e first, or use the sample at \u003ccode\u003eokf-loom/samples/demo_bundle\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"what-you-will-have-at-the-end\"\u003eWhat you will have at the end\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBy the end of this tutorial you will have:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eServed a bundle with \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eNavigated the root index, a concept page, the source and split views, the graph view, and search.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003ePosted a comment from the studio.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eFound that comment on disk in \u003ccode\u003edirectives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou will be able to serve the studio and direct work via comments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-1-serve-the-bundle\"\u003eStep 1: Serve the bundle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePoint \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e at your bundle and open it without auto-launching a browser (so you can control the URL yourself):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom serve ~/my-first-bundle --no-open\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio prints a URL like the one below and then runs in the foreground of that terminal:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eserving bundle on http://127.0.0.1:8787/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBy default the studio binds to \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e only — your loopback interface — so only you can reach it. Binding to the network requires an explicit \u003ccode\u003e--public\u003c/code\u003e flag and an acknowledgement, which this tutorial does not need.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eLeave that terminal running. Open a second terminal for the rest of the steps, and open the URL in your browser.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-2-open-the-root-index\"\u003eStep 2: Open the root index\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio's landing page is the bundle root index.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eIn your browser, visit:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8787/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see a dashboard: the bundle name with stat chips (concepts, types, links) and an \u003cstrong\u003eExplore the graph\u003c/strong\u003e button, the bundle description, then every concept as a card grouped by type — each card carries its type icon, a short description, outgoing/incoming link counts (→ / ←), and tag chips. While the studio runs you also get a \u003cstrong\u003eRecently changed\u003c/strong\u003e rail (the last few edited concepts with relative times) and live comment-count chips on cards that have open threads.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe route behind this page is \u003ccode\u003e/\u003c/code\u003e, documented in \u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHTTP server routes\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-3-open-a-concept-page\"\u003eStep 3: Open a concept page\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eClick any concept — for example \u003cstrong\u003eOrders\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe page opens with a type-tinted header band: the type chip and icon, a reading-time estimate, the description as a lede, alias subtitles, entity chips, and any typed relations. Below the full-width rendered body you get \u003cstrong\u003eLinks to\u003c/strong\u003e and \u003cstrong\u003eCited by\u003c/strong\u003e as connection cards (type icon + directional relation chips). The left rail holds the Related list, a Sections outline that highlights where you are as you scroll, and Quick actions; hovering a heading reveals a ¶ deep-link anchor.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe route is the concept id with the \u003ccode\u003e.md\u003c/code\u003e stripped — for example:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8787/tables/orders\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTry editing the file on disk while the studio is running and saving it. The page updates in place without a full reload — that is the live-update layer at work.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-4-switch-to-source-and-split-view\"\u003eStep 4: Switch to source and split view\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe concept page has a view-mode switcher with three options:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eMode\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eWhat it shows\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRendered\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe markdown rendered as HTML.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSource\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eThe raw markdown file, exactly as it sits on disk.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003eSplit\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eRendered on one side, source on the other.\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSwitch to \u003cstrong\u003eSource\u003c/strong\u003e to see the frontmatter and body verbatim — useful when you want to copy the exact text of a link or a schema row.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSwitch to \u003cstrong\u003eSplit\u003c/strong\u003e to compare the rendered view against the source side by side. This is the mode most authors settle into during a session.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-5-open-the-graph-view\"\u003eStep 5: Open the graph view\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio renders the whole bundle as a live force-directed graph (fCoSE layout).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eVisit:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8787/__graph\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach node is a concept drawn with its type's icon; colour carries the \u003cstrong\u003edetected themes\u003c/strong\u003e (community detection), and node size carries real influence (PageRank) — so the picture answers questions instead of restating the schema. On your first visit a three-step tour points out the essentials. The controls live in a \u003cstrong\u003elens bar pinned at the top of the right-hand pane\u003c/strong\u003e; each lens answers one question and ranks its answers in the pane below:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ctable class=\"okf-table\"\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003cth\u003eLens\u003c/th\u003e\u003cth\u003eThe question it answers\u003c/th\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMap\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eHow does this knowledge fit together?\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThemes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhat are the main topic areas — and which barely touch?\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlow\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhat feeds into what? (dependency layers, left → right)\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBridges\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhich concepts hold the areas together?\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRecent\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhat is fresh, what is going stale?\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFocus\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003ctd\u003eWhat surrounds the selected concept?\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe collapsed \u003cstrong\u003eAdvanced\u003c/strong\u003e disclosure holds the fine-tuning (spacing sliders, type filter, relationship labels, and a colour-by-theme toggle).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWays to explore:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHover\u003c/strong\u003e a node: its neighbourhood stays lit while the rest fades, and a preview card shows the description and link counts.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClick\u003c/strong\u003e a node: its full page renders in the right pane, beneath the pinned lens bar — diagrams, math, and code render there just like on the wiki pages.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShift-click\u003c/strong\u003e a second node to trace the shortest path between the two; the chain lights up and the status line reads it out.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDouble-click\u003c/strong\u003e (or press Enter) to open the concept's wiki page.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eKeyboard\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ef\u003c/code\u003e fits the view, \u003ccode\u003e/\u003c/code\u003e focuses search, arrows walk the selection along edges, Esc clears.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLegend chips\u003c/strong\u003e (bottom-left) toggle a type's visibility; alt-click solos it.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eConcepts with no links sit apart with a dashed \"not yet linked\" outline — this view is still the fastest way to spot orphans and clusters that ought to be connected. If a file changes on disk while you watch, the canvas updates in place and a \"Graph updated\" chip offers a re-layout.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-6-search\"\u003eStep 6: Search\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio has a built-in search bar.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eType a word that appears in your bundle — for example \u003ccode\u003ecustomer\u003c/code\u003e — and press Enter. The results page lists matching concepts ranked by relevance, with the matched snippet shown for each.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eBehind the scenes the route is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:8787/__search?q=customer\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eSearch runs dependency-free out of the box. The default mode is lexical; other modes (semantic, hybrid, tag, entity, relation) are described in \u003ca href=\"/reference/search_modes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eSearch modes\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-7-post-a-comment\"\u003eStep 7: Post a comment\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe studio's right-hand panel is the \u003cstrong\u003eComments\u003c/strong\u003e panel — your primary way to direct work without leaving the browser. (The \u003cstrong\u003eCommands\u003c/strong\u003e button in the studio bar — shortcut \u003ccode\u003eCtrl+K\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e⌘K\u003c/code\u003e on a Mac — opens a palette that jumps to any page or panel.)\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eOpen the panel and type a short directive, for example:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-text\"\u003eAdd a link from orders to the checkout service.\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePost it. The comment appears in the panel as an open thread.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou have just written the only kind of studio input a human makes: a comment. Everything else (edits, links, entities) is authored by the agent through the mutator commands, driven by the comments you post.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-8-watch-the-comment-land-in-directivesjsonl\"\u003eStep 8: Watch the comment land in directives.jsonl\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEvery comment you post is appended to a JSON Lines file inside the bundle's session directory.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFrom your second terminal, list the open directives:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-list ~/my-first-bundle --state open\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou should see the comment you just posted, with an id, a concept anchor, a state of \u003ccode\u003eopen\u003c/code\u003e, and the body you typed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe same record lives on disk:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cpre\u003e\u003ccode class=\"language-bash\"\u003ecat ~/my-first-bundle/.okf-loom/session/directives.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eEach line is one comment object. This file is the contract between the studio (where you write comments) and the agent loop (which consumes them).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe comment states and the rules for moving between them are documented in \u003ca href=\"/reference/comment_lifecycle.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eComment lifecycle and archive rules\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"step-9-stop-the-studio\"\u003eStep 9: Stop the studio\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen you are done, return to the first terminal and stop the server with \u003ccode\u003eCtrl-C\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe session directory (\u003ccode\u003e.okf-loom/session/\u003c/code\u003e) stays on disk, so the comments you posted are preserved. The next \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e picks them back up.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"where-to-go-next\"\u003eWhere to go next\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eYou can now serve the studio and direct work via comments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe comments you posted are consumed by the agent loop — the canonical shape is \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom wait\u003c/code\u003e → claim → write → resolve:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/tutorials/author_with_agent.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eDirect the agent loop\u003c/a\u003e — drive the comment-to-resolve loop end to end.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eWhen threads start to pile up, you will want to triage them:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/how-to/archive_threads.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eArchive and resolve comment threads\u003c/a\u003e — the archive and resolution rules.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eThe machinery behind every route above is documented in:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/http_routes.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eHTTP server routes\u003c/a\u003e — every URL the studio serves.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/reference/cli.md\" class=\"okf-internal\"\u003eCLI command reference\u003c/a\u003e — \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom serve\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003escripts/okf-loom comment-list\u003c/code\u003e, and friends.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eFor the design rationale behind the studio's comment-driven model, see \u003ca href=\"/explanation/live_studio_design.md\"  *     so Technical + Auto survives reload and navigation.

    // ====================================================================
    // Signal controls — presets, panel build, control wiring
    // ====================================================================
    // ====================================================================
    // Lens analytics — real algorithms behind each lens.
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Research-grounded (see docs/design/graph-lenses.md): communities are
    // the color dimension that reveals structure (Gephi/InfraNodus/Bloom
    // convergence), PageRank finds what matters better than raw degree,
    // betweenness finds the bridgers (Kumu's "top bridgers"), and
    // timestamps make freshness a first-class lens. All computed locally,
    // lazily, and cached until the graph changes.
    function invalidateLensCache() { _lensCache = {}; }

    // Deterministic label propagation: seeds by sorted id, iterates in
    // sorted order, ties break to the SMALLEST label — same input, same
    // communities, every load. Communities are then renumbered by size
    // (0 = biggest) so colors are stable and legends read biggest-first.
    function computeCommunities() {
      if (_lensCache.communities) return _lensCache.communities;
      // Deterministic single-level-iterated Louvain (modularity
      // optimization) — the Gephi-standard community method. Label
      // propagation was tried first and collapses densely cross-linked
      // bundles into one community; modularity splits them along real
      // link-density boundaries. Determinism: nodes processed in sorted
      // order, ties broken toward the smallest community id, fixed pass
      // cap — same bundle, same communities, every load.
      var ids = Object.keys(nodeIndex).sort();
      var idx = {};
      ids.forEach(function (id, i) { idx[id] = i; });
      var n = ids.length;
      // Undirected weighted adjacency (dedup multi-edges to weight).
      var adj = ids.map(function () { return {}; });
      var m2 = 0;  // 2m (sum of all degrees)
      cy.edges().forEach(function (e) {
        var a = idx[e.source().id()], b = idx[e.target().id()];
        if (a == null || b == null || a === b) return;
        adj[a][b] = (adj[a][b] || 0) + 1;
        adj[b][a] = (adj[b][a] || 0) + 1;
        m2 += 2;
      });
      var community = ids.map(function (_, i) { return i; });
      var degree = adj.map(function (nb) {
        var d = 0; Object.keys(nb).forEach(function (k) { d += nb[k]; }); return d;
      });
      if (m2 > 0) {
        var commTot = degree.slice();       // Σtot per community
        for (var pass = 0; pass < 10; pass++) {
          var moved = false;
          for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            var current = community[i];
            // Links from i into each neighbouring community.
            var kIn = {};
            Object.keys(adj[i]).forEach(function (j) {
              var c = community[j];
              kIn[c] = (kIn[c] || 0) + adj[i][j];
            });
            // Remove i from its community.
            commTot[current] -= degree[i];
            var best = current;
            var bestGain = (kIn[current] || 0) - commTot[current] * degree[i] / m2;
            Object.keys(kIn).map(Number).sort(function (a, b) { return a - b; }).forEach(function (c) {
              if (c === current) return;
              var gain = kIn[c] - commTot[c] * degree[i] / m2;
              if (gain > bestGain + 1e-9) { bestGain = gain; best = c; }
            });
            commTot[best] += degree[i];
            if (best !== current) { community[i] = best; moved = true; }
          }
          if (!moved) break;
        }
      }
      // Renumber by community size (desc), tie → smallest member id.
      var members = {};
      ids.forEach(function (id, i) {
        (members[community[i]] = members[community[i]] || []).push(id);
      });
      var ordered = Object.keys(members).sort(function (a, b) {
        var d = members[b].length - members[a].length;
        return d !== 0 ? d : (members[a][0] < members[b][0] ? -1 : 1);
      });
      var out = {}, list = [];
      ordered.forEach(function (lab, k) {
        members[lab].forEach(function (id) { out[id] = k; });
        list.push({ index: k, ids: members[lab] });
      });
      _lensCache.communities = { of: out, list: list };
      communityOf = out;
      return _lensCache.communities;
    }
    function communityColor(i) {
      // Golden-angle hues (same technique as the type palette) at a calmer
      // saturation so regions read as areas, not warnings.
      return "hsl(" + Math.round((i * 137.508) % 360) + ", 52%, 52%)";
    }

    function computePageRank() {
      if (_lensCache.pagerank) return _lensCache.pagerank;
      var out = {}, max = 0;
      try {
        var pr = cy.elements().pageRank({ dampingFactor: 0.85, precision: 1e-6 });
        cy.nodes().forEach(function (n) {
          var r = pr.rank(n);
          out[n.id()] = r;
          if (r > max) max = r;
        });
        if (max > 0) Object.keys(out).forEach(function (k) { out[k] = out[k] / max; });
      } catch (e) { /* empty graph */ }
      _lensCache.pagerank = out;
      return out;
    }

    function computeBetweenness() {
      if (_lensCache.betweenness) return _lensCache.betweenness;
      var out = {}, max = 0;
      try {
        var bc = cy.elements().betweennessCentrality({ directed: false });
        cy.nodes().forEach(function (n) {
          var b = bc.betweenness(n);
          out[n.id()] = b;
          if (b > max) max = b;
        });
        if (max > 0) Object.keys(out).forEach(function (k) { out[k] = out[k] / max; });
      } catch (e) { /* empty graph */ }
      _lensCache.betweenness = out;
      return out;
    }

    // Recency in days (Infinity = undated). Uses the authored frontmatter
    // timestamp shipped per node.
    function recencyDays(id) {
      var d = nodeIndex[id] || {};
      if (!d.timestamp) return Infinity;
      var t = Date.parse(d.timestamp);
      if (isNaN(t)) return Infinity;
      return Math.max(0, (Date.now() - t) / 86400000);
    }
    function recencyColor(days) {
      if (!isFinite(days)) return "#94a3b8";               // undated: neutral slate
      // Fresh teal → aged amber → stale grey-brown over ~180 days.
      var t = Math.min(1, days / 180);
      var hue = 175 - 135 * t;                              // 175 (teal) → 40 (amber)
      var sat = 62 - 30 * t;
      var light = 46 + 10 * t;
      return "hsl(" + Math.round(hue) + ", " + Math.round(sat) + "%, " + Math.round(light) + "%)";
    }
    function bridgeColor(score) {
      // Muted slate for low scores → strong violet for the top bridgers
      // (distinct from the teal selection accent).
      var t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, score));
      return "hsl(268, " + Math.round(12 + 60 * t) + "%, " + Math.round(62 - 20 * t) + "%)";
    }

    // ====================================================================
    // Lenses — each answers one question a user actually has.

    // Naming follows the products users understand (Kumu, InfraNodus,

    // ====================================================================
    var LENSES = {
      map: {

        state: { spacing: 1, separation: 1, groupStrength: 1, groupBy: "community",

      },
      flow: {

      },
      recent: {

                 showBridges: false, layout: "cose" },

      focus: {
        label: "Focus", question: "What surrounds the selected concept?",

    var ui = {};

    function applyLens(name) {

      applyFilters();

    // ---- Lens summary: the ranked answers beside the picture -----------
    // Every analytic view ships a clickable ranked list (the pattern that
    // makes Kumu/InfraNodus/Graph-Analysis land where bare pictures
    // don't). Rendered into #detail-empty, i.e. visible whenever no node
    // is selected; click a row -> select that node.
    function renderLensSummary() {
      var empty = document.getElementById("detail-empty");
      if (!empty) return;
      while (empty.firstChild) empty.removeChild(empty.firstChild);
      empty.classList.add("okf-lens-summary");
      var lensKey = controlState.lens;
      var ids = Object.keys(nodeIndex);
      if (!ids.length) { empty.appendChild(el("p", {}, ["No concepts in this bundle."])); return; }
      var frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
      function heading(text) { frag.appendChild(el("h3", { class: "okf-lens-summary__title" }, [text])); }
      function verdict(text) { frag.appendChild(el("p", { class: "okf-lens-summary__verdict" }, [text])); }
      function row(id, note, score, barColor) {
        var d = nodeIndex[id] || {};

        var bar = el("span", { class: "okf-lens-summary__bar" });

        if (barColor) bar.style.background = barColor;
        btn.appendChild(bar);
        btn.appendChild(el("span", { class: "okf-lens-summary__label" }, [d.label || id]));
        btn.appendChild(el("span", { class: "okf-lens-summary__note" }, [note]));
        btn.addEventListener("click", function () { clearPath(); showDetail(id); });
        frag.appendChild(btn);
      }
      var orphans = ids.filter(function (id) {
        return ((outgoing[id] || []).length + (backlinks[id] || []).length) === 0;
      });

      if (lensKey === "bridges") {
        var bt = computeBetweenness();
        heading("Top bridgers");
        verdict("These concepts sit on the paths between themes; losing one disconnects areas.");
        ids.slice().sort(function (a, b) { return (bt[b] || 0) - (bt[a] || 0); })
          .slice(0, 8).forEach(function (id) {
            row(id, Math.round((bt[id] || 0) * 100) + "%", bt[id] || 0);
          });
      } else if (lensKey === "recent") {
        heading("Freshness");
        var dated = ids.filter(function (id) { return isFinite(recencyDays(id)); });
        var stale = dated.filter(function (id) { return recencyDays(id) > 180; });
        var undated = ids.length - dated.length;
        verdict(stale.length + " of " + ids.length + " concepts are older than ~6 months" +
          (undated ? "; " + undated + " carry no timestamp" : "") + ".");
        dated.sort(function (a, b) { return recencyDays(b) - recencyDays(a); })
          .slice(0, 8).forEach(function (id) {
            var d = recencyDays(id);
            row(id, d > 365 ? Math.round(d / 365) + "y old" : Math.round(d) + "d old",
                Math.min(1, d / 365));
          });
      } else if (lensKey === "flow") {
        heading("Sources and sinks");
        var roots = ids.filter(function (id) { return (backlinks[id] || []).length === 0 && (outgoing[id] || []).length > 0; });
        var leaves = ids.filter(function (id) { return (outgoing[id] || []).length === 0 && (backlinks[id] || []).length > 0; });
        verdict(roots.length + " sources feed the flow; " + leaves.length + " sinks end it. Arrows read left to right.");
        var maxOut = 1;
        ids.forEach(function (id) { maxOut = Math.max(maxOut, (outgoing[id] || []).length); });
        ids.slice().sort(function (a, b) { return (outgoing[b] || []).length - (outgoing[a] || []).length; })
          .slice(0, 8).forEach(function (id) {

        var linked = {};
        cy.edges().forEach(function (e) {

        });

          }

        function exemplar(c) {
          return c.ids.slice().sort(function (a, b) { return (pr[b] || 0) - (pr[a] || 0); })[0];
        }
        var themes = com.list.filter(function (c) { return c.ids.length > 1; }).length;
        var bits = themes + " theme" + (themes === 1 ? "" : "s");
        if (orphans.length) bits += " - " + orphans.length + " not yet linked";
        if (gap) {
          var ga = nodeIndex[exemplar(gap[0])] || {}, gb = nodeIndex[exemplar(gap[1])] || {};
          bits += " - the areas around \u201c" + (ga.label || "?") + "\u201d and \u201c" + (gb.label || "?") + "\u201d share no links";
        }
        verdict(bits + ".");
        com.list.slice(0, 8).forEach(function (c) {
          if (c.ids.length < 2 && com.list.length > 3) return;
          var ex = exemplar(c);
          var d = nodeIndex[ex] || {};
          var btn = el("button", { type: "button", class: "okf-lens-summary__row" });
          var bar = el("span", { class: "okf-lens-summary__bar" });
          bar.style.width = Math.round(100 * c.ids.length / Math.max(1, com.list[0].ids.length)) + "%";
          bar.style.background = communityColor(c.index);
          btn.appendChild(bar);
          btn.appendChild(el("span", { class: "okf-lens-summary__label" },
            ["Theme " + (c.index + 1) + " - around \u201c" + (d.label || ex) + "\u201d"]));
          btn.appendChild(el("span", { class: "okf-lens-summary__note" }, [c.ids.length + " concepts"]));

    function buildSignalPanel() {
